The pressure at that time is then determined by the centered phase primitive of $|\kappa|^{-2}\kappa\cdot(f-2MV)$. Thus pressure has no independent initial datum: for $t_0=0$ it need not vanish at launch if $f(0)$ has a nonzero normal component.

e02.transverse.smooth-unique.TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator: In the projected equation the coefficients are independent of $s$ and vary smoothly in $a$. Thus the variation-of-constants integral can be differentiated in either parameter, with no coupling to the velocity at another label or phase. The phase primitive preserves that regularity. Uniqueness also transfers the symmetries of the data, when the coefficients have the corresponding symmetries.
e02.transverse.smooth-unique.TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.TransverseSoluti: For two solutions with the same force, the velocity difference solves the homogeneous projected equation from zero. It vanishes identically. Equation (5.16) then gives a phase-independent pressure difference, which is zero by the normalization at each time and label.

e02.transverse.constraints.TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator: The projected equation gives $\partial_t(\kappa\cdot V)=0$, using $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$. Taking its phase average gives a homogeneous linear equation for $\langle V\rangle_s$ because the coefficients are phase independent and $\langle f\rangle_s=0$. Both constraints hold initially and so persist.

e02.transverse.support.TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator: For a fixed label outside $\operatorname{supp}g$, the force at that label is identically zero, so its forward solution and normalized pressure vanish. On the lifted labels the support is repeated over the lattice; in the original cell it lies strictly in the interior. This locality comes from solving an ODE at fixed $(a,s)$, in contrast to the mean pressure equation, which couples the labels.

e02.transverse.activation-endpoint.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans: The zero-start condition is at time zero. If $t_0>0$, vanishing of the force on the inactive prefix and continuity of the solution give $V(t_0)=0$; if $t_0=0$, this is the prescribed initial condition. The statement needed for (5.21) is zero velocity at launch, not an independently imposed pressure value.
e02.transverse.activation-endpoint.TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.eq_zer: For positive $t_0$ the inactive condition gives zero at every earlier time, and continuity extends it to $t_0$. For $t_0=0$ there is no such earlier interval, so the conclusion instead uses the initial condition. This justifies dropping the launch contribution in (5.20).
e02.transverse.activation-endpoint.TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator: The joint smooth existence theorem preserves the vanishing prefix. In particular its velocity at the activation time is zero, by continuity for positive $t_0$ and by the given launch value when $t_0=0$. This is the property needed to pass from (5.20) to the forced bound (5.21).

e02.transverse.forward-frame.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.coframeLif: Let $E$ have orthonormal columns spanning $k_*^\perp$ and put $F=D_aX$. The identity $(F^{-T}k_*)\cdot FEw=k_*\cdot Ew=0$ shows that the image of $A_\perp=FE$ is precisely the moving plane. Its two coordinates remain in the same fixed space at every label, even when the physical wave vector changes direction.

e02.transverse.inverse-frame.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.coframePul: For a transverse vector $y$, $F^{-1}y$ lies in $k_*^\perp$ and its coordinates are $E^TF^{-1}y$. For an arbitrary $y$ one must first take $(I-P_\kappa)y$. This gives $A_\perp^\dagger=E^TF^{-1}(I-P_\kappa)$ and in particular removes the pressure direction before taking coordinates.

e02.transverse.frame-identities.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.coframe_id: The two identities express that $A_\perp^\dagger$ is a left inverse on the two coordinates and a projected inverse on the three physical coordinates. In particular $A_\perp^\dagger\kappa=0$. This lets one derive (5.18) directly from (5.15) without first substituting the formula for the phase pressure.

e02.transverse.frame-time.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.coframeLif: The coefficient in the two-dimensional equation includes the derivative of the moving frame. Substituting $V=A_\perp v$ gives $V_t=A_\perp v_t+MA_\perp v$. Adding the strain $MV$ gives a second copy of $MA_\perp v$; multiplying by $A_\perp^\dagger$ kills the pressure direction and yields (5.18).

e02.transverse.coordinate-equation.TorusEuler.fixedTransverseGenerator: The fixed-plane generator in Lean is $-\mathcal M_\perp$, with $\mathcal M_\perp=2A_\perp^\dagger MA_\perp$. In these coordinates it makes sense to subtract the matrix at label zero from the matrix at $a$ without first identifying two different transverse planes. The difference acts as an additional forcing term in the central equation, the starting point of the estimate (5.23).

e02.lemma53.near-origin.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.paper_hier: The coefficient of the principal Hessian of the leading pressure is $-c_{\mathbf a}F_h'$, where $c_{\mathbf a}=2\widetilde\chi g(\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a)/|\kappa|^2$. The sign in (5.19) ensures $c_{\mathbf a}\ge0$. Thus the largest positive curvature from that tensor occurs where $F_h'$ is negative, and is bounded by $Chc_{\mathbf a}|\kappa|^2$. Positivity of the coupling is needed on the whole envelope, not just at its center.
e02.lemma53.near-origin.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3: The seed hypothesis is relative: (5.5) controls the propagation of every transverse vector at the origin, not just the selected seed. Together with the positive central coupling margin, it gives (5.19) on a sufficiently small envelope. The numbered Lean statement permits an upper-normalized nonzero central seed rather than requiring the maximum to attain the normalization; it also admits the broader parent pressure class.
e02.lemma53.near-origin.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_3: The pressure condition is an upper bound as a quadratic form, not a small norm of the Hessian. By (5.19), $0\le c_{\mathbf a}|\kappa|^2\le2|\kappa||M||\mathbf a|\lesssim\mathsf D^3\lambda^{1/4}$. Since $F_h'\ge-Ch$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, its principal Hessian is bounded above by $C\mathsf D^3\lambda^{-1/4}I$. The linked numbered theorem establishes the seed bound and sign used here, with an upper-normalized nonzero central seed.
e02.lemma53.near-origin.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.seedNear_of_h51: To retain the sign, compare the error in the triple product with $\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa(t,0)||\mathbf a(t,0)|$, its lower bound at the origin. The variation estimates give an error of size $C\mathsf D^C|a||\kappa(t,0)||\mathbf a(t,0)|$. On $|a|\le2\ell_*$ the ratio can be made less than $1/2$ by a single radius choice. An error bound independent of the central amplitude would not prove positivity at early times.

e02.lemma53.forward-hypotheses.TorusEuler.exists_paper_hierarchy_invers: Part (i) is an estimate for a given solution of the projected velocity equation with possibly nonzero launch data. Its support assumptions keep every label of interest within reach of the central propagator comparison. The active-profile theorem treats data on $[t_0,T]$ with compatible lattice-phase translations, without assuming a centered force.
e02.lemma53.forward-hypotheses.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3: The estimate in part (i) does not require zero initial velocity or a centered forcing, because it concerns the projected ODE alone. The numbered Lean statement assumes full-slab smoothness and then estimates its active restriction; the related active-profile theorem covers data smooth only on the active interval.

e02.lemma53.forward-bound.TorusEuler.exists_paper_hierarchy_invers: The central propagator costs $\mathsf D^3\gamma(t)/\gamma(t')$ in the fixed-plane coordinates, and the comparison at nearby labels adds at most $e$. Dividing the variation-of-constants formula by $\gamma(t)$ leaves a time integral of $|\psi(t')|/\gamma(t')$, which is bounded by its supremum since $T\le1$. Multiplication by the frame and its inverse costs parent powers. The active-interval formal estimate uses exponent $20$.
e02.lemma53.forward-bound.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist: The term $\gamma(t_0)^{-1}\|V(t_0)\|_{[n]}$ permits two different applications of (5.20). For the leading homogeneous solution the initial data have size proportional to $\gamma(t_0)$; for the forced correction the initial data are zero. The full-slab formal helper measures both on the active interval, and therefore yields the same type of estimate in each case.
e02.lemma53.forward-bound.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3: Integrating a bound using only $|M|\le\mathsf D$ could give an exponential in $\mathsf D$, too costly for the power-separated frequencies. Instead (5.5) supplies a polynomial bound for the central propagator after dividing out the intended amplification. A small envelope transfers it to nearby labels. The numbered formal statement takes full-slab smooth data; the active-profile helper allows smoothness just on $[t_0,T]$.

e02.lemma53.zero-start-hypotheses.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist: The support condition puts the labels of the forced solution in the region where the central propagator estimate extends. The inactive-prefix condition gives $V(t_0)=0$, removing the launch term of (5.20). Centering of the force has a separate role: it yields a centered velocity and a periodic pressure primitive. The mean correction is not required to share this support or time prefix.
e02.lemma53.zero-start-hypotheses.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3: This part of the lemma concerns a force defined on the entire slab and switched on only on the active interval. In addition to the support and prefix assumptions it is centered at every time and label, making the pressure normalization possible. The formal statement uses a fixed admissible envelope, a broader admissible pressure class and the central amplitude upper bound.

r3c8-lemma53-transverse-existence.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist: The existence theorem produces the normalized pair with $V(0)=0$ and keeps the prescribed support and inactive prefix. It also has the phase-shift compatibility needed when the parent phase is not a lattice vector. The subsequent estimate in (5.21) controls this pair quantitatively; existence itself is not the estimate.
r3c8-lemma53-transverse-existence.TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.TransverseSoluti: After solving the velocity ODE there is no remaining freedom in the phase pressure. If two normalized pairs solve the same equation from zero, uniqueness for the velocity and (5.16) give equality of the pressure derivatives; the average removes the integration constant. The linked result proves uniqueness, not existence.

e02.lemma53.transverse-pressure-bound.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist: Equation (5.16) gives $|\partial_s\mathsf p|\le |\kappa|^{-1}(|f|+2|M||V|)$. The inverse wave-vector length provides the factor $\lambda^{-1}$, while taking the normalized phase primitive is bounded at the same scaled derivative order. In particular the pressure does not have to be obtained by inverting a spatial Laplacian on the torus at this step. The full-slab helper gives (5.21) with exponent $20$.
e02.lemma53.transverse-pressure-bound.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3: The pressure estimate is later used together with the equation, not by differentiating it twice in physical space. At level two, $\mathsf p_2$ has size $\lambda^{-1-23/12}$ up to parent powers; two physical derivatives could leave $\lambda^{1/12}$. But $\kappa\partial_s\mathsf p_2=P_\kappa(f_2+f_2^S-2MV_2)$ has size $\lambda^{-23/12}$. Only one physical derivative is then needed, leaving $\lambda^{-5/12}$ in the Hessian bound. The numbered Lean estimate allows the broader parent pressure and central-amplitude hypotheses.

e02.lemma53.leading-bound.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_pap: The factor $h$ in (5.22) is a bound on the phase profile, not on its slope at the origin. Indeed $F_h(0)=0$, $F_h'(0)=1$ and $g(0)=1$ give the central gradient $\mathbf a(t,0)\otimes\kappa(t,0)$ before switching. Thus the velocity can have size $\gamma\lambda^{-5/4}$ while its central gradient has scale $\gamma\lambda^{1/4}$ up to parent powers. The formal estimate uses a fixed admissible envelope.
e02.lemma53.leading-bound.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3: Part (iii) starts from a nonzero homogeneous seed, not from the zero-start inverse of part (ii). The bound at launch is proportional to $\gamma(t_0)$, which cancels the launch denominator in (5.20); multiplication by $F_h$ contributes $h$. The numbered formal statement fixes one admissible envelope instead of ranging over all cutoffs in the paper's class.

e02.lemma53.frame-bounds.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_cofra: Let $E$ be the constant matrix with the two initial orthonormal columns. Then $A_\perp=FE$ and $|A_\perp w|\le\mathsf D|Ew|=\mathsf D|w|$. The transported frame need not be orthogonal. The corresponding lower bound from $F^{-1}$ controls its inverse on the transverse plane.

For transverse $y$, $A_\perp^\dagger y$ consists of the coordinates of $F^{-1}y$ in the initial orthonormal basis. On general $y$ there is first an orthogonal projection, of norm at most one. This gives $|A_\perp^\dagger|\le\mathsf D$ and explains why the inverse Gram matrix has norm at most $\mathsf D^2$.

e02.lemma53.coframe-coefficient-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.transverseCofra: The Gram matrix $K_\perp=A_\perp^TA_\perp$ has eigenvalues between $\mathsf D^{-2}$ and $\mathsf D^2$. Differentiating $K_\perp^{-1}K_\perp=I$ bounds the jets of the inverse, and hence those of $A_\perp^\dagger$ and $\mathcal M_\perp$. These are bounds before multiplication by the radius weights; (D.7) then absorbs the cost of each positive label derivative.

e02.lemma53.gronwall.TorusEuler.weighted_near_label_forward: In the fixed-plane equation, write the generator at $a$ as the one at $0$ plus a perturbation. Its norm is at most $\mathsf D^{-3}$, while the weighted central propagator has norm at most $\mathsf D^3$. Their product is at most one. Variation of constants therefore gives an integral inequality for $|v(t)|/\gamma(t)$ with coefficient one, so the cost of leaving the origin is at most $e^{T-t'}\le e$.

e02.lemma53.forced-integral.TorusEuler.weighted_near_label_forced_no: Let $\Phi_a(t,t')$ denote the two-dimensional homogeneous propagator. The preceding estimate bounds $\Phi_a(t,t')$ by $e\mathsf D^3\gamma(t)/\gamma(t')$. Substituting this in the variation-of-constants formula gives (5.23); the denominator in the integrand is $\gamma(t')$, not $\gamma(t)$. Thus even a very small early forcing is measured in relation to the early seed, and amplification from that time is already included.

e02.lemma53.near-seed-comparison.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.seedNear_of_h51: In the fixed coordinates, the difference $v_a-v_0$ has initial value $(A_\perp^\dagger(t_0,a)-A_\perp^\dagger(t_0,0))\mathbf a(t_0,0)$, and force $-(\mathcal M_\perp(t,a)-\mathcal M_\perp(t,0))v_a$. Both coefficient differences are bounded by a parent power times $|a|$. After applying (5.23), return to the physical vectors by writing $\mathbf a(t,a)-\mathbf a(t,0)=A_\perp(t,a)(v_a-v_0)+(A_\perp(t,a)-A_\perp(t,0))v_0$. This retains the factor $|\mathbf a(t,0)|$. The Lean conclusion records the comparison with a coefficient depending on the parent bound.
e02.lemma53.near-seed-comparison.TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.SeedNear: The comparison is required relative to the central seed at every active time. This is what permits the initial projection and coefficient variation to be small even when the central seed is far below its terminal size. A uniform absolute error would not suffice to retain the positive coupling margin in (5.5). The definition does not supply the bound on its comparison coefficient.

e02.lemma53.word-lifting.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.odeWordBound_of: Applying $\ell_*\partial_{a_i}$ to (5.18) gives the same left-hand operator acting on $\ell_*\partial_{a_i}v$, with datum $\ell_*\partial_{a_i}\psi-(\ell_*\partial_{a_i}\mathcal M_\perp)v$. By (D.7) the latter coefficient pays for the factor $\mathsf D^3$ of the zero-order inverse. A phase derivative has no such commutator. Higher mixed derivatives use this same argument with lower-order solutions.

e02.lemma53.weight-after-derivatives.TorusEuler.paperHierarchyActiveVelocityN: The norm divides by $\gamma(t)$ after taking the scaled label and phase derivatives. Since $\gamma$ depends only on time, these derivatives commute with division by it. No estimate of $\gamma_t/\gamma$ is needed in the lifting argument, which differentiates the spatial parameters of the original equation rather than a time-rescaled unknown.

e02.lemma53.pressure-coefficient-route.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.rescaled_pressu: Rewrite $\lambda\partial_s\mathsf p$ as $(\lambda^2/|\kappa|^2)(\kappa/\lambda)\cdot(f-2MV)$. The two normalized coefficients have scaled bounds with no frequency power by (5.8). Their product, followed by the zero-mean primitive of Lemma D.1, bounds the pressure without using a higher-order velocity estimate.

e02.lemma53.pressure-estimate.TorusEuler.oscillatoryPhasePressure_weig: For a centered periodic integrand $r$, the primitive $\int_0^s r$ is periodic, and subtracting its mean gives the normalized primitive with supremum at most $2\|r\|_\infty$. Differentiation in labels commutes with this operation; differentiation in phase does too on centered periodic profiles. Thus the same bound applies to every scaled derivative word, with no extra $h^{-1}$ beyond the derivatives already included in $\|r\|_{[n],\gamma}$.

e02.lemma53.leading-proof-route.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.lemma_5_3_of_le: At $t_0$ the initial value for the homogeneous estimate is $g(I-P_\kappa)\mathbf a(t_0,0)$. Its scaled norm contains $|\mathbf a(t_0,0)|=\gamma(t_0)\lambda^{-3/4}$, so the small denominator in (5.20) cancels. The factor $F_h$ contributes a further $h$ only after estimating $g\mathbf a$; this is the origin of $\lambda^{-5/4}$ in (5.22).

e02.lemma53.leading-homogeneous.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.pap: At fixed $(a,s)$, $g(a)F_h(s)$ is constant in time. Multiplication of the seed equation by this factor produces the pressure term $-2g(\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a)|\kappa|^{-2}F_h\kappa$, because $P_h'=F_h$. This gives the homogeneous equation for the pair $(A_1,\mathsf p[A_1])$. Switching the wave on adds the separate time-cutoff error rather than a force in this homogeneous estimate.

e02.hierarchy.velocity-blocks.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Cd: The correction entering $Y_p$ is $C_p=C[V_{p-1}]$, already available from the previous level. The stored index of that field is $p-1$. In particular the paper's $C_{P+1}$ is stored at $P$ and survives the end of the recursion.
e02.hierarchy.velocity-blocks.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Yd: In the size grouping $Y_p=V_p+C[V_{p-1}]$, so both fields can be counted as level $p$ in the quadratic terms. In the divergence calculation the two fields must instead be $V_p+C[V_p]$. The individual $Y_p$ need not be divergence free, even though the full retained sum is.
e02.hierarchy.velocity-blocks.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Zd: In $(Z_i\cdot\widetilde{\mathbf d})Z_j$, the slow derivative acts on all of $Z_j=Y_j+B_j$. The fast derivative kills $B_j$, and $V_i\cdot\kappa=0$, so only $((C_i+B_i)\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY_j$ remains. This is why the fast sum can be split into a known completion term and a term containing the new mean.
e02.hierarchy.velocity-blocks.TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity_eq: Grouping $W$ by size gives $\sum_{p=1}^P Z_p+C_{P+1}$; grouping by generating oscillation gives $\sum_{p=1}^P(V_p+C_{p+1}+B_p)$. The equality follows by shifting the correction index and using $C_1=0$. The first grouping organizes the products by level, while the second establishes divergence via the curl identity.

e02.hierarchy.level-placement.TorusEuler.hierarchy_completion_previous: For $p\ge2$ write $S_p=\lambda^{-5/4-2(p-1)/3}$. The correction estimate gives $C_p$ the scale $\lambda^{-1}S_{p-1}=\lambda^{-1/3}S_p$. In particular it is better than the level-$p$ bound by $\lambda^{-1/3}$. The extra gain matters when $C_p$ advects the phase of another oscillation.
e02.hierarchy.level-placement.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Yd: The definition of $Y_p$ places the known completion $C_p$ with the new oscillation $V_p$ because their bounds fit the same level budget. It does not assert that they are of equal size or form a curl pair. The completion estimate gives the stronger gain used in the phase-advection estimates.

e02.hierarchy.first-mean-source.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.levelSource: The material derivative of $C_2=C[V_1]=\widetilde\chi C[A_1]$ has a term $\widetilde\chi'C[A_1]$. Together with $\widetilde\chi'A_1$ from the leading transverse equation it gives $R_{\widetilde\chi}$, set aside from the hierarchy. Consequently the linear term of $H_2$ contains $\widetilde\chi(\partial_t+M)C[A_1]$ rather than $(\partial_t+M)C_2$. This permits use of the homogeneous equation for $A_1$ in the relay estimate (5.32).
e02.hierarchy.first-mean-source.TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.levelSource_eq_s: At level two only $(i,j)=(1,1)$ occurs in the slow sum and only $(2,1)$ in the completion phase sum. With $Y_1=Z_1=V_1$, the products are precisely $(V_1\cdot\mathbf d)V_1$ and $(C_2\cdot\kappa)\partial_sV_1$. The bridge also identifies the linear relay after removing the cutoff derivative of the completion.
e02.hierarchy.first-mean-source.TorusEuler.HierarchyOperators.sourceBefo: The abstract pre-mean source at $p=2$ contains the material derivative of the stored completion of $V_1$, the slow gradient of its pressure and the two quadratic interactions. It subtracts the completion of the activation error at that level. With the cutoff identities this gives precisely the switched linear term in (5.25).

e02.hierarchy.first-linear-mean-zero.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera: Averaging commutes with the material operator $\partial_t+M$ and the slow gradient $\mathbf d$, since their coefficients are independent of the phase. Thus the linear relay has zero mean at every level. At level two the completion of the cutoff derivative, which is removed from the relay, has zero mean as well. No estimate on the size of a time derivative is needed for this cancellation.

e02.hierarchy.mean-fast-integration.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera: In the fast product, transfer $\partial_s$ to $C_2\cdot\kappa$ and use $-\partial_s(C_2\cdot\kappa)=\mathbf d\cdot V_1$. The sum with the slow product is then $\sum_i\mathbf d_i\langle (V_1)_i V_1\rangle_s$. Before averaging, the fast product costs $\lambda^{-9/4}\lambda^{3/2}\lambda^{-5/4}=\lambda^{-2}$; afterward the two factors of $V_1$ cost $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and the remaining label derivative costs only a parent power. The mean gains a further $\lambda^{-1/2}$.

e02.hierarchy.first-residual-inclusion.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.meanSource: The averaged wave force is at most a parent power times $\lambda^{-5/2}$, the square of the leading velocity scale. At each active time it even carries the square of the seed weight (up to parent powers), whereas the inherited residual is only bounded in the whole-slab unweighted norm. Equation (5.10) gives it the same frequency scale at every label order. This is why the first mean inverse can remove both errors at once without losing the improved power of $\lambda$.
e02.hierarchy.first-residual-inclusion.TorusEuler.exists_parentResidualWeighted: The parent residual has Fourier support in frequencies at most $4\mathsf D$, so Bernstein controls its order-$m$ derivative by $C_m\mathsf D^m\|R_U\|_\infty$. The chain rule for composition with $X$ introduces at most a fixed power of $\mathsf D$ per derivative; the formal radius condition $\ell_*\mathsf D^6\le1$ absorbs that cost. Consequently no additional parent power is needed in the bound for the residual in label norms.

e02.hierarchy.quadratic-levels.TorusEuler.hierarchyAdvectionLevel: Counting one level for a fast derivative is bookkeeping for the whole interaction, not a bound on the derivative operator alone. The first completion $C_2$ is of size $\lambda^{-9/4}$, so its fast transport multiplies another oscillation by $\lambda^{-9/4}\lambda^{3/2}=\lambda^{-3/4}$. The first mean instead gives $\lambda^{-5/2}\lambda^{3/2}=\lambda^{-1}$. Thus a level gain of $\lambda^{-2/3}$ leaves a reserve of at least $\lambda^{-1/12}$.

e02.hierarchy.general-pre-source.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.levelSource: At level three the slow products are $(Z_1\cdot\mathbf d)Z_2+(Z_2\cdot\mathbf d)Z_1$. The fast products are $(C_2\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY_2+(C_3\cdot\kappa)\partial_sV_1$. Both use only earlier oscillations and means, since $C_3=C[V_2]$. The linear terms carry the completion of $V_2$ and the slow gradient of its pressure to the next level. This is the general indexing in (5.26).
e02.hierarchy.general-pre-source.TorusEuler.HierarchyOperators.sourceBefo: Neither $V_p$ nor $B_p$ occurs in $H_p$. In the slow sum $i+j=p$, both indices are below $p$. In the fast sum $i+j=p+1$, $i\ge2$, the largest possible first index is $p$, but that factor is $C_p=C[V_{p-1}]$, already known. The derivative in the second factor has $j\le p-1$. These index restrictions are the reason the next mean force is prescribed.

e02.hierarchy.sources.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.oscSource: The slow quadratic source splits into mean–mean, mean–oscillation, oscillation–mean and oscillation–oscillation products. Centering removes the first group exactly. The other three groups all contain an oscillatory factor, and so vanish off the envelope and before activation; in the weighted estimate for $f_p$ one places $1/\gamma$ on such a factor. The supplementary source likewise vanishes there, since it differentiates earlier oscillations in phase.
e02.hierarchy.sources.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.meanSource: Adding the prescribed mean and transverse sources gives $\bar f_p+f_p=-H_p$ for $p\ge3$ and $-H_2-R_U\circ X$ for $p=2$. These are exactly the negatives of the known errors before the new mean starts transporting the earlier phases. The supplementary source then cancels the additional phase products. This split is the cancellation of the momentum residual through level $p$ in (5.29).
e02.hierarchy.sources.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The lattice compatibility is $H_p(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=H_p(t,a,s)$. Hence $\langle H_p(t,a+n,\cdot)\rangle_s$ equals $\int_0^1 H_p(t,a,s-k_*\cdot n)\,ds$, which is the original phase integral by periodicity. In particular the mean force descends to the label torus even when the carrier is not integral. The inherited residual is also periodic in the labels.

e02.hierarchy.pre-source-known.TorusEuler.HierarchyOperators.sourceBefo: The potentially troublesome index is $i=p$ in the fast sum: its term is $(C_p\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY_1$, already determined by $V_{p-1}$ and $V_1$. The theorem states the precise independence property: changing the stored families at levels $p$ and above leaves $H_p$ unchanged.

e02.hierarchy.mean-before-transverse.TorusEuler.FiniteHierarchySolvers.constr: The force $\bar f_p$ is now known on the whole slab $[0,T]$. Apply the endpoint inverse of Section 4 to select $B_p(0)$ by $\int_0^T(D_aX)^{-1}B_p\,dt=0$. This may require an initial mean even when all new oscillations start later. The recursion selects a supplied inverse output; the analytic existence and bound are Theorem 4.2 and Proposition 5.2.

e02.hierarchy.supplementary-source.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.suppSource: The only new mean in (5.28) occurs in $-(B_p\cdot\kappa)\partial_sV_1$; all differentiated oscillations are already known. It is important here that the mean has the improved bound. If $S_p=\lambda^{-5/4-2(p-1)/3}$, the ordinary level bound $B_p=O(S_p)$ would give a fast product of size $\lambda^{1/4}S_p$ up to parent powers. The stronger induction bound $O(\lambda^{-1/2}S_p)$ instead gives $\lambda^{-1/4}S_p$. The phase mean of the product is zero.
e02.hierarchy.supplementary-source.TorusEuler.HierarchyOperators.meanPhaseA: The indices of the fast mean interactions satisfy $i+j=p+1$, $i\ge2$, $j\ge1$. The allowed pairs can therefore be enumerated by $2\le i\le p$, with $j=p+1-i$. The endpoint $i=p$ pairs the current mean with $Y_1=V_1$; the linked equality is for the positive advection, so (5.28) has a minus sign.

e02.hierarchy.transverse-after-mean.TorusEuler.FiniteHierarchySolvers.constr: The new mean enters the transverse equation only in the now known supplementary force. Both $f_p$ and $f_p^S$ are centered, and the preceding oscillations make their sum vanish outside the envelope and on the inactive prefix. Thus the zero-start transverse inverse can be applied once to the entire force, with the pressure determined afterward by (5.16). There is no coupled same-level iteration.

r2.hierarchy.complete-current-field.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsExpansion: Complete the oscillation using $Q_p=-\partial_s^{-1}(\kappa\times V_p/|\kappa|^2)$ and $C_{p+1}=\mathbf d\times Q_p$. Transversality gives $\kappa\times\partial_sQ_p=V_p$, so the completed pair is the full curl. This last operation both enforces exact divergence freedom and produces the known correction used in $H_{p+1}$; it requires no third inverse.
r2.hierarchy.complete-current-field.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Cd: `Cd u (p+1)` is the correction stored with $V_p$. It belongs to $Y_{p+1}$ by size, and to the curl pair of $V_p$ by construction. For $p=P$ these two conventions explain why $C_{P+1}$ survives although the next level is not solved.

e02.hierarchy.order-required.TorusEuler.HierarchyOperators.meanPhaseA: For fixed $p$, every $Y_{p+1-i}$ in (5.28) has index at most $p-1$. Thus at level three the supplementary source is $-(B_2\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY_2-(B_3\cdot\kappa)\partial_sV_1$. The second term needs the mean just obtained, but neither term needs $V_3$. The congruence lemma expresses precisely this dependence on previously computed oscillations.

The term with $i=p,j=1$ has assigned level $p+1-1=p$, even though $B_p$ has just been found. The first index can start at two because $B_1=0$. Expanding the fast advection by the means on the diagonal $i+j=p+1$ gives the sum in (5.28), with a minus sign when it is moved to the source side of the equation.

e02.hierarchy.supplementary-mean-zero.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera: At fixed $(t,a)$, $(B_i\cdot\kappa)$ can be taken out of the phase integral. The remaining integral is $Y_j(t,a,1)-Y_j(t,a,0)=0$, by periodicity. In particular one can determine the entire mean source without knowing $B_p$, although $B_p$ is needed in the oscillatory source at the same level.

e02.hierarchy.reflection.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const: Reflection fixes time and reverses both spatial variables $a$ and $s$. Since $M$, $\kappa$ and $D_aX$ are even, differentiating an odd profile in either spatial variable gives an even profile; the quadratic momentum source is consequently odd. The centered phase primitive of an odd velocity is even, so its label curl is odd. The mean and transverse solves preserve the velocity parity by uniqueness with their endpoint and zero-start data, respectively. The formal parity induction assumes these properties of the chosen inverses.

e02.prop54.well-defined.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: At level $p$ the last correction already known is $C_p=C[V_{p-1}]$. It is the only level-$p$ field in $H_p$. The mean inverse applied to (5.27) therefore determines $B_p$ before (5.28) is formed; the transverse inverse and curl then determine $V_p,\mathsf p_p,C_{p+1}$. This also shows that increasing the final depth does not change the lower levels. The formal proposition asserts existence of the seed and uniqueness for fixed seed and normalized pressures.
e02.prop54.well-defined.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_4: The mean is selected by zero displacement at the two ends of the parent trajectory, whereas the transverse equation is solved forward from zero velocity. Both inverses use the same fixed coefficients of the parent; no flow of $U+W^\natural$ has to be computed to solve them. The numbered Lean proposition includes existence and uniqueness for fixed seed, cutoff and normalized pressures.
e02.prop54.well-defined.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The recursive definition takes the leading profiles and the solution operators as input. At step $p$ it uses the previous transverse field to obtain $C_p$, solves for the new mean and then determines the new transverse field. The definition itself does not establish that the supplied operators solve the linear PDE and ODE; their properties are what make the recursion a construction of Euler profiles.

In the general identity theorem the solution operators and their defining properties are part of `PhysicalApproximationData`. It proves that the finite expansion has the asserted momentum, divergence and support identities. Showing that the parent admits such operators is the separate solvability step of Proposition 5.4.

e02.prop54.velocity-pressure-sums.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: There are two ways to group the velocity. Pairing $V_p$ with $C_{p+1}$ gives a completed curl, whose divergence is zero. Pairing $V_p$ with $C_p$ groups fields at comparable frequency powers for the quadratic estimates. Shifting the index of the curl sum gives the displayed equality, since $C_1=0$ and the final $C_{P+1}$ is included.
e02.prop54.velocity-pressure-sums.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_4: Stopping at depth $P$ means stopping the linear solves, not discarding all fields assigned level $P+1$. The last solve yields $V_P$ and $\mathsf p_P$, and the explicit curl of its potential yields $C_{P+1}$. No mean or transverse pressure is solved at $P+1$.
e02.prop54.velocity-pressure-sums.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.expansion: In the Lean notation `Cd u (p+1)` is the correction generated by `u.V p`. The definition `expansion` sums these pairs and the means directly. Its equality with the sum of $Z_p$ uses the extra $C_{P+1}$ at the upper endpoint.
e02.prop54.velocity-pressure-sums.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.expansionPressure: The phase derivative of $\bar q_p$ vanishes. The phase derivative of $\mathsf p_p$ enforces $\kappa\cdot V_p=0$ in (5.15), while its label gradient is left for the next level. In particular the label gradient of $\mathsf p_P$ remains in (5.30), even though $\mathsf p_P$ is included in the pressure sum.
e02.prop54.velocity-pressure-sums.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsExpansion: `IsExpansion` specifies the equations of the finite family. It sets $C_1=B_1=\bar q_1=0$, requires $C_{p+1}=C[V_p]$ through $p=P$, and imposes the new mean and transverse solves for $2\le p\le P$. In particular it keeps the correction from the last solve even though there is no new solve at its assigned level.
e02.prop54.velocity-pressure-sums.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The correction stored as `u.C p` belongs to $V_p$, whereas the paper calls it $C_{p+1}$. The identity theorem uses this shifted index to prove the two expressions for $W$ coincide, including the correction from $V_P$.

e02.prop54.divergence.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: With $V_0=V_{P+1}=0$, (3.6) gives $\widetilde{\mathbf d}\cdot Z_i=\mathbf d\cdot V_i-\mathbf d\cdot V_{i-1}$ for $1\le i\le P+1$. Here the slow divergence of the curl $C_i$ and of the mean $B_i$ are both zero. Summing telescopes, with $Z_{P+1}=C_{P+1}$ providing the last cancellation. The proof uses the equivalent sum of completed curls.
e02.prop54.divergence.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The divergence conclusion of the identity is for the whole sum including $C_{P+1}$. For an individual $V_p$, transversality eliminates $\kappa\cdot\partial_sV_p$, but not $\mathbf d\cdot V_p$. The attached correction cancels the latter exactly.

e02.prop54.residual.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: The residual of the parent is a function of $(t,a)$ alone after composition with $X$. It belongs entirely to the mean source at level two, with sign $-R_U\circ X$ in (5.27). Its cancellation in (5.29) is therefore pointwise in the independent phase as well as on the physical graph. The next residual consists only of the tail and the activation term.
e02.prop54.residual.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: Equation (5.29) is an exact identity for the finite sum, not an approximate equality of momenta. Increasing $P$ moves the first omitted level in $R_P$ farther out. It does not change the switch term $\widetilde\chi'(A_1+C[A_1])$, which must instead be made small on the time interval where $\widetilde\chi$ changes.

e02.prop54.phase-means.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: At each $(t,a)$, averaging the transverse equation gives a homogeneous ODE for $\langle V_p\rangle_s$ with zero initial value. The centered potential and its slow curl also have zero mean. Hence $\langle W\rangle_s=\sum_{p=2}^PB_p$. This is an average in the independent phase before setting $s=k_*\cdot a$; it is not the spatial average of $W^\natural$ on the torus.

e02.prop54.oscillatory-support.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: At a label outside the closed support of $g$, all earlier $Y_i$ and their spatial derivatives vanish. Thus $H_p$ is independent of $s$, even if the earlier means are nonzero there: centering kills $H_p$ and every summand of $f_p^S$ contains a vanishing phase derivative. The transverse ODE is homogeneous there with zero initial value. Its centered pressure primitive and the curl of its potential have the same support.
e02.prop54.oscillatory-support.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The localization is preserved by the oscillatory inverse because it acts at fixed $(a,s)$. Even when $B_i$ has global support, its product with a phase derivative is zero wherever the earlier oscillation is zero. Its product with another mean is removed by centering. No spatial support property of the endpoint inverse is required.

e02.prop54.vanishing-prefix.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: For $p\ge2$ the transverse correction vanishes at $t_0$: by the vanishing prefix if $t_0>0$, and by its initial condition if $t_0=0$. In (5.20) the term $\gamma(t_0)^{-1}\|V_p(t_0)\|_{[n]}$ is therefore zero. At the level of the iteration this same exact vanishing eliminates all sufficiently late oscillations on any fixed interval before $T_\infty$, which is how Proposition 8.1 obtains convergence of high derivatives.
e02.prop54.vanishing-prefix.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: Before $t_0$ the only possible terms of $H_p$ are products of means. They are removed by $H_p-\langle H_p\rangle_s$, and the phase derivatives in $f_p^S$ vanish. In particular the parent residual, although it can be nonzero before $t_0$, occurs only in $\bar f_2$. The zero-start transverse ODE propagates vanishing without imposing it on the mean inverse.

e02.prop54.final-index.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: The convention $V_{P+1}=B_{P+1}=0$ makes the top block exactly $C_{P+1}$. It completes $V_P$ to a curl; it is not a new solution at level $P+1$. Its products with the other blocks must still be included in the residual, because the momentum identity is for the actual divergence-free velocity.
e02.prop54.final-index.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsExpansion: The `top` condition of `IsExpansion` sets `u.V (P+1)` and `u.B (P+1)` to zero. Its separate correction condition still includes $C[V_P]$ at the last retained generating index. The top block $Z_{P+1}$ consequently need not be zero.
e02.prop54.final-index.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The identity is written with the correction stored at its generating index. Thus the top block contains `u.C P`, not a newly computed `u.C (P+1)`. Products with this block are included even though there is no transverse or mean solve at level $P+1$.

e02.prop54.tail.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.remainder: A slow label product has assigned level $i+j$, and a fast phase product has level $i+j-1$. Canceling all levels through $P$ leaves $i+j\ge P+1$ and $i+j\ge P+2$, respectively. The remaining linear terms are precisely the correction of $V_P$ and the label gradient of its pressure, which would be relayed to level $P+1$.
e02.prop54.tail.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: For $P=2$, the canceled quadratic terms are the slow pair $(1,1)$ and the fast pair $(2,1)$, the latter including transport by $B_2$. Among the first surviving terms are slow pairs $(1,2),(2,1)$ and fast pairs $(2,2),(3,1)$. The last pair uses $C_3=C[V_2]$, despite there being no solve at level three. The linear relay from $V_2$ also remains.
e02.prop54.tail.TorusEuler.HierarchyOperators.remainder: The formal remainder writes the fast transport by the curl correction and by the mean separately. They combine to the displayed sum since $Z_i\cdot\kappa=(C_i+B_i)\cdot\kappa$ by transversality. Also $\partial_sZ_j=\partial_sY_j$. The slow sum includes the full top block $Z_{P+1}=C_{P+1}$.
e02.prop54.tail.TorusEuler.hierarchyTailPairs: The index square is filtered by $i+j-\mathrm{shift}>P$. Taking shift zero for label advection and one for phase advection gives the two thresholds in (5.30). In the fast case the first index can start at two because $C_1=B_1=0$. The filtration is a finite-sum identity; the estimates for those products come later.

e02.prop54.outside-phase.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: Outside the envelope the linear relay and every product containing a phase-dependent field vanish. The tail there is exactly the sum of $(B_i\cdot\mathbf d)B_j$ with $i+j\ge P+1$. The envelope lies strictly inside the cell, so near its faces the tail is a periodic mean field. This is sufficient to evaluate the phase graph smoothly even for a nonintegral $k_*$.
e02.prop54.outside-phase.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The twisted continuation is $F(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=F(t,a,s)$ for $n\in\mathbb Z^3$. Consequently $F(t,a+n,k_*\cdot(a+n))=F(t,a,k_*\cdot a)$. The phase independence of the tail near the cell faces allows this continuation without a jump in any derivative; its periodic mean products need no phase matching.

e02.prop54.smooth.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: Smoothness is obtained before estimating the expansion: the smooth lower profiles give smooth sources, the endpoint inverse and the transverse ODE give smooth solutions, and the centered primitive and label curl preserve smoothness. At any fixed $P$ only finitely many of these operations are needed.
e02.prop54.smooth.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The smooth profile type also incorporates the compatibility law $F(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=F(t,a,s)$ for $n\in\mathbb Z^3$. Substituting $s=k_*\cdot a$ gives a periodic label field, even when $k_*$ is not integral. Joint smoothness in the identity theorem follows from the smooth profile types; constructing the profiles with those types uses the separate solvability argument.

r2.prop54.divergence-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_4_o: The equality uses two separate constraints: every completed wave is a full curl, and every mean satisfies $\mathbf d\cdot B_p=0$. Thus Proposition 5.4 is divergence-free at every finite depth, independently of the smallness of $R_P$.
r2.prop54.divergence-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.totalDivergence: Indeed, $\kappa\times\partial_sQ[V]=V$, so the full curl of $Q[V]$ is $V+C[V]$. Since $\kappa=\mathbf d(k_*\cdot a)$ and the coefficients are independent of $s$, the components of $\widetilde{\mathbf d}$ commute; its divergence of a curl is zero. This holds for every generating index, including $p=P$.

The endpoint inverse writes $B=D_aX v$, with $v=z_t$ and $\operatorname{div}_a v=0$. Since the parent flow preserves volume, the Piola identity gives $\mathbf d\cdot B=\operatorname{div}_a v=0$. The mean has no phase derivative. This is how the label-space constraint of the inverse yields incompressibility in physical coordinates.

r2.prop54.quadratic-expansion.TorusEuler.HierarchyOperators.momentum_e: Expand the two derivative terms of $\widetilde{\mathbf d}=\mathbf d+\kappa\partial_s$ separately. In the fast term one can replace the advecting $Z_i$ by $C_i+B_i$, since $V_i\cdot\kappa=0$, and the differentiated $Z_j$ by $Y_j$, since $\partial_sB_j=0$. The two replacements are independent: both are needed to obtain the exact fast quadratic sum that is split into $H_p$ and $-f_p^S$.

r2.prop54.level-cancellation.TorusEuler.HierarchyOperators.momentum_e: Adding the new linear momentum equations cancels the full level, not only its phase average: $f_p+f_p^S+\bar f_p=-H_p+f_p^S$ for $p\ge3$. At $p=2$ it equals $-H_2+f_2^S-R_U\circ X$. The actual quadratic and relayed terms have the opposite signs, $H_p-f_p^S$, with the parent residual added at level two. The formal cancellation is an equality before taking any norm.
r2.prop54.level-cancellation.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsExpansion: The two equations in `IsExpansion` have separate right sides because the inverse for $B_p$ uses displacement endpoints while that for $V_p$ uses zero initial velocity. Adding them restores the full $-H_p$ and the supplementary source, along with the parent residual cancellation at level two. This is the termwise momentum cancellation used in (5.29).

r2.prop54.switch-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_4_o: The cutoff $\widetilde\chi$ commutes with $C[\cdot]$ and with the slow pressure gradient, because they use only spatial derivatives. In the two linear momentum terms, differentiating the cutoff in time gives $\widetilde\chi'A_1$ and $\widetilde\chi'C[A_1]$. Their sum is the switch residual; the term $\widetilde\chi[(\partial_t+M)C[A_1]+\mathbf d\mathsf p[A_1]]$ is instead canceled at level two.
r2.prop54.switch-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.leadingSwitch: The leading equation is homogeneous for $A_1$ on the active interval. The first equality is its product rule with the cutoff. Applying the same rule to the slow curl gives the second cutoff derivative, so the activation error must contain both the leading transverse field and its completion.

e02.prop54.surviving-levels.TorusEuler.hierarchy_advection_filtratio: The filtration groups each product by the integer $i+j-\mathrm{shift}$. Subtracting the sums for levels $2$ through $P$ leaves exactly the two tails in (5.30). This applies to arbitrary summands; the expansion equations identify the terms to subtract.
e02.prop54.surviving-levels.TorusEuler.hierarchyTailPairs: The first omitted slow diagonal is $i+j=P+1$. For the fast sum it is $i+j=P+2$, with $i\ge2$ because the first block is transverse. The fast term on that diagonal contains $C_i$ generated by $V_{i-1}$ or the mean $B_i$; it is their improved size, together with the derivative cost, that makes the shifted diagonal estimate possible in Theorem 5.6.

r2.prop54.endpoint-citation.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_4_o: The parent need not solve Euler exactly. The endpoint inverse uses $H^\#=(D^2p_U-\nabla R_U)\circ X$, the coefficient of the displacement equation, and its quadratic form enters with a minus sign in the coercive energy. The upper bound $H^\#\le\mathrm{Id}$ suffices on $T\le1$. This is the reason for carrying both a pressure-Hessian bound and a residual-gradient bound to the next step.
r2.prop54.endpoint-citation.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanSolvable_of: Writing $B_p=D_aXz_t$, the endpoint condition is $\int_0^T(D_aX)^{-1}B_p\,dt=0$ at every label. It selects $B_p(0)$, not $B_p(T)$. Even for $U=0$ with a solenoidal source, $B_p(t)=B_p(0)+\int_0^t\bar f_p(t')\,dt'$ gives $B_p(0)=-T^{-1}\int_0^T(T-t)\bar f_p(t)\,dt$. Thus a source supported late can require a nonzero mean velocity at time zero. Theorem 4.2 obtains the corresponding inverse for the actual parent.

e02.prop54.inactive-region.TorusEuler.hierarchyInactiveRegion: The inactive region is a union, not an intersection: every phase at a label outside the envelope is inactive at all times, and every label is inactive before $t_0$. These are the two sets on which the zero-start ODE will preserve vanishing. The mean has neither support restriction.

r2.prop54.support-induction.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.IsExpansion.ina: The zero-start ODE is local in $(a,s)$. For a label outside the support the source vanishes for the whole slab, and for $t<t_0$ it vanishes on the elapsed interval at every label. Thus $V_p$ vanishes on the inactive region; its centered pressure primitive and curl then vanish there. This closes the support induction without requiring the endpoint mean to be localized.

e02.prop54.inactive-mean-tail.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi: On the inactive region the only tail products are $(B_i\cdot\mathbf d)B_j$ with $i+j>P$. The first possibly nonzero pair is $(2,2)$, of level four. It survives when $P=2$ or $3$, even before the oscillations begin. More generally the surviving mean pairs need a full-slab unweighted estimate; their support is not controlled by $g$ or $t_0$.

r5-B-linear-curl-estimate.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_5: The part of the previous linear momentum not yet used is the momentum of $C_p=C[V_{p-1}]$ and the slow gradient of $\mathsf p_{p-1}$. This is exactly the first line of (5.26). Lemma 5.5 gives an estimate for their sum using only the spatial norms of the preceding velocity and its forcing. For the first relay the unswitched homogeneous wave is used instead.

r2.lemma55.hypotheses.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_5: Centering permits a periodic phase primitive with zero mean, and transversality makes the fast curl of that primitive equal to $V$. In the formal statement centering is on the full slab and transversality is required on the active interval. The constructed profiles satisfy these conditions.

e02.lemma55.completion.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_5: The factor $\lambda^{-1}$ comes from $\kappa/|\kappa|^2$ in $Q[V]$. An arbitrary centered periodic $V$ need not have a primitive smaller by $h$: even the phase mode $\sin(2\pi s)$ is permitted. The primitive estimate (D.5) is uniform in $h$, and the slow curl costs a fixed parent power and one label derivative. This suffices for the inverse-frequency gain.
e02.lemma55.completion.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_5: The estimate uses the normalized covector, its normalized reciprocal squared length, and the inverse deformation in the slow curl. Their scaled derivatives are controlled by (5.8). The weight $\gamma^{-1}$ commutes with the spatial operators, so the same bound holds even during the small-amplitude part of the launch interval.
e02.lemma55.completion.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren: The general relay theorem makes the coefficient budget explicit: if $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, the completion bound has a factor $\mathsf D^{2(15+a)}\lambda^{-1}$. The exponent is fixed before the derivative order varies. The theorem permits any positive continuous time weight and assumes the corresponding coefficient estimates.

e02.lemma55.momentum-hypothesis.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_5: Use the momentum equation to eliminate $V_t$ before estimating $Q_t$. The potentially fast pressure term disappears since $\kappa\times(\kappa\partial_s\mathsf p)=0$. The remaining label pressure gradient is estimated separately from (5.16); its centered primitive also has the factor $|\kappa|^{-1}$. The relay thus needs $f$ at one higher spatial order, with no time derivative of $f$.
e02.lemma55.momentum-hypothesis.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren: The completion estimate needs only a centered transverse profile; the relay estimate additionally uses its momentum equation and normalized pressure on $[t_0,T]$. The actual hierarchy has centered forcing $f_p+f_p^S$ on the whole slab. The general theorem allows that source and a general positive time weight.

e02.lemma55.relay.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_5: For $V_p$, $p\ge2$, the source in (5.32) is $f_p+f_p^S$. The left side is precisely the linear contribution sent to $H_{p+1}$, or to $R_P$ at $p=P$. Its exponent is $-5/4-2(p-1)/3-1$, which is $1/3$ below the required exponent at level $p+1$. Thus the relay can be estimated using the same source and velocity bounds, without losing a time derivative or enlarging the level cost.
e02.lemma55.relay.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren: The left side of the relay bound is the sum entering the next linear forcing, including the slow pressure gradient. The cross product in the potential removes the longitudinal pressure force from its time derivative, and the commutator of time and the slow curl contains only $M$ and first spatial derivatives. Thus the estimate gains $\lambda^{-1}$ with one extra spatial order on $V$ and $f$, for any admissible time-only weight.

e02.lemma55.unswitched.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_5: At level two use $A_1$ in (5.32), which solves the homogeneous equation on $[t_0,T]$. Using $V_1=\widetilde\chi A_1$ would instead introduce the forcing $\widetilde\chi'A_1$. Those switch derivatives belong to $R_{\widetilde\chi}$, leaving the homogeneous relay multiplied by $\widetilde\chi$ in $H_2$.
e02.lemma55.unswitched.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.pap: For $A_1=g\mathbf aF_h$, the homogeneous pressure is $\mathsf p[A_1]=-2g(\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a)|\kappa|^{-2}P_h$. Since $\partial_sP_h=F_h$, its phase gradient cancels the longitudinal part of $A_{1,t}+MA_1$ required by the changing transverse plane. No cutoff derivative occurs in this equation.
e02.lemma55.unswitched.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren: The general unswitched relay theorem works with a localized seed and its smooth twisted-periodic representatives on the full slab. On the active interval they agree with $A_1$ and its pressure, so the relay inequality has only the velocity norm on the right. The regularity needed for those representatives is an explicit hypothesis here and is supplied by the numbered construction.

e02.lemma55.potential-frequency.TorusEuler.wavePotential_frequency_scale: Set $k=\kappa/\lambda$. Then $Q[V]=-\lambda^{-1}(k/|k|^2)\times\partial_s^{-1}V$, because $k$ is independent of $s$. The normalized coefficient $k/|k|^2$ has scaled label norms controlled by (5.8); differentiation of it does not cost an additional power of $\lambda$. The slow curl of this expression retains the same prefactor.

r2.lemma55.curl-definition.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.curlCorrection: In `curlCorrection` the curl is taken at fixed phase. The full curl of the same potential has the additional term $\kappa\times\partial_sQ[V]$. From $\partial_sQ[V]=-\kappa\times V/|\kappa|^2$ and $\kappa\cdot V=0$, that term equals $V$. Hence the defined correction is exactly the slow part required for incompressibility.

r2.lemma55.parent-product-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_5_of: Factor $\lambda^{-1}$ out of $Q[V]$. Use (D.5) for its phase primitive and (D.4) with (5.8) for the normalized coefficients. Applying the slow curl via (D.3) costs one label derivative and $\ell_*^{-1}$, another fixed power of $\mathsf D$. These are the estimates combined in the proof of (5.31).
r2.lemma55.parent-product-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.lemma55_main: The all-order coefficient bounds are needed here: if the $n$-th coefficient derivative cost an additional parent power for every $n$, the exponent in (5.31) would grow with $n$. Proposition 5.1 uses the small label scale to avoid that. The proof `lemma55_main` combines those bounds with the primitive and curl estimates.

e02.lemma55.potential-time.TorusEuler.hasDerivWithinAt_wavePotentia: Since $Q[V]=\partial_s^{-1}(-r\kappa\times V)$ with $r=|\kappa|^{-2}$, differentiate the three factors at fixed $(a,s)$. Substitution of $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$ and $V_t=f-MV-\kappa\partial_s\mathsf p$ gives $-r_t\kappa\times V+r(M^T\kappa)\times V+r\kappa\times(MV-f)$. Here $r_t=2(\kappa\cdot M\kappa)|\kappa|^{-4}$. The centered primitive commutes with time differentiation; this is (5.33).
e02.lemma55.potential-time.TorusEuler.wavePotentialTimeSource: `wavePotentialTimeSource` is the expression inside the phase primitive in (5.33). It is centered because the coefficients depend only on $(t,a)$ and both $V$ and $f$ are centered. Its primitive is fixed by zero phase mean, so there is no additional function of $(t,a)$ to estimate in $Q_t$.

e02.lemma55.curl-commutator.TorusEuler.pulledBackCurl_material_eq: Although the phase is held fixed, the slow derivative moves with the parent: $\mathbf d_j=\sum_\alpha(D_aX)^{-1}_{\alpha j}\partial_{a_\alpha}$. Differentiating $D_aX$ gives $\partial_t(D_aX)^{-1}=-(D_aX)^{-1}M$. Hence $[\partial_t,\mathbf d_j]=-\sum_\ell M_{\ell j}\mathbf d_\ell$. Commuting time past the curl therefore costs only a first spatial derivative, with no derivative of $M$ in time.

r2.lemma55.relay-product-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.lemma55_main: The differentiated coefficient of the potential still has degree $-1$ in $\kappa$: the last term of (5.33) contains three covector factors and a denominator $|\kappa|^4$. The same degree occurs in (5.16) for $\partial_s\mathsf p$. The primitive estimate and a single label derivative therefore leave $\lambda^{-1}$ in every term of the relay. Taking a direct bound on $\partial_t V$ would not exhibit this gain.

e02.lemma55.no-time-derivatives.TorusEuler.wavePotentialTimeSource: In (5.33) the forcing is evaluated at the current time. For the relay from $V_p$, the contribution of the newly solved mean enters through $f_p^S$ and hence algebraically through $B_p$. This avoids the need to estimate $\partial_t B_p$ using the endpoint equation. The smoothness of the profiles justifies differentiation; the quantitative induction needs only the label and phase norms.
e02.lemma55.no-time-derivatives.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren: The commutator uses $M$, while differentiating the potential uses $M$ and $f$. Hence the linear relay needs no estimate of $\partial_t M$ or $\partial_t f$. Nor is there a term involving $\gamma'$: the estimate is for the differentiated field divided by $\gamma$, not for the derivative of a weighted field.

e02.hierarchy.spare-frequency.TorusEuler.hierarchy_fast_completion_exp: At level two the fast term with $C_2$ costs $\lambda^{3/2}\lambda^{-9/4}\lambda^{-5/4}=\lambda^{-2}$, up to parent factors. The target at that level is $\lambda^{-5/4-2/3}=\lambda^{-23/12}$. The difference is $1/12$. The exponent lemma is the same calculation for $i+j=p+1$, where the first generating velocity has index $i-1$. Choosing a decrement of $3/4$ would exhaust the gain of this interaction.
e02.hierarchy.spare-frequency.TorusEuler.hierarchy_absorb_parent_loss: After each solve the auxiliary bounds may carry a parent factor, but the next source is estimated using (5.40), which carries none. For each surplus $\delta\ge1/12$, $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-\delta}\le1$. Absorbing this factor before starting the next level is what lets one use a single exponent $C$ at every depth; it does not require the numerical constants of the levels to be uniform.

r2.thm56.all-orders.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.master_recurrence: For $B_p$ at order $n$, the mean inverse (5.12) requires the source at order $n+1$. Its slow products require earlier blocks at order $n+2$, and a curl in such a block may require its generating oscillation at order $n+3$. All generating indices are strictly below $p$. This accounts for the finite derivative reserve in the formal recurrence, or equivalently the paper's induction on the level at all orders.
r2.thm56.all-orders.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_5_6_of: The only current-level unknown on the source side of (5.28) is the already solved $B_p$, multiplying $\partial_sV_1$. Thus the order-$n$ transverse estimate needs only order $n$ of the new mean. The derivative loss in obtaining the mean is taken from earlier levels, which is why the finite expansion can use (5.12) without a derivative-losing estimate for $V_p$ itself.

e02.thm56.smallness.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_5_6: The hypothesis can be read as $\lambda\ge\mathsf D^{12C}$. For a fixed localization exponent in $\ell_*$, the exponent $C$ is chosen before $n,p,P$. The paper permits $C_{n,p}$ and $C_{m,P}$ to depend on those indices. In the actual step the stronger condition $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$ also accounts for the finite-depth constants needed after phase evaluation.
e02.thm56.smallness.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_5_6: If one propagated (5.34) directly, the coefficient powers from the inverse and from products of earlier velocities could accumulate. The induction instead keeps $f_p+f_p^S$ and $\lambda^{1/2}B_p$ bounded by pure powers of $\lambda$. Applying the inverse to that source recovers $V_p,\mathsf p_p$, and applying the curl estimate recovers $C_{p+1}$, with a bounded number of parent factors at each level.
e02.thm56.smallness.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc: In the existence theorem with a general cutoff the coefficient budget is $L=\mathsf D^{2a+b_0}$ for $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, so the smallness test is $\mathsf D^{6(2a+b_0)}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$. It chooses a seed and constructs a hierarchy for every allowed cutoff and depth; the numbered theorem instead bounds every admissible expansion.

The depth theorem for a supplied leading input starts after its homogeneous and switch identities, support and leading norm estimates have been verified. Its threshold absorbs the losses of the ensuing recurrence, not those missing leading-wave hypotheses. This is the part of the construction that can be reused without repeating the seed estimates.

e02.thm56.level-bounds.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_5_6: For the first correction $V_2$, (5.34) gives $\lambda^{-23/12}$, whereas the leading wave has size $\lambda^{-5/4}$. One physical derivative costs $\lambda^{3/2}$, so the correction gradient is at most a parent factor times $\lambda^{-5/12}$. The leading gradient at the origin, $\widetilde\chi\mathbf a\otimes\kappa$, is retained in Lemma 5.9. The mean $B_2$ and the curl $C_3$ are smaller still.
e02.thm56.level-bounds.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_5_6: At $p=2$, the pressure bound alone gives $\mathsf p_2$ of size $\lambda^{-35/12}$. Two physical derivatives at cost $\lambda^3$ would yield $\lambda^{1/12}$. Instead (5.16) gives $\kappa\partial_s\mathsf p_p=P_\kappa(f_p+f_p^S-2MV_p)$, and the slow gradient costs only parent powers. The full pressure gradient has the scale $\lambda^{-23/12}$; one further physical derivative gives $\lambda^{-5/12}$ as in (5.52). This is why the source is kept in (5.34).
e02.thm56.level-bounds.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc: The cutoff existence theorem packages the measured norms of the selected expansion with the uniform parent factor $L^6$. Its output includes the stronger mean bound as well as the weaker parent-free bound needed in the induction. This makes the recurrence applicable at every depth, with the choice of seed made before the depth and cutoff.

The center-wave version chooses the localized seed starting from the central solution of the transverse wave ODE. It uses the later-wave cutoff, then produces the level bounds for the resulting expansion. The parent and frequency condition are still required; central amplitude information alone would not imply the estimates for the spatially localized profiles.

The later-wave theorem uses the particular activation cutoff selected for the successive waves and a supplied regular seed. It concludes the frequency bounds for that construction, including the completion and mean. The more general numbered theorem does not require this particular cutoff shape beyond the prescribed cutoff conditions.
e02.thm56.level-bounds.TorusEuler.hierarchyOscExponent: Write $e_p=-5/4-2(p-1)/3$. The base scale $e_1=-5/4$ comes from $\mathbf a$ of size $\gamma\lambda^{-3/4}$ times a profile of size $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$. The chosen decrement is $2/3$. The first omitted level has $e_{P+1}=-5/4-2P/3$, exactly the exponent in (5.38).
e02.thm56.level-bounds.TorusEuler.hierarchyMeanExponent: The mean exponent is the sum of the two ordinary velocity exponents on $i+j=p$. In particular at level two the mean source has the scale of the square of the leading velocity, $\lambda^{-5/2}$. Averaging the fast product would give a worse power without (5.42), which transfers its phase derivative to the slow divergence of the preceding generator. The mean inverse preserves the resulting frequency power up to parent factors.
e02.thm56.level-bounds.TorusEuler.hierarchyCompletionExponent: The completion exponent is attached to the generating index $p$: if $e_p=-5/4-2(p-1)/3$, then $C_{p+1}$ has exponent $e_p-1=e_{p+1}-1/3$. It is smaller than the next transverse velocity by a further third of a frequency power, which justifies placing it in the next block $Y_{p+1}$.

e02.thm56.level-one.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_5_6: Level one is a prescribed leading wave, not a forced zero-start solve of the recursion. Lemma 5.3 bounds the unswitched amplitude and pressure, and Lemma 5.5 bounds its completion. The convention $f_1=f_1^S=0$ leaves the activation error separate even when $\widetilde\chi'$ is nonzero.
e02.thm56.level-one.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc: For the constructed seed the homogeneous estimate (5.22) and completion bound (5.31) apply before switching. Since the cutoff depends only on time and lies between zero and one, the same spatial and phase bounds hold for the switched fields. The existence theorem makes this the base of the chosen hierarchy.
e02.thm56.level-one.TorusEuler.HierarchyMeasuredLevels.ofPro: The first-level source entry in the measured family is zero by convention, whereas the actual switched leading wave has forcing $\widetilde\chi'A_1$. That forcing and its curl partner are kept in $R_{\widetilde\chi}$, so they do not enter the numerical recurrence for the higher levels.

e02.thm56.sum.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_5_6:
The summed mean equation is linear over the same parent, so its physical divergence gives $\Delta\sum_p ar q_p^
atural=\operatorname{div}(\sum_p ar f_p)^
atural-2\operatorname{tr}(
abla U
abla ar W^
atural)$. The time derivative of the mean drops out by solenoidality. All fields on the right other than the fixed parent are phase independent, so physical differentiation costs only parent powers. This is why Lemma 5.9 uses the bounds for both sums in (5.37) to control the mean pressure Hessian.
e02.thm56.sum.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc: For the selected hierarchy, the sum theorem keeps the amplitude weight on the oscillatory velocity and no weight on the means or mean sources. This is useful because the means may already be present before launch, unlike the oscillations. The bound is at finite depth and retains the common parent coefficient $L^6$.
e02.thm56.sum.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: This summation lemma assumes the numerical level bounds at the chosen order. The oscillatory sum includes $V_p$ and its attached $C_{p+1}$, whose extra $\lambda^{-1}$ is at most one; the mean sums begin at $p=2$. Bounding every term by its first-level power gives the explicit factor of order $P$ in the theorem.

e02.thm56.tail-estimate.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_5_6: The tail bound is in the independent profile variables. Lemma 5.7 costs at most $\lambda^3$ times a parent factor to evaluate it in physical $C^{1,1/2}$, using two scaled derivative orders. Thus the tail contributes $\lambda^{7/4-2P/3}$ up to those factors, weakened to $C_{\rm step}\lambda^2\lambda^{-2P/3}$ in Lemma 5.8. With $P=6K_{j+1}$ and $\lambda_{j+1}=\lambda_j^{K_{j+1}}$, the depth factor becomes $\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$. This is before adding the separately controlled switch and truncation errors.
e02.thm56.tail-estimate.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc: The constructed hierarchy has a remainder bound at every finite derivative order for the same depth, with $L^6\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$ used to absorb the parent coefficient. Increasing depth makes the frequency power smaller without changing the required exponent of the parent scale. The result concerns the selected expansion, with the cutoff error still separate.

e02.thm56.advection-bounds.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound: After centering, $(B_i\cdot\mathbf d)B_j$ disappears. Each remaining slow product contains at least one $Y$ factor, so put the single factor $\gamma^{-1}$ on it. In particular a product with two oscillations could be bounded pointwise by a factor $\gamma^2$, but the recurrence needs just $\gamma\le1$. No bound for $B_i/\gamma$ is required. The centering operator has norm at most two in the weighted supremum estimate, since $\gamma$ is constant in phase.

The second term in (5.39) has the slow derivative on the advecting field: $(\mathbf d\cdot Z)Z'$. This is the form produced by phase integration by parts in (5.42). Its bound costs one label derivative of $Z$, but no factor $\lambda^{3/2}$.
e02.thm56.advection-bounds.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli: In the scaled phase norm the derivative is $h\partial_s$. Thus $\kappa\partial_s=(\kappa/h)(h\partial_s)$ costs $\mathsf D^2\lambda^{3/2}$ since $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$ and $|\kappa|\le\mathsf D^2\lambda$. The fast term only uses $C_i+B_i$ in the advecting factor. The factor $\lambda^{3/2}$ by itself is larger than the level decrement; it is the smaller size of those fields that permits the shifted level assignment.

r2.thm56.leading-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_5_6_of: No estimate of $\widetilde\chi'$ is needed for the base of the spatial-norm induction. The cutoff commutes with the label and phase derivatives and reduces the magnitude of $A_1$, its pressure and completion. Its time derivative appears only in the separately retained activation error.

e02.thm56.induction-claim.TorusEuler.hierarchyInductiveMeanExponen: The separate estimate for the mean is needed in the fast products. Write $e_p=-5/4-2(p-1)/3$. A fast product with $i+j=p+1$ and both factors of ordinary level size would cost $\lambda^{3/2+e_i+e_j}=\lambda^{e_p+1/4}$. Giving $B_i$ the extra $\lambda^{-1/2}$ changes the exponent to $e_p-1/4$. Equation (5.42) supplies an even smaller mean, of exponent $e_i-7/12$, so one can lose $1/12$ in absorbing the parent power and still retain the half-power.
e02.thm56.induction-claim.TorusEuler.HierarchyLevelBound: In `HierarchyLevelBound`, $L$ bounds a primitive parent cost. The mean source has budget $L^5\lambda^{e_p-7/12}$ and its solve gives $L^6\lambda^{e_p-7/12}$, up to the level constant. From $L^6\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$ the same mean also satisfies the parent-free bound $\lambda^{e_p-1/2}$. Both are retained: the former for (5.35), the latter for the next source estimate.
e02.thm56.induction-claim.TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_bounds: The finite numerical induction makes the reserve of derivatives explicit: order $n$ at level $p$ is available if the recurrence holds through $H\ge n+3(p-1)+1$. This is a sufficient reserve, not a regularity requirement of exactly that many derivatives in the paper. The smooth construction and all-order recurrence allow $H$ to be chosen separately for each $(n,p)$.

e02.thm56.mean-induction-shift.TorusEuler.hierarchy_mean_inductive_shif: With $e_p=-5/4-2(p-1)/3$, the sharp mean estimate is $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{e_p-7/12}$. The smallness hypothesis gives $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-7/12}\le\lambda^{-1/2}$. This is the origin of the half-power in (5.40): the extra mean decay survives even after removing the parent factor.

r2.thm56.parent-exponent.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.master_recurrence: For the numerical recurrence take $L$ to bound each primitive coefficient or inverse cost. Starting with the parent-free transverse source, the inverse gives $V_i$ a factor $L$, and the completion can cost $L^2$. A slow product of two such blocks, including its advection estimate, costs at most $L^5$. The mean inverse gives $L^6$; the smallness condition absorbs this factor before the new mean is used in (5.28). This counts losses along the current level, not along all previous levels.

e02.thm56.constant-does-not-accumulate.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_5_6: Uniformity concerns the exponent of $\mathsf D$, not the constants $C_{n,p}$. The latter account for the number of products and the estimates at higher derivative orders in earlier levels. The theorem needs no growth bound for these constants as $p\to\infty$ because the hierarchy for each wave is finite.
e02.thm56.constant-does-not-accumulate.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc: In the cutoff existence result one budget $L^6$ suffices for every retained level, with the seed chosen before the cutoff and depth. The level constants and the finite-sum constants remain separate. It does not assert that these constants stay bounded as $P$ tends to infinity; the construction needs only finite depth for each wave.
e02.thm56.constant-does-not-accumulate.TorusEuler.hierarchy_absorb_parent_loss: For $\lambda\ge1$, a surplus $\delta\ge1/12$ gives $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-\delta}\le\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$. The same numerical inequality works at any level. The parent-free induction, rather than this inequality alone, is what ensures the parent exponent to be absorbed remains fixed.

c8-hierarchy-source-support-step.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.master_recurrence: The forward inverse compares transverse evolution on the envelope with the evolution at the origin. Its weighted bound is based on a ratio $\gamma(t)/\gamma(t')$ for the propagator, so dividing by $\gamma(t)$ leaves the integral of the forcing divided by $\gamma(t')$. Proposition 5.4 provides exactly the support and zero-start conditions for applying this estimate to the source at level $i$; without those conditions the bound near the origin would not control the full profile.

c8-hierarchy-solve-completion-step.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.master_recurrence: The order-$n$ transverse bound (5.21) uses the source at order $n$, but the order-$n$ curl estimate (5.31) uses the velocity at order $n+1$. Thus (5.40) at order $n+1$ supplies the necessary bound to form $C_{i+1}$, including its extra $\lambda^{-1}$. There is no circular estimate involving the derivative of the new mean because (5.28) contains it undifferentiated.

r2.thm56.level-block-definitions.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Yd: The subscript of $C_i$ here is its size level, not the index of the oscillation that generates it. Thus $Y_i=V_i+C[V_{i-1}]$ for $i\ge2$ and $Y_1=V_1$. Lean stores the correction at its generating index; `Cd u i` supplies the preceding correction for the paper's size block.
r2.thm56.level-block-definitions.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Zd: At fixed level $i$, $Z_i$ has full divergence $\mathbf d\cdot V_i-\mathbf d\cdot V_{i-1}$. This is generally nonzero. The size blocks are chosen to estimate products; the solenoidal grouping instead pairs $V_i$ with $C_{i+1}$. The difference between these two groupings is essential in (5.42), where the divergence of $V_{i-1}$ replaces phase differentiation of $C_i$.

e02.thm56.previous-completion.TorusEuler.hierarchy_completion_previous: At $i\ge2$, the estimate of $C_i=C[V_{i-1}]$ is $\lambda^{-9/4-2(i-2)/3}=\lambda^{-1/3}\lambda^{-5/4-2(i-1)/3}$ up to parent powers. The completion is already one third of a power below its assigned level, so replacing $V_i$ by $Y_i$ does not change the target exponent. At $i=1$ the correction is zero.
e02.thm56.previous-completion.TorusEuler.hierarchyInductiveMeanExponen: For the mean the induction gives $\|B_i\|_{[n]}\lesssim\lambda^{e_i-1/2}$, with $e_i=-5/4-2(i-1)/3$ and the level constant understood. Since $Y_i$ vanishes before activation, its unweighted norm is at most its weighted norm on the active interval. Adding $B_i$ therefore gives the unweighted $Z_i$ bound in (5.41). The mean need not obey the corresponding weighted bound.

e02.thm56.block-bounds.TorusEuler.HierarchyLevelBound: The paper writes a bound for $\|Z_i\|_{[n]}$. The formal recurrence uses the stronger quantity $\|Y_i\|_{[n],\gamma}+\|B_i\|_{[n]}$. The two summands are kept separate because a weighted quadratic estimate may place its time weight on an oscillatory factor, but cannot necessarily place it on a mean. The stronger quantity bounds the paper's norm by the triangle inequality and the vanishing prefix.
e02.thm56.block-bounds.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc: The hierarchy produced by the theorem bounds the two measured quantities $Y$ and $Z$ with the same frequency exponent and a common parent budget. Here the measured $Z$ is a sum of the weighted oscillatory norm and the unweighted mean norm, a stronger budget than the unweighted norm in (5.41). It does not require the mean to vanish before $t_0$ or to be small relative to $\gamma(t)$.

e02.thm56.label-product-power.TorusEuler.hierarchy_label_product_expon: In a slow product with $i+j=p$, the exponents add to $-5/2-2(p-2)/3=e_p-7/12$. The derivative acts at fixed phase, so it introduces no factor of $\lambda$. The same diagonal appears in the mean source after integration by parts in (5.42), which explains why its target exponent in (5.35) is the slow-product exponent rather than the fast-product exponent.

e02.thm56.fast-completion-power.TorusEuler.hierarchy_fast_completion_exp: The first index of the fast sum is the size level of the completion, not its generating level. With $e_i=-5/4-2(i-1)/3$, the product has exponent $3/2+e_{i-1}-1+e_j=e_p-1/12$ when $i+j=p+1$. The cost $\lambda^{3/2}$ is thus paid by the extra inverse frequency of the completion and the small size of the two generating oscillations. This is the smallest margin among the three bounds for $f_p$.

e02.thm56.fast-mean-integration.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera: Integrate in the independent phase at fixed $(t,a)$: $\langle(C_i\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY_j\rangle_s=-\langle\partial_s(C_i\cdot\kappa)Y_j\rangle_s$. By (3.6), $\partial_s(C_i\cdot\kappa)=-\mathbf d\cdot V_{i-1}$. Thus the averaged interaction contains a label derivative of $V_{i-1}$ and no fast derivative. Its indices now sum to $(i-1)+j=p$, rather than $i+j=p+1$. In particular at $p=2$ it has two leading-wave factors, just like the slow product.

e02.thm56.linear-mean-zero.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera: The relay is $\partial_t C_p+MC_p+\mathbf d\mathsf p_{p-1}$ (with the unswitched expression times the cutoff at $p=2$). All three operations commute with the phase average because the coefficients and cutoff are independent of $s$. The centered potential makes $C_p$ centered and the transverse pressure is normalized to be centered. Thus the relay contributes nothing to the mean at any level.

e02.thm56.mixed-products-zero.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera: For the product $(Y_i\cdot\mathbf d)B_j$, the mean and its derivatives can be taken out of the phase integral. Its average is $(\langle Y_i\rangle_s\cdot\mathbf d)B_j=0$. This uses phase independence of the differentiated factor and centering of the advecting factor.

For $(B_i\cdot\mathbf d)Y_j$, the phase-independent advecting field and derivative coefficients commute with averaging. The result is $(B_i\cdot\mathbf d)\langle Y_j\rangle_s=0$. Both possible mixed label products thus disappear from the mean equation.

e02.thm56.slow-mean-source.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera: Since $\mathbf d\cdot C_i=0$, the two oscillatory terms on the right can be added pairwise: their component $\ell$ is $\sum_k\mathbf d_k\langle(Y_i)_k(Y_j)_\ell\rangle_s$. The same product rule applies to $(B_i\cdot\mathbf d)B_j$, since $\mathbf d\cdot B_i=0$. Thus $-\bar f_p$ is the slow divergence of the stresses on $i+j=p$, plus $R_U\circ X$ at $p=2$. The linked lemma proves the three-sum form of $\langle H_p\rangle_s$.
e02.thm56.slow-mean-source.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: At $p=2$ the only stress is $\langle V_1\otimes V_1\rangle_s$. Writing $A=\widetilde\chi g\mathbf a$, it equals $A\otimes A\int_0^1 F_h(s)^2\,ds$. The divergence differentiates $A$ at fixed phase and so costs no power of $\lambda$.
