Its two factors give $\lambda^{-5/2}$ up to parent factors. The term $R_U\circ X$ is included only at $p=2$ because it has the same permitted scale by (5.10).

e02.thm56.mean-product-power.TorusEuler.hierarchy_mean_product_expone: The mean products have the same slow diagonal $i+j=p$, but each factor has the additional half-power in (5.40). Hence their power is $e_i+e_j-1=-7/2-2(p-2)/3$, one full inverse frequency smaller than the averaged oscillatory products. Since $B_1=0$, there are no such products at $p=2$ or $3$.

e02.thm56.supplementary-source-power.TorusEuler.hierarchy_fast_mean_exponent: The most immediate use of the new estimate of $B_p$ is the summand $-(B_p\cdot\kappa)\partial_sV_1$. The differentiated leading profile costs $\lambda^{1/4}$ up to parent factors; multiplying by the parent-free mean $\lambda^{e_p-1/2}$ gives $\lambda^{e_p-1/4}$. The same calculation with $i+j=p+1$ gives the common exponent for all summands, without taking a derivative of the new mean.

e02.thm56.absorption.TorusEuler.hierarchy_absorb_parent_loss: The mean source first has the power $e_p-7/12$. The mean inverse and absorption of the parent factor spend at most $1/12$, leaving the mean at $e_p-1/2$. Only then is the supplementary source estimated, at $e_p-1/4$ up to parent factors. Together with the centered source at $e_p-1/12$, it gives the parent-free transverse source in (5.40). These are successive estimates of different quantities at the same level.

r2.thm56.depth-independent-constants.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.levelConstant_indep: Changing the ultimate depth does not change the sums defining the lower levels: only indices at most the current level enter. The corresponding numerical recurrence likewise gives the same level constant at index $p$ for all ambient depths at least $p$, with its recurrence parameter fixed. This equality does not assert boundedness of the constants as $p$ increases.
r2.thm56.depth-independent-constants.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_5_6_of: For an estimate at order $n$ and level $p$, the formal proof chooses its finite derivative reserve using $n+3p+1$. The resulting level constant is defined before choosing a final depth $P$. The constants for the total sum and the remainder may depend on $P$, as expected for a finite expansion.

e02.thm56.sum-from-levels.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_5_6_of: In the oscillatory sum each generator is paired with its own curl, which has an extra $\lambda^{-1}$, so the largest frequency power comes from $p=1$. For the two mean sums the first possible level is $p=2$, giving $\lambda^{-5/2}$. The constants of these finitely many levels are included in $C_{m,P}$, rather than assuming uniform convergence as $P$ increases.
e02.thm56.sum-from-levels.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The finite-sum lemma bounds the sum of the transverse fields and their attached corrections by a common level constant times $2P$, and treats the two mean sums starting at level two. This makes no assumption about convergence of the hierarchy as $P\to\infty$.

r2.thm56.weighted-to-unweighted.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_le_wNorm: For every spatial derivative of a profile that vanishes before $t_0$, its supremum over $[0,T]$ is its supremum over $[t_0,T]$. On this latter interval multiply its weighted bound by $\gamma(t)\le1$ to recover an unweighted bound. The linear relay and each product containing an oscillatory factor have this property; a product of two means need not have it and is estimated directly over $[0,T]$.

r2.thm56.remainder-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_5_6_of: The first omitted level is $q=P+1$: a slow product has $i+j=q$, a fast product $i+j=q+1$. With $e_q=-5/4-2(q-1)/3$, both are bounded by a parent factor times $\lambda^{e_q-1/12}$ or better. Since $e_q$ decreases and $\lambda\ge1$, the largest such bound is at $q=P+1$. The final linear relay has power $e_P-1=e_{P+1}-1/3$. Absorb the parent factors and sum; no inverse at level $P+1$ is needed.
r2.thm56.remainder-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.master_recurrence: The proof can use the same product estimates at the first omitted level because $Z_{P+1}=Y_{P+1}=C[V_P]$ has exponent $e_P-1=e_{P+1}-1/3$. Although the formal recurrence stops at $P$, the last completion already meets the next size-block bound. The tail then consists of known products and the final relay; the switch residual is outside this estimate.

euler02.approximate.fields.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_8: Here the decomposition of $W$ is in the independent phase variable $s$, before graph evaluation. In particular $\bar W(t,a)$ still depends on the label $a$. In physical coordinates it is read at the inverse parent label; differentiation therefore involves no derivative of the new phase.
euler02.approximate.fields.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: At $x=X(t,a)$ the definition reads $V(t,X(t,a))=U(t,X(t,a))+W(t,a,k_*\cdot a)$. The flow used in this substitution is the flow of the parent $U$, not the flow of $V$; the child flow will be estimated after the construction.

The pressure $\Pi$ is the one obtained in canceling the hierarchy. Since (5.46) has a momentum defect, $\Delta\Pi=\operatorname{div}R_V-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla V)^2)$. Even if $V$ were left unchanged, its Poisson pressure would differ from $\Pi$ by a solution of $\Delta(p_V-\Pi)=-\operatorname{div}R_V$. Subtracting a spatial constant cannot remove this source. The pressure estimate after truncation must therefore account for the defect as well as the velocity tail.

The oscillatory terms $V_p+C_{p+1}$ have zero average in $s$, so $\bar W=\sum_{p=1}^PB_p$ (with $B_1=0$). Evaluation of this sum at the inverse label gives $\bar W^\natural(t,x)$. It is not obtained by averaging the evaluated velocity in $x$, which would give a vector independent of $x$ rather than the mean correction field.

euler02.approximate.common-exponent.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_8: The point of a depth-independent exponent is that (5.43) must still hold at $P=6K_{j+1}$, not only at some fixed depth. In Section 7 the parent loss $\mathsf D^b$ becomes $\lambda_j^{9b/K_j}$ and the depth-dependent constant is bounded by the threshold at $q_{j+1}$. Enlarging the depth to reduce the remainder does not enlarge this exponent of the new frequency.
euler02.approximate.common-exponent.TorusEuler.paperPhysicalStepExponent: The explicit choice $b=6r+5a+2a_{\rm mean}+160$ depends on the hierarchy, coframe and mean exponents, not on the number of levels. For instance, the residual tail uses the power $2(\max(a,1)+1)$ and the residual from activation uses this power plus $a+27$. Both are at most $b$; the remaining coefficients, including the number of levels, are absorbed into $\Gamma_P$.

euler02.approximate.step-constant.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_8: In step $j$, $\mathsf D=\lambda_{j-1}^9$ and $\Gamma_P\le\mathcal B(q_{j+1})\le\lambda_{j-1}$. Hence $C_{\rm step}\le\lambda_{j-1}^{9b+1}\le\lambda_{j-1}^{10b}$. In terms of the new frequency this is at most $\lambda_j^{10b/K_j}$, which is the parent loss to be absorbed in (7.8).
euler02.approximate.step-constant.TorusEuler.exists_paperPhysicalStepBudge: The constant $\Gamma_P$ is chosen before the parent scale. Each of the required bounds has finitely many terms of the form $c\mathsf D^e$, with $c\ge0$ independent of $\mathsf D$ and $e\le b$. The proof adds the coefficients for the flow, oscillation, two residual sources, central gradient and pressure. Since $\mathsf D\ge1$, the sum times $\mathsf D^b$ bounds all six expressions simultaneously.

euler02.approximate.constant-dependence.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_8: The bound $C_{\rm step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ is used for the fixed-order estimates that must be small at every step. For truncation we instead need the full velocity through the increasing order $P$. The factor $\mathsf D^{b(P+2)}$ in (5.48) is allowed there because the cutoff supplies $\Lambda^{2-P}$ in (5.55). The proof of Theorem 7.1 checks the balance between these two depth-dependent powers separately.
euler02.approximate.constant-dependence.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.lemma_5_8_of_odd: The two terms of the residual in (5.46) both need two profile derivatives for the physical $C^{1,1/2}$ estimate. In the activation term these are derivatives of the completed field $A_1+C[A_1]$: Lemma 5.5 uses three derivatives of $A_1$ to control two of its completion. These are still fixed orders, so the coefficient of the residual need not depend on the arbitrary order $m$ of the velocity estimate.
euler02.approximate.constant-dependence.TorusEuler.exists_paperPhysicalStepBudge: For the oscillation the finite sum gives the coefficient $2P C_{\rm level}$, multiplying $\mathsf D^{2r}$. The number of summands may grow without changing the power $2r$ of the parent. In contrast a factor $\mathsf D^P$ would not be a fixed-order constant: it could not be included in $\Gamma_P$ independently of the parent.

euler02.approximate.smallness.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_8: After fixing the parent and the depth, (5.43) amounts to $\lambda\ge(\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b)^{12}$. In the induction there is a stronger margin: $C_{\rm step}\le\lambda^{1/32}$ by (7.8). It leaves, for example, the negative power $\lambda^{-7/32}$ in the one-sided pressure estimate (5.49).
euler02.approximate.smallness.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc: The central wave is an input, normalized by $\max|\mathbf a(t,0)|=\lambda^{-3/4}$. The linked existence theorem then selects a localized seed before quantifying over admissible time cutoffs. Hence the size and sign estimates for the seed apply to the very wave whose early amplitude is used in choosing the switch; there is no need to repeat the seed construction after choosing the cutoff.

euler02.approximate.hierarchy-smallness.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.lemma_5_8_of_odd: If $C_6$ is the exponent supplied by Theorem 5.6, the choice $b\ge C_6$ and $\Gamma_P\ge1$ gives $\mathsf D^{C_6}\lambda^{-1/12}\le\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$. In the proof of Lemma 5.8, $b$ also absorbs the fixed powers from two graph derivatives and the estimate for the completed primary field.
euler02.approximate.hierarchy-smallness.TorusEuler.PaperPhysicalStepBudget.hiera: In the scalar budget the hierarchy loss is $\mathsf D^r$ and its smallness test involves its sixth power. Thus $\mathsf D^{6r}\lambda^{-1/12}\le\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, using $b\ge6r$, $\Gamma_P\ge1$ and $\mathsf D\ge1$.

euler02.approximate.graph-evaluation.TorusEuler.hierarchyGraphPoint: The graph point is $(t,A(t,x),k_*\cdot A(t,x))$, with $A(t,\cdot)=X(t,\cdot)^{-1}$. Along the parent trajectory $x=X(t,a)$ this becomes $(t,a,k_*\cdot a)$: only the first coordinate changes with time. At fixed $x$, however, both the label and phase vary, which is why spatial differentiation below uses the twisted coframe.
euler02.approximate.graph-evaluation.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph:
For a scalar component $f$, write $f^
atural(t,x)=f(t,A(t,x),k_*\cdot A(t,x))$. The ordinary chain rule gives $\partial_{x_i}f^
atural=\sum_l(\partial_{x_i}A_l)(\partial_{a_l}f+k_{*,l}\partial_s f)^
atural$. This is the operator $\widetilde{\mathbf d}_i$ used throughout the hierarchy.

euler02.approximate.graph-cell-hypothese.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_7: The carrier need not be a dual-lattice vector. In two neighboring label cells the phases differ by $k_*\cdot n$ under translation by a lattice vector $n$. Near each face only the phase average of $g_0$ is present, and this average is periodic. Thus all graph values and derivatives agree across the face; no restriction on $k_*$ is needed to obtain a smooth periodic physical field.
euler02.approximate.graph-cell-hypothese.TorusEuler.paperLemma57_periodicGraphFro: In the periodic lift the inverse label satisfies $A(t,x+n)=A(t,x)+n$ for $n\in\mathbb Z^3$. The phase need not agree after this translation. The collar condition makes the profile equal to its periodic mean there, so the mean may be extended periodically and the oscillation by matching zero values near the cell faces. The two extensions yield a smooth periodic graph field with the same local derivative estimates.

euler02.approximate.graph-bounds.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_7: The same oscillatory profile can be small in value and large in gradient. At $m=0$ no derivative of the phase is taken, giving the scale $\lambda^{-5/4}$. At $m=1$ the upper bound loses $\lambda^{3/2}$, giving $\lambda^{1/4}$ up to parent powers. This is an upper estimate on the whole wave, not a lower bound on its central gradient; the latter uses the normalization $F_h'(0)=1$ and the central identity (5.50).
euler02.approximate.graph-bounds.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_7: In the formal version the sum in (5.44) runs over all ordered words of $m$ spatial directions. A multi-index $\beta$ occurs $m!/\beta!$ times in that sum, since the derivatives of the smooth evaluated field commute. The word bound therefore implies the displayed multi-index bound, and permits iteration of the one-derivative estimate without collecting multiplicities at each stage.
euler02.approximate.graph-bounds.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.paper: On the active interval write $g_0=\gamma(t)(g_0/\gamma(t))$. Every spatial graph derivative commutes with the factor $\gamma(t)$, so it is restored just once, regardless of the derivative order. The linked estimate assumes the carrier and scaled inverse-coframe bounds; it applies to any positive continuous weight, not just the weight obtained from the central wave.
euler02.approximate.graph-bounds.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc: The inverse coframe in the evaluation operator belongs to $X$, the flow of the already constructed parent $U$. In particular the coefficient of a graph derivative is fixed independently of the field being evaluated. The same estimate can be applied to $W$, $\mathsf P$, or $R_P$ before any bounds on the flow of the new velocity $V$ have been established.

euler02.approximate.graph-unweighted.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_7: An inactive wave need not give a zero remainder. Outside the active region $R_P$ is phase independent, but it still contains the mean interactions $(B_i\cdot\mathbf d)B_j$ of levels with $i+j>P$. The unit-weight estimate controls these on $[0,T]$, without extending the active-time amplitude weight $\gamma$ to times before $t_0$.
euler02.approximate.graph-unweighted.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.paper: Taking the weight identically one gives a bound on the whole parent slab, rather than only on $[t_0,T]$. This is a change in the time supremum, not in the spatial differentiation operator: the factor $\lambda^{3m/2}$ in (5.44) and the extra derivative for (5.45) are unchanged.

euler02.approximate.graph-mean.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_7: For the mean, $\widetilde{\mathbf d}f=\mathbf df$; all successive derivatives remain phase independent since the coframe has no $s$ dependence. Thus each derivative costs only a power of the parent bound, regardless of the new carrier. This accounts for the common frequency power $\lambda^{-5/2}$ at all orders of the mean in (5.48).
euler02.approximate.graph-mean.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.paper: For a phase-independent profile let $f_0(t,a)=f(t,a,0)$. Then $f^\natural(t)=f_0(t)\circ X(t)^{-1}$. All derivatives in the profile norm involving $s$ vanish, and the remaining chain rule contains only derivatives of the inverse parent flow and the label envelope. The factor $\gamma(t)$ is still restored after evaluation; it is a time weight, not part of the phase scale.

The mean does not vanish just because the wave has not started. Indeed its endpoint condition constrains the integral of the label velocity, not its value at $t=0$. Here one takes the unit weight on all of $[0,T]$ and uses the phase-independent graph estimate. No extension of $\gamma$ to the inactive interval is necessary.

euler02.approximate.graph-extension.TorusEuler.paperLemma57_periodicGraphFro: One may extend the graph field first in the label variable and then compose with the inverse flow. At identified faces the phase shifts by $k_*\cdot n$, but the field agrees with its periodic mean in a neighborhood of each face. The same holds after differentiation, since the coframe is periodic in the label and independent of the phase.

euler02.approximate.derivative-cost.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_7_of: In the profile norm, $\ell_*\nabla_a$ and $h\partial_s$ are the scaled derivatives. The physical derivative contains $k_*\partial_s=(k_*/h)(h\partial_s)$. Since $|k_*|\le\mathsf D\lambda$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, its cost is $\mathsf D\lambda^{3/2}$; the cost of $\ell_*^{-1}$ and of the coframe is absorbed in the parent power.
euler02.approximate.derivative-cost.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.words_general: Put $D_l=\partial_{a_l}+k_{*,l}\partial_s$ and write $\widetilde{\mathbf d}_i=\sum_l c_{il}D_l$. Then $\widetilde{\mathbf d}_i\widetilde{\mathbf d}_jf=\sum_{l,n}c_{il}c_{jn}D_lD_nf+\sum_{l,n}c_{il}(\partial_{a_l}c_{jn})D_nf$. The second sum is why the differentiated inverse coframe is needed in the scaled product estimate. No phase derivative falls on a coframe coefficient.
euler02.approximate.derivative-cost.TorusEuler.physicalHierarchy_graph_cost: In physical coordinates the phase derivative has coefficient $\kappa=(D_aX)^{-T}k_*$. The steep part of the profile has physical normal thickness of order $h/|\kappa|$ locally, where $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$; differentiating it costs $|\kappa|/h\le\mathsf D^2\lambda^{3/2}$. In labels the same cost is $|k_*|/h\le\mathsf D\lambda^{3/2}$ before the inverse coframe is applied. The envelope and differentiated coframe cost powers of the parent alone.
euler02.approximate.derivative-cost.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc: The coefficient estimates use the parent flow and its inverse, whose higher derivatives are controlled through the parent Fourier bound. Thus the $\mathsf D$ losses in the chain rule refer to data already available at the start of the step. No estimate on the child flow is used to differentiate its profiles.

euler02.approximate.graph-iteration.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_7_of: At each application of the one-derivative estimate, the required profile order increases by one. Thus bounding the order-zero norm of all words of length $m$ uses the estimates at orders $0,\ldots,m-1$ successively, and costs at most $(\prod_{n=0}^{m-1}C_n)(\mathsf D^C\lambda^{3/2})^m\|g_0\|_{[m],\gamma}$. The exponent $C$ is fixed throughout; only the coefficient depends on $m$.
euler02.approximate.graph-iteration.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.paper: The weighted norm controls a profile at time $t$ after division by $\gamma(t)$. Since each of the spatial operators acts only on $a,s$, this division can be made before the entire sequence of derivatives. The last evaluation therefore restores a single factor $\gamma(t)$, not one such factor per derivative.

euler02.approximate.holder-from-jets.TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalfNorm_le_of_u: For $d=|x-y|>0$, let $B_j,B_{j+1}$ bound the derivatives of orders $j,j+1$. The difference of the order-$j$ derivatives is at most $\min(2B_j,B_{j+1}d)\le\sqrt{2B_jB_{j+1}d}$. Dividing by $\sqrt d$ gives the half-Hölder seminorm. Taking $B_j,B_{j+1}\le B$ gives the linked bound $3(m+1)B$ on the sum of the supremum norms and seminorms through $m$. This explains the one extra ordinary derivative used in (5.45).

euler02.approximate.mean-no-phase-cost.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.words_phaseIndep: Since the coefficients of $\mathbf d$ do not depend on phase, $\partial_s\mathbf d_i f=\mathbf d_i\partial_s f$. Thus if $\partial_s f=0$, every iterated label derivative is also phase independent. The factor $k_*\partial_s$ drops out at every order of the graph differentiation.
euler02.approximate.mean-no-phase-cost.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_7_of: Applied to $\bar W$, the mean version of (5.45) gives $C_{m,P}\mathsf D^{b(m+2)}\lambda^{-5/2}$ in (5.48). The extra derivative needed for the half-Hölder seminorm increases the parent power but leaves $\lambda^{-5/2}$ unchanged. It is this fixed negative power of the new frequency, even at high spatial orders, that will control the nonoscillatory increments in (7.4).
euler02.approximate.mean-no-phase-cost.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.paper: For the mean there is no derivative in $s$ even when derivatives fall on the inverse coframe, because that coframe is itself phase independent. Thus the estimate at order $m$ contains the same parent cost for the label jets, but no factor $\lambda^{3(m+1)/2}$. In particular increasing the spatial order does not consume the mean's $\lambda^{-5/2}$ decay.

euler02.approximate.regularity.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_8: The approximation is exact in the divergence equation; only the momentum equation has the defect (5.46). This distinction is necessary when deriving the projected equation for the truncated child, since no correction to enforce incompressibility is then needed.
euler02.approximate.regularity.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_8: The retained transverse and mean equations stop at level $P$, but $C_{P+1}=\mathbf d\times Q[V_P]$ is still included. Pairing each $V_p$ with its own completion gives a twisted curl, and the mean terms are separately divergence free. Thus stopping the momentum cancellation at level $P$ does not truncate the exact divergence cancellation. The completion is not in general purely longitudinal.
euler02.approximate.regularity.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_smooth: Composition with the smooth inverse parent flow gives smoothness of each evaluated profile. The extension across the cell faces uses the phase-independent collar. Oddness and zero divergence follow instead from the reflection law and the exact profile divergence identity.
euler02.approximate.regularity.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The matrix and coframe in the hierarchy are those of the actual flow of $U$, namely $M=\nabla U\circ X$ and $(D_aX)^{-T}$. Although the leading wave is chosen using the equations at the center, graph evaluation uses the full spatially varying coefficients. Consequently there is no additional error from replacing the parent by its linearization in (5.46).

This equality reads out the two momentum sources from the assembled profiles, assuming their smoothness, parity, divergence and exact momentum identity in `PhysicalApproximationProperties`. It is the identity part of Lemma 5.8, not yet its estimate. The bounds on the hierarchy tail and the unswitched primary field enter only when estimating the two sources in (5.48).

euler02.approximate.euler-residual.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_8: The negative of the parent's residual is included in the profile source at level two. After adding the parent equation, the only momentum sources left are $R_P$ from the finite expansion and $\widetilde\chi'(A_1+C[A_1])$ from activation. They are made small by different choices: increasing the depth $P$ and placing the switch while the unswitched wave is small.
euler02.approximate.euler-residual.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_residual: The momentum operator of $U+W^\natural$ is $R_U$ plus the evaluation of $W_t+MW+(W\cdot\widetilde{\mathbf d})W+\widetilde{\mathbf d}\mathsf P$. Equation (5.29) identifies the profile expression with $-R_U\circ X+R_P+R_{\widetilde\chi}$. Evaluation cancels $R_U$ exactly.
euler02.approximate.euler-residual.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The residual here is the residual of the pair $(V,\Pi)$, not of $V$ with its zero-mean Poisson pressure. The record gives the exact identity (5.46); (5.48) then estimates its right-hand side. The projection and change of pressure needed for the next parent occur only after truncation.

At a point $x=X(t,a)$ the source in the profile equation is the negative of the parent residual at $x$. Adding the parent equation therefore cancels it pointwise. There is no remainder from the change of coordinates; only the finite expansion and time-cutoff terms remain.
euler02.approximate.euler-residual.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.momen:
At $x=X(t,a)$ we have $(\partial_t+U\cdot
abla)W^
atural=(W_t)^
atural$, while $W^
atural\cdot
abla W^
atural=((W\cdot\widetilde{\mathbf d})W)^
atural$. Adding gives the derivative of the correction along $V=U+W^
atural$. The additional term $(MW)^
atural$ is the derivative of the parent velocity in the correction direction; together these account for the full quadratic nonlinearity.

euler02.approximate.oscillation-sup.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_8: Only the supremum bound for $W_{\rm osc}^\natural$ is needed to sum the velocities on the full slab. The estimate therefore uses (5.44) at order zero, rather than the half-Hölder estimate (5.45). The latter would spend a full extra graph derivative and lose the negative power of $\lambda$ needed here.
euler02.approximate.oscillation-sup.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: At each active time the evaluated phase is among those in the profile supremum, so $|W_{\rm osc}^\natural(t,x)|\le\gamma(t)\|W_{\rm osc}\|_{[0],\gamma}$. The profile bound sums the transverse fields with their curl completions, including the last one. The whole oscillation is zero before $t_0$, and $\gamma\le1$ on the active interval; hence the time supremum costs no additional frequency factor.
euler02.approximate.oscillation-sup.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc: The estimate is for the oscillatory part of the same finite expansion that satisfies (5.46). Its global supremum does not require a bound on its gradient. The subsequent estimate of the mean and the Fourier tail, rather than (5.47), controls the rest of the increment in the prescribed derivative orders.

euler02.approximate.physical-estimates.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_8: The high-order bound on the oscillation is used in the opposite way from (5.47): it need not be small, since it is multiplied by a Fourier-tail factor. At the chosen depth item 4 of Theorem 7.1 gives $1+\|V\|_{C_tC^{P,1/2}}\le3\lambda^{2(P+1)}$. In (5.55) the cutoff $\Lambda=\lambda^5$ then gives $9\lambda^{5(2-P)+4(P+1)}=9\lambda^{14-P}$. With this bound, a cutoff at $\lambda^4$ would not yield decay with $P$. The extra power makes increasing the depth effective even after squaring the full velocity norm.
euler02.approximate.physical-estimates.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: For $m=1$, (5.48) gives a frequency factor $\lambda^{7/4}$ because the Hölder estimate spends two graph derivatives. The first derivative alone has the sharper bound $\lambda^{1/4}$ from (5.44). The extra loss is a convenient way of estimating the seminorm, not a new contribution to the gradient. The separate value and first-derivative bounds can also be interpolated to obtain spatial Hölder estimates of order below one.

The absence of a carrier cost does not mean that higher means have uniformly bounded derivatives in the parent scale. At step $j$, for $m\le q_j$, the coefficient $\mu^{10b(m+2)}$ is at most $\lambda^{1/16}$ by $K_j=320b(q_j+1)$ and $m+2\le2(q_j+1)$. Thus $\lambda^{-5/2}$ has ample decay left: the mean is bounded by $\lambda^{-3/2}$ through all the orders required at this step. The other part of (7.4) is supplied by the Fourier tail.

Both residuals are estimated in $C^{1,1/2}$ by the order-two profile bound. Multiplication by $\lambda^3$ turns the hierarchy tail into $\lambda^{7/4-2P/3}$ and the switch term into $\lambda^{7/4}|\widetilde\chi'|\gamma$, apart from parent factors. Replacing $7/4$ by $2$ gives the common prefactor in (5.48). The first estimate is unweighted on the entire slab; the second is needed only on the support of the switch derivative.
euler02.approximate.physical-estimates.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc: For each admissible cutoff the linked result supplies one expansion with all the bounds of (5.48), as well as the pressure and central-gradient estimates. In particular the residual belongs to the velocity whose norms are estimated here. Its cutoff term retains the factor $\|\widetilde\chi'\gamma\|_\infty$; obtaining a small residual still requires the specific early switch of Section 6.

euler02.approximate.cutoff-supremum.TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.derivativeSiz: The crucial bound is on $|\widetilde\chi'|\gamma$, not on $\widetilde\chi'$ alone or on the product of the two separate suprema. The derivative vanishes outside the first unit of normalized time, where the gain estimate gives $\gamma\le e^{3-\varepsilon^{-1/2}}$. Consequently even a switch with $|\widetilde\chi'|\le Cr$ has residual coefficient at most $Cr e^{3-\varepsilon^{-1/2}}$. For wave one this coefficient is zero.

euler02.approximate.momentum-chain-rule.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_residual: At $x=X(t,a)$, differentiating $W(t,a,k_*\cdot a)$ in time holds $a$ and $k_*\cdot a$ fixed. This gives the first identity. Differentiating in $x$ holds time fixed and differentiates both label and phase, giving $\widetilde{\mathbf d}$ in the other identities. The parent gradient contributes $M(t,a)=\nabla U(t,X(t,a))$.
euler02.approximate.momentum-chain-rule.TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.moment:
For the full velocity, the transport operator on the correction decomposes as $(\partial_t+U\cdot
abla)W^
atural+W^
atural\cdot
abla W^
atural$. The first term is a derivative at fixed $(a,s)$, and the second uses the physical graph derivatives. The remaining cross term $W^
atural\cdot
abla U$ is $(MW)^
atural$. This accounts for all terms in (5.29).

euler02.approximate.parent-cancellation.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_residual: Explicitly, $(R_U\circ X)^\natural(t,x)=R_U(t,X(t,A(t,x)))=R_U(t,x)$. The profile equation contains its negative, so this cancellation also removes the phase-independent part of the old defect. The new residual is not the sum of the old residual and the hierarchy remainder.
euler02.approximate.parent-cancellation.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.momen: In label coordinates the parent source in the momentum equation is $R_U(t,X(t,a))$, independent of $s$. The hierarchy has been constructed with its negative as the level-two mean source. At the physical point $x=X(t,a)$ the two terms are literally equal with opposite signs; no estimate on $\|R_U\|$ is needed for their cancellation in (5.46).

euler02.approximate.divergence.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_divergence: The divergence identity follows from the same spatial chain rule as the momentum equation: $\operatorname{div}_x W^\natural=(\widetilde{\mathbf d}\cdot W)^\natural=0$. The divergence completion at each level, including the last, is what gives this identity for the finite sum.
euler02.approximate.divergence.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: Exact divergence is needed before the frequency cutoff. The identity $\operatorname{div}W^\natural=(\widetilde{\mathbf d}\cdot W)^\natural=0$ preserves the localization of the oscillatory part without applying a spatial projection to it. A Leray projection of an approximately solenoidal localized wave could produce a nonlocal oscillatory correction, whereas the later limit argument uses exact vanishing outside a small ball.

euler02.approximate.reflection.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_8_of: By oddness of $U$, the functions $X(t,-a)$ and $-X(t,a)$ solve the same trajectory equation with the same initial label. Hence the inverse labels at $x$ and $-x$ differ by a sign, as do the phases. The odd velocity reflection of the hierarchy therefore gives $V(t,-x)=-V(t,x)$. In particular $V(t,0)=0$; an even Fourier multiplier preserves this property for the truncated child.
euler02.approximate.reflection.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.oddExpansions_of: The reflection is $(a,s)\mapsto(-a,-s)$, rather than reflection in $s$ alone. The prescribed leading velocity is odd under this operation; the coefficients obtained from the odd parent have the required even parity. Reflecting the forced mean and transverse problems preserves their endpoint and zero-start data, so uniqueness transfers the parity to every level. The pressure profiles are even. After evaluation, $A(t,-x)=-A(t,x)$ gives oddness of the physical velocity.
euler02.approximate.reflection.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.inver: At $-x$ the inverse-flow label is $-A(t,x)$ and the evaluated phase is $-k_*\cdot A(t,x)$. The profile parity therefore passes directly to the physical field. The graph lemma assumes the inverse-flow and profile reflection identities, which are supplied by the parent symmetry and hierarchy respectively.

euler02.approximate.sup-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.graph_norm_le_wNorm: The evaluated phase is just one of the phases over which the profile supremum is taken. Thus at active times $|W_{\rm osc}^\natural(t,x)|\le\gamma(t)\|W_{\rm osc}\|_{[0],\gamma}$; there is no derivative or oscillatory integration estimate involved.
euler02.approximate.sup-proof.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The weighted order-zero profile bound and $\gamma\le1$ give (5.47) with no carrier loss. In item 5 of the induction $C_{\rm step}\le\lambda^{1/32}$, hence $\|O_j\|_\infty\le\lambda_j^{-39/32}\le\lambda_j^{-1}$. The derivative bound on the rest of the increment is established separately.

euler02.approximate.primary-two-jets.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.lemma_5_8_of_odd: Differentiating the switched primary field gives the term $\widetilde\chi'(A_1+C[A_1])$, with no remaining factor $\widetilde\chi$. It is consequently the bound on the unswitched completed primary field in the two-jet norm that enters (5.48); a small bound on the already-switched field would not control this term.
euler02.approximate.primary-two-jets.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The estimate concerns $A_1+C[A_1]$ before multiplication by the cutoff. At each active time the formal two-jet bound is proportional to $\gamma(t)\lambda^{-5/4}$ up to parent powers, with the derivatives taken in the rescaled variables $(a/\ell_*,s/h)$. For instance the mixed derivative is $\ell_*h\,\partial_a\partial_s$. This allows the switch residual to retain the small amplitude at the time of switching even after two spatial graph derivatives.

euler02.approximate.cutoff-derivative.TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.lemma_5_8_of_odd: At a fixed time $\widetilde\chi^{\prime}(t)$ commutes with spatial derivatives. The $m=1$ case of (5.45) costs $\lambda^3$, and the unswitched amplitude is bounded by $\lambda^{-5/4}\gamma(t)$ up to parent factors. This gives $\lambda^{7/4}|\widetilde\chi^{\prime}(t)|\gamma(t)$; enlarging $7/4$ to $2$ yields the second term in (5.48).
euler02.approximate.cutoff-derivative.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The product rule applied to the switched divergence-free primary field produces $\widetilde\chi^{\prime}(A_1+C[A_1])$. Multiplication by the scalar time cutoff preserves the divergence identity, but its time derivative enters the momentum equation. The linked equality identifies the resulting source before its norm is estimated.

Apply (5.45) with weight one to $R_P$ and with weight $\gamma$ to the unswitched primary field. The factor $\widetilde\chi'$ depends only on time, so the spatial derivatives do not act on it. The supremum in (5.48) is therefore of the product $|\widetilde\chi'|\gamma$ at the times of the switch.

r5-B-depth-remainder.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_8: The depth is measured in powers of the current frequency but the required smallness is measured at the next one. Indeed $P=6K_{j+1}$ turns $\lambda_j^{-2P/3}$ into $\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$. The early-amplitude estimate turns $e^{-L_j}$ into precisely the same next-frequency power. The remaining prefactors in (5.48) and in the bound for the switch derivative are absorbed in Section 7, leaving the residual small enough to serve as the next parent defect.

r5-B-pressure-sign-in-energy.TorusEuler.integral_endpointLabelEnergy_: The rank-one tensor $-c_{\mathbf a}F_h'\kappa\otimes\kappa$ has only one possibly nonzero eigenvalue, $-c_{\mathbf a}F_h'|\kappa|^2$. The sign condition on the seed gives $c_{\mathbf a}\ge0$; hence only the shallow negative part of $F_h'$ can contribute positively to the Hessian. In the next calculation $c_{\mathbf a}|\kappa|^2\le4\mathsf D^3\lambda^{1/4}$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, giving an upper bound $C\mathsf D^3\lambda^{-1/4}I$. Large negative curvature helps (4.7), whereas positive curvature must be paid for by the kinetic term. In passing to the next truncated parent one must also subtract $\nabla R_U$ in $H^\#=(D^2p_U-\nabla R_U)\circ X$.

r5-B-rank-one-after-activation.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_9: With the cutoff equal to one the leading increment is $\mathbf a\otimes\kappa$. In its moving frame it maps $E_1=\kappa/|\kappa|$ to $\sigma E_2$, $\sigma=|\mathbf a||\kappa|$, and kills $E_2,E_3$. The correction error in (5.50) and the truncation error in (5.56) must both be included in the next parent matrix.

euler02.pressure-flow.pressure-upper.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_9: The inequality in `Statement.lemma_5_9` is tested against every vector $z$: $z\cdot D_x^2\mathsf P^\natural z\le C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/4}|z|^2$, uniformly in time and position. In particular the size of a negative eigenvalue is unrestricted. This is the form used when adding the pressure increments in Section 7.
euler02.pressure-flow.pressure-upper.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_9: By (4.7), the displacement form is $\int(|\xi_t|^2-\xi\cdot H^\#\xi)\,dt$. An upper bound $H^\#\le\operatorname{Id}$ and $T\le1$ give a lower bound $\frac12\int|\xi_t|^2\,dt$ by (4.5). Thus Section 7 sums the upper pressure increments and estimates the current residual derivative separately; large negative pressure curvature is not an obstruction to this argument.
euler02.pressure-flow.pressure-upper.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi:
The pressure bound concerns the increment $\mathsf P^
atural=\mathsf p_1^
atural+\sum_{p=2}^P\mathsf p_p^
atural+\sum_{p=2}^P ar q_p^
atural$. Only the first Hessian is estimated with its sign. For either other Hessian $H$, $z\cdot Hz\le\|H\||z|^2$ permits its norm bound to be added. The linked assembly uses these component estimates for the selected expansion.
euler02.pressure-flow.pressure-upper.TorusEuler.exists_parent_genericLeading_: The center coupling $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a$ remains positive on the chosen label support by (5.19). This extension of the sign, rather than positivity only at $a=0$, is needed for the Hessian bound on the whole torus. The time cutoff is nonnegative, and outside the active support the primary pressure coefficient is zero.
euler02.pressure-flow.pressure-upper.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc: The seed is selected first from the parent and central wave data. For every admissible time cutoff the existence theorem then produces the corrected expansion, with the upper Hessian bound for its pressure increment. This order allows the switching interval to be chosen using the already determined amplification of the seed.

euler02.pressure-flow.central-gradient.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_9: In any orthonormal frame, (5.50) bounds the error in each entry of the gradient. After the switch has finished, in the wave's frame the leading increment has a single nonzero entry, $(2,1)=|\mathbf a||\kappa|$. The error estimate is what permits this matrix, rather than just its size, to be used in the next coupling calculation.
euler02.pressure-flow.central-gradient.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.centralReturnCl: The primary oscillation gives the tensor exactly. Its slow derivative at the center is multiplied by $F_h(0)=0$, while the phase derivative carries $F_h'(0)=1$. The error bound in the central-return theorem includes the primary curl correction, the higher oscillations and the mean, before truncation.
euler02.pressure-flow.central-gradient.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The primary gradient is known exactly; the rest of the central gradient is estimated by the profile bounds. The assembly leaves the inherited gradient untouched and uses (5.43) only to absorb the constant in the error. In particular the curl correction need not have zero gradient at the origin.
euler02.pressure-flow.central-gradient.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc: For the seed selected before the cutoff, the theorem constructs a hierarchy whose central gradient retains the switched rank-one increment. It simultaneously controls its pressure and deformation. The cutoff can thus be chosen from the seed's early amplitude without changing the desired central wave.

euler02.pressure-flow.leading-pressure.TorusEuler.oscillatoryPhasePressure_prim: The scalar oscillatory pressure is determined by the component of the momentum equation along $\kappa$. At level one, $\kappa\partial_s\mathsf p_1=-2P_\kappa(MV_1)$, since the transverse source is zero. Substituting $V_1=\widetilde\chi g\mathbf a F_h$ and integrating with zero phase mean gives $\mathsf p_1=-c_{\mathbf a}P_h$.

euler02.pressure-flow.coefficient.TorusEuler.wavePressureCoefficient: In the frame of the new wave, $E_{1,+}=\kappa/|\kappa|$ and $E_{2,+}=\mathbf a/|\mathbf a|$, the coupling is $\nu_+=E_{1,+}\cdot ME_{2,+}$. Thus at a nonzero seed $c_{\mathbf a}|\kappa|^2=2\widetilde\chi g\,\nu_+|\kappa||\mathbf a|$. The positivity of the first coupling needed in Section 6 is also what gives the favorable pressure sign here.

euler02.pressure-flow.primary-hessian.TorusEuler.wavePrimaryPressure_hessian: Write $c=c_{\mathbf a}\circ X^{-1}$ and $\theta=k_*\cdot X^{-1}$ locally on the supported cell. Differentiating $-cP_h(\theta)$ twice gives $-cF_h'\kappa\otimes\kappa-F_h(\nabla c\otimes\kappa+\kappa\otimes\nabla c+cD^2\theta)-P_hD^2c$. In (5.51) the first term is the only one that differentiates the phase profile twice; the other terms vanish in the affine case with spatially constant coefficient and normal.

euler02.pressure-flow.primary-coefficien.TorusEuler.wavePressureCoefficient_mul_n: We only require positivity of $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a$ where the seed is used. There $\widetilde\chi g\in[0,1]$ gives $0\le c_{\mathbf a}|\kappa|^2\le2|\kappa||M||\mathbf a|$. Off the active support the pressure is extended by zero; the rank-one coefficient is zero there, without a condition on any extension of the seed.

euler02.pressure-flow.primary-rank-one-u.TorusEuler.wavePrimaryPressure_leading_u: With $|\mathbf a|\le2\lambda^{-3/4}$, $|\kappa|\le\mathsf D^2\lambda$ and $|M|\le\mathsf D$, the direct norm bound for the primary tensor is $4\mathsf D^3\lambda^{1/4}$. Its upper quadratic-form bound instead gains the factor $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$ from the negative part of $F_h'$. This gives $C\mathsf D^3\lambda^{-1/4}$ even when the central negative curvature grows.

euler02.pressure-flow.primary-remainder.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.leadingHessianC: Each of the four remaining tensors in (5.51) contains at most one fast phase derivative; the others differentiate parent coefficients or the slow profile. Their total norm is bounded by $C\mathsf D^C\lambda^{3/2}\|\mathsf p_1\|_{[2]}\lesssim\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-3/4}$. The paper takes the primary pressure norm from (5.22); the linked proof reads the same estimate for the actual hierarchy from (5.34) at $p=1$.
euler02.pressure-flow.primary-remainder.TorusEuler.norm_wavePrimaryPressure_geom: The mixed tensors pay for one fast derivative, not two: $\mathbf d\partial_s\mathsf p_1$ costs $h^{-1}$ and its multiplication by $\kappa$ costs $O(\mathsf D^2\lambda)$. The term with $\mathbf d\kappa$ has the same frequency cost, since its derivative is slow. The purely slow Hessian costs only parent powers. Multiplying the largest cost $\lambda^{3/2}$ by $\lambda^{-9/4}$ gives the bound $\lambda^{-3/4}$.

euler02.pressure-flow.transverse-gradien.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans: Take the scalar product of (5.16) with $\kappa$. Differentiating $\kappa\cdot V_p=0$ gives $\kappa\cdot V_{p,t}=\kappa\cdot MV_p$, accounting for the second copy of $MV_p$. This yields the fast pressure gradient directly as $P_\kappa(f_p+f_p^S-2MV_p)$. At $p=2$ the bound is $O(\lambda^{-23/12})$ up to parent constants, whereas differentiating the pressure profile by (5.44) alone would give $O(\lambda^{-17/12})$.

euler02.pressure-flow.higher-gradient-bu.TorusEuler.higherPressureGradientBudget_: For $p\ge2$, (5.34) bounds $\lambda\mathsf p_p$, $V_p$ and the sources at the same level rate. The slow gradient of $\mathsf p_p$ gains $\lambda^{-1}$ relative to that rate, up to parent factors; the phase gradient is recovered directly from (5.16) at the level rate. Thus the sum of gradient profiles in $[1],\gamma$ has the level-two bound $C_{2,P}\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-23/12}$.

euler02.pressure-flow.higher-hessian.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.HigherHessianCl: `HigherHessianClaim` is the bound in (5.52) for the whole higher oscillatory pressure, with $p=1$ excluded. At level two the pressure scale is $\lambda^{-35/12}$. Paying twice for a physical derivative would give $\lambda^{1/12}$; recovering the first gradient from (5.16) saves a factor $\lambda^{1/2}$ and yields the required decay.
euler02.pressure-flow.higher-hessian.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.higherHessianCl: The first gradient is already known as a profile, $G_p=\mathbf d\mathsf p_p+P_\kappa(f_p+f_p^S-2MV_p)$. Hence $D_x^2\mathsf p_p^\natural=D_xG_p^\natural$, and (5.44) is applied only once. The level-two exponent changes by $3/2$, from $-23/12$ to $-5/12$; no favorable sign is required of these Hessians.
euler02.pressure-flow.higher-hessian.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: For the actual hierarchy, this theorem combines the pressure-gradient identity, the level estimates and the physical derivative cost to bound the higher oscillatory Hessian. The same result provides a separate bound for the mean Hessian using its equation. Both are norm bounds, unlike the one-sided primary estimate.

euler02.pressure-flow.mean-momentum.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi:
All mean equations are linearized about the same parent $U$, so they can be added before taking a divergence. If $B= ar W^
atural$, the sum has the form $B_t+U\cdot
abla B+B\cdot
abla U+
abla q=f$. The divergence of $B_t$ vanishes identically, so the pressure can be estimated without differentiating the endpoint solution in time.

euler02.pressure-flow.mean-poisson.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi:
For solenoidal $U$ and $B= ar W^
atural$, the divergence of $B_t$ vanishes and the two advection terms both give $\sum_{i,j}(\partial_iU_j)(\partial_jB_i)$. This yields the Poisson source $\operatorname{div} f-2\operatorname{tr}(
abla U
abla B)$. Its spatial mean vanishes, as each summand arises from a periodic divergence, so the constant mode of the inverse Laplacian is immaterial.

euler02.pressure-flow.hessian-multiplier.TorusEuler.pressureHessianMultiplier: For the Fourier mode $e^{2\pi i n\cdot x}$ with $n\ne0$, $D^2\Delta^{-1}$ has symbol $n\otimes n/|n|^2$, the projection onto the mode normal. The zero mode maps to zero. The bounded operator here acts on $C^{0,1/2}$; the regularity of the symbol, not simply its pointwise norm, is used to control the multiplier on this space.

euler02.pressure-flow.mean-hessian.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.MeanHessianClai: `MeanHessianClaim` is the norm estimate for the sum of the phase-independent pressures. Since the mean velocity and source in its Poisson equation are phase independent, their conversion to physical $C^{1,1/2}$ norms costs powers of $\mathsf D$ but no $\lambda^{3/2}$ factor. This leaves the rate $\lambda^{-5/2}$ from (5.37).
euler02.pressure-flow.mean-hessian.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.meanHessianClai: The mean source and mean velocity both have $C^{1,1/2}$ size $O(\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/2})$, and $\nabla U$ has a parent-polynomial $C^{0,1/2}$ bound. The right side of the Poisson equation thus has the same frequency decay in $C^{0,1/2}$. Applying $D^2\Delta^{-1}$ retains it, giving a Hessian norm bound without the fast derivative factor.
euler02.pressure-flow.mean-hessian.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The mean pressure is recovered here from its Eulerian Poisson equation, not by applying the fast phase equation. The summed mean velocity and force have small $C^{1,1/2}$ norms, so the source of $\Delta q$ is small in $C^{0,1/2}$. Applying the order-zero Hessian multiplier preserves this decay for the actual mean pressure.

euler-r2.pressure-flow.pressure-assembly.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_9_of: Combine the signed primary bound $C\mathsf D^3\lambda^{-1/4}\operatorname{Id}$ with the norm errors of rates $\lambda^{-3/4}$, $\lambda^{-5/12}$ and $\lambda^{-5/2}$. All these exponents are at most $-1/4$. In `lemma_5_9_of` the finitely many parent powers and depth constants are absorbed by $\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b=C_{\rm step}$; the central gradient claim is assembled separately.

euler02.pressure-flow.center-leading.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.gen: Since the odd parent fixes zero, evaluation there means $a=0$, $s=0$ at every time. In (3.1) the slow gradient of $\widetilde\chi g\mathbf a F_h$ carries the zero factor $F_h(0)$; the fast gradient carries $g(0)F_h'(0)=1$. This identifies the exact contribution of $V_1$ to (5.50).

euler02.pressure-flow.center-error-defin.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.centralReturnCl: All profiles have now been evaluated at the origin. Subtracting the inherited gradient and the exact primary tensor leaves $E_c$, the gradient of the nonprimary oscillations, including the curl correction of $V_1$, plus the mean gradient. Oddness makes the velocity zero at the origin, not these derivatives.
euler02.pressure-flow.center-error-defin.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The formula defines the error before truncation. The hierarchy controls the gradient of the entire nonprimary part rather than imposing a vanishing first jet on the corrections. After truncation the small Fourier-tail gradient must also be included in the matrix used at the next launch.

euler02.pressure-flow.remainder-profile.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.centralReturnCl: Although $V_1$ has the exact central gradient, its correction $C_2$ may contribute another gradient there. Thus the remainder starts with $C_2$ and $V_2$ and includes every further completion, through $C_{P+1}$. The mean is included separately in the central error.
euler02.pressure-flow.remainder-profile.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The indexing is $C_{p+1}=C[V_p]$. Thus $W_{\rm osc}-V_1$ contains $V_2,\ldots,V_P$ and $C_2,\ldots,C_{P+1}$. The last completion is part of the velocity although the expansion stops solving for new transverse oscillations at level $P$.

euler-r2.pressure-flow.central-remainder.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.centralReturnCl: The weakest decay among the nonprimary profiles is the bound for $V_2$, namely $\lambda^{-5/4-2/3}=\lambda^{-23/12}$. The bound for $C_2$ is already $\lambda^{-9/4}$, and later profiles have stronger decay. A finite sum of these bounds therefore controls $W_{\rm osc}-V_1$ at the level-two rate before evaluation.

euler02.pressure-flow.center-intermediat.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.centralReturnCl: For the remainder, the $[1]$ norm controls the slow gradient and $h\partial_s$ of the oscillation. The physical gradient in (3.1) therefore costs at most $O(\mathsf D^C\lambda^{3/2})$. At the level-two rate this leaves $\lambda^{-5/12}$, while the phase-independent mean needs no fast derivative. The difference between $-5/12$ and $-1/3$ is the frequency gain available for absorbing constants.
euler02.pressure-flow.center-intermediat.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: At the origin the derivative of the oscillatory remainder involves both its fixed-phase label derivative and its phase derivative multiplied by $\kappa$. The mean involves only the former. The linked bound combines these actual derivative estimates into a parent-polynomial multiple of $\lambda^{-5/12}$; the final coefficient absorption is separate.

The rate $\lambda^{-5/12}$ is written as $\lambda^{-1/3}\lambda^{-1/12}$. The second factor pays for the parent and depth constants through (5.43). This is why (5.50) has no step constant in front of its central error.

euler02.pressure-flow.center-smallness.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.centralReturnCl: The intermediate estimate is $C_{2,P}\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/12}$. Since $C_{2,P}\mathsf D^C\le C_{\rm step}$, the factor $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/12}$ in (5.43) is at most one. This leaves $\lambda^{-1/3}$, a bound with no parent-dependent prefactor, as required for the next frame comparison.
euler02.pressure-flow.center-smallness.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The parent constant is removed from the central error by reserving the factor $\lambda^{-1/12}$: $\lambda^{-5/12}=\lambda^{-1/3}\lambda^{-1/12}$. Condition (5.43) absorbs that factor uniformly on the slab. The pressure inequality has a different purpose and retains $C_{\rm step}$ in its bound.

euler02.pressure-flow.physical-from-labe.TorusEuler.ChildFlow.physicalTransition: Write $\mathcal A_t(a)=X(t,\cdot)^{-1}(Y(t,a))$. The original particle label of a child trajectory is $a$, but its current parent label is $\mathcal A_t(a)$. Differentiating in time, its label velocity is the pulled-back increment. The corresponding phase velocity is $k_*\cdot\dot{\mathcal A}_t$, whose large factor $k_*$ must be controlled before estimating the flow.

euler02.pressure-flow.perturbation-hypot.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_10: The statement allows any smooth solenoidal $v$ of the stated $C_tC^2$ size, not just a perturbation supported in the wave region. In particular the Fourier tail in Proposition 5.11 is admissible. It enters the lifted velocity only in the phase-independent part; the divergence-free assumption preserves the solenoidality of the full field $V+v$.
euler02.pressure-flow.perturbation-hypot.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The extra velocity contributes $(D_aX)^{-1}(v\circ X)$ to the mean pullback and nothing to its oscillation. Its first label derivative contains a derivative of the inverse deformation and a derivative of $v\circ X$. The $C^2$ size hypothesis is more than sufficient for this first jet. Solenoidality gives zero label divergence of this contribution by Piola.

euler02.pressure-flow.deformation.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_10: In the constant shear model $N=\mathbf a\otimes k$ with $\mathbf a\cdot k=0$, one has $N^2=0$ and the deformation is $I+tN$, with inverse $I-tN$. Bounding it by $\exp(t\|N\|)$ misses this property. Lemma 5.10 obtains a polynomial bound for the nonuniform corrected wave by estimating a flow in which label and phase are separate variables.
euler02.pressure-flow.deformation.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_10: The estimate is uniform in the admissible solenoidal perturbation $v$, so in Section 7 it applies directly to the truncated child, not merely to the untruncated approximation. Both the deformation and its inverse are among the parent bounds in (5.1). This is the reason for retaining polynomial control of both directions of the flow.
euler02.pressure-flow.deformation.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The bound is on both the forward deformation and the inverse matrix, not on $\nabla(V+v)$ or a small difference from the identity. The proof obtains bounded derivatives of a lifted flow and small derivatives of its label displacement in scaled variables. Restriction to the physical phase graph then introduces the growing factor in (5.53).
euler02.pressure-flow.deformation.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc: The selected wave and its hierarchy are fixed before the perturbation $v$ is specified. The bound holds for every admissible small solenoidal $v$, in particular the truncation tail chosen later. This order of quantifiers is needed to pass from the constructed expansion to its truncated successor.

euler02.pressure-flow.pullback.TorusEuler.ChildFlow.pullbackField: Let $G=(D_aX)^{-1}$. Differentiating $Y=X(t,\mathcal A)$ gives $D_aX\,\dot{\mathcal A}=(W^\natural+v)\circ Y$. The independent-phase version of this label velocity is $c=G(W+v\circ X)$. Since $G^Tk_*=\kappa$, the leading transverse wave contributes zero to $k_*\cdot c$; the correction and mean contribute the remaining phase velocity.

euler02.pressure-flow.twisted-periodicit.TorusEuler.ChildFlow.pullbackField_skewP: On the lattice extension $c_{\rm osc}(a+n,s)=c_{\rm osc}(a,s-k_*\cdot n)$. At $s=k_*\cdot(a+n)$ this becomes $c_{\rm osc}(a,k_*\cdot a)$, so restriction gives an ordinarily periodic label velocity. Because the shift is constant in the independent variables, the supremum bounds on the scaled derivatives extend unchanged from one cell to all cells.

euler02.pressure-flow.piola.TorusEuler.ChildFlow.slope_divergence_pu: At fixed $s$, Piola gives $\operatorname{div}_a(Gb)=\mathbf d\cdot b$ for $b=W+v\circ X$, since the parent flow preserves volume. Also $k_*\cdot G\partial_sb=\kappa\cdot\partial_sb$. Thus $\widetilde{\mathbf d}\cdot b=0$ becomes $(\nabla_a+k_*\partial_s)\cdot c=0$ with constant $k_*$. Both operations are performed before restricting to the phase graph.

euler02.pressure-flow.longitudinal-primi.TorusEuler.phaseOscillation_longitudinal: Average the Piola equation and subtract its mean: $\partial_s(k_*\cdot c_{\rm osc})=-\operatorname{div}_a c_{\rm osc}$. The zero mean of $c_{\rm osc}$ determines the integration constant. The resulting phase velocity costs one slow label derivative instead of multiplication by $|k_*|$. The phase-independent perturbation drops out of this identity; its longitudinal velocity is estimated separately.

euler02.pressure-flow.pullback-jets.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_10_of: The two oscillatory derivatives are needed because one is used by $\operatorname{div}_a c_{\rm osc}$ to bound the first derivative of the longitudinal primitive. For the mean, $|k_*|\|\bar c\|_{[1]}\lesssim\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-3/2}$ is enough. The linked proof uses this order-one mean bound, rather than requiring the order-two mean estimate displayed here.
euler02.pressure-flow.pullback-jets.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: For $v=0$, the linked result gives the order-two oscillatory and order-one mean jets of the pullback at rates $\lambda^{-5/4}$ and $\lambda^{-5/2}$. These are the orders needed in the lifted gradient estimate. The stronger order-two mean bound in the printed display is not a conclusion of this particular theorem.

The deformation theorem adds the solenoidal $v$ to the pullback. Its first derivative is controlled at the mean scale, and the longitudinal primitive uses the second derivative only of the oscillation. The linked proof therefore does not require the displayed order-two mean bound.

euler02.pressure-flow.scaled-field.TorusEuler.ChildFlow.scaledField: In $(y,z)=(a/\ell_*,s/h)$ the velocities are $(c/\ell_*,k_*\cdot c/h)$ evaluated at $(\ell_*y,hz)$. Thus the input derivatives are $\ell_*\partial_a$ and $h\partial_s$, whereas the two output components are divided by $\ell_*$ and $h$ respectively. The large carrier would appear in the second row unless $k_*\cdot c$ were controlled by the longitudinal identity.

euler02.pressure-flow.scaled-gradient.TorusEuler.child_flow_scaled_gradient_le: The label row costs $\ell_*^{-1}\|c\|_{[1]}\lesssim\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/4}$. The phase row costs $h^{-1}\|k_*\cdot c\|_{[1]}\lesssim\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-3/4}$. Replacing the latter longitudinal bound by $|k_*|\|c\|_{[1]}$ would give a bound of order $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{1/4}$ instead, putting the large shear back into Gronwall’s exponent.

euler02.pressure-flow.gradient-smallness.TorusEuler.child_flow_scaled_gradient_sm: Since $\lambda\ge1$, $\lambda^{-3/4}\le\lambda^{-1/12}$. The hypothesis $\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$ and $b\ge C$ give $C_{2,P}\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-3/4}\le C_{2,P}/\Gamma_P$. Choosing $\Gamma_P$ large makes the lifted gradient small independently of the parent and frequency.

euler02.pressure-flow.scaled-gronwall.TorusEuler.scaledFlow_fderiv_and_displac: For a bound $L$ on the scaled gradient, integration between any two times $t_1,t_2$ gives the flow derivative bound $\exp(L|t_2-t_1|)$. The same estimate applies when $t_2<t_1$, so the inverse is controlled without estimating a matrix inverse from the forward bound. Here $LT\le1/2$ gives a bound by two.

euler02.pressure-flow.displacement.TorusEuler.scaledFlow_fderiv_and_displac: Integrating $\dot\eta_a=c(t,\mathscr L_t(a,s))$ and differentiating with respect to the scaled initial variables costs at most the flow derivative bound two times the scaled derivative of $c$. Therefore $h|\partial_s\eta_a|+\ell_*|\partial_a\eta_a|$ retains the small rate $\lambda^{-5/4}$, up to parent factors. The identical integration from $t$ back to zero bounds the inverse displacement.

euler02.pressure-flow.invariant-graph.TorusEuler.ChildFlow.phaseDefect_transit: For the independent variables, $d(s-k_*\cdot a)/dt=k_*\cdot c-k_*\cdot c=0$. Thus every affine graph $s=k_*\cdot a+s_0$ is invariant (with $s$ taken modulo one if desired). The physical flow uses the graph $s_0=0$, and invariance for the backward flow justifies restricting its inverse to the same graph.

euler02.pressure-flow.label-map.TorusEuler.ChildFlow.labelTransition: Restricting the lifted map to the graph means starting from $(a,k_*\cdot a)$ and retaining its first component. The second component then equals $k_*\cdot\mathcal A_t(a)$. Applying the inverse lifted map to the same graph supplies the inverse label map, which is why the backward displacement estimate is also needed.

euler02.pressure-flow.graph-derivative.TorusEuler.ChildFlow.graphDerivative_app: The slow part $\partial_a\eta_a$ has size $O(\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/4})$, while $|\partial_s\eta_a|\lesssim\mathsf D^C h^{-1}\lambda^{-5/4}=\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-3/4}$. The graph derivative multiplies the latter by $k_*$, giving a rank-one term of size $O(\mathsf D^C\lambda^{1/4})$. A tangent variation with $k_*\cdot v=0$ sees only the small slow part.

euler02.pressure-flow.parent-product.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_10_of: The graph restriction gives $\|D\mathcal A_t^{\pm1}-I\|\lesssim\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/4}(\ell_*^{-1}+|k_*|/h)\lesssim\mathsf D^C\lambda^{1/4}$, with depth-dependent constants. Adding the identity and multiplying by the corresponding parent deformation bound costs another factor $\mathsf D$. The choice of $C_{\rm step}$ includes these constants for both the forward and inverse maps.
euler02.pressure-flow.parent-product.TorusEuler.ChildFlow.physicalTransition_: At $x=Y(t,a)$ the inverse deformation is $D_xY^{-1}(t,x)=D\mathcal A_t^{-1}(\mathcal A_t(a))(D_aX(t,\mathcal A_t(a)))^{-1}$. Both factors have already been bounded. In particular the inverse bound is obtained from the backward lifted flow, without using a bound on a determinant to estimate the inverse of the forward graph derivative.

euler02.truncation.pressure-residual-sou.TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalfNorm_cutoffP: For the approximate pair, $\Delta\Pi=-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla V)^2)+\operatorname{div}R_V$. If one retained $V$ without truncation but replaced $\Pi$ by the Poisson pressure of $V$, the Hessian would change by $-D^2\Delta^{-1}\operatorname{div}R_V$. Thus the pressure-recovery error has a residual term even when the velocity tail is zero.

euler02.truncation.fields-and-budget.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: To bound $R_u$ in $C^{1,1/2}$ one first bounds its quadratic tensors in $C^{2,1/2}$, before applying the divergence. The cutoff estimate (B.2) at that order gives $\Lambda^{2-P}$ from a $C^{P,1/2}$ norm. The product has two velocity factors, hence the budget $\varepsilon_\Lambda=\Lambda^{2-P}(1+\|V\|_{C_tC^{P,1/2}})^2$. It also covers the linear velocity tail.
euler02.truncation.fields-and-budget.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage: The stage fixes $u=S_\Lambda V$ and obtains its mean-zero Poisson pressure. Its definition records the filtered velocity and the projected momentum identity for that same velocity. The constants controlling the error of the stage occur in the estimates proved afterward.
euler02.truncation.fields-and-budget.TorusEuler.paperProposition511_physicalC: `paperProposition511_physicalCutoff` separates the physical truncation from the construction of the expansion. It takes the approximate momentum identity, smooth periodic $V,R_V$, odd solenoidal $V$, and an upper bound on $D^2(\Pi-p_U)$ as inputs. Its constants are chosen from the cutoff symbol (and, for the tail, $P$) before choosing the fields or $\Lambda$. No hierarchy or wave frequency occurs in its hypotheses.

euler02.truncation.poisson-pressure.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsTruncation: The recovered pressure is generally not $S_\Lambda\Pi$. In fact $\Delta S_\Lambda\Pi=S_\Lambda\operatorname{div}R_V-S_\Lambda\operatorname{tr}((\nabla V)^2)$, while $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla S_\Lambda V)^2)$. The two discrepancies, the residual divergence and the change of the quadratic source, are precisely the terms estimated in the pressure-difference equation.
euler02.truncation.poisson-pressure.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: For the cutoff pair, $\operatorname{div}R_u=\operatorname{div}u_t+\operatorname{tr}((\nabla u)^2)+\Delta p=0$. This uses the newly recovered pressure. For $(V,\Pi)$ the corresponding divergence is $\operatorname{div}R_V$, which need not vanish and appears explicitly in the pressure-difference equation.
euler02.truncation.poisson-pressure.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage: The stage gives the Poisson identity for its new pressure and the projected formula for its new momentum defect. In estimating $p-\Pi$ use the former; in estimating $R_u$ use the latter. In particular no bound on the high derivatives of the approximate pressure $\Pi$ is needed in the cutoff budget.
euler02.truncation.poisson-pressure.TorusEuler.nonempty_truncatedChildStage: The cutoff velocity has finitely many smooth time-dependent Fourier coefficients. Its quadratic pressure source has band at most $4\Lambda$ and integral zero. Inverting the Laplacian on that finite band, with zero constant coefficient, constructs a pressure smooth on the entire slab. This does not rely on solving Euler for the cutoff velocity.
euler02.truncation.poisson-pressure.TorusEuler.periodicPoissonPressure_uniqu: The difference of two recovered pressures is periodic, harmonic and has zero mean. Integrating its equation against the difference gives zero gradient; the zero mean then gives zero difference. Thus the pressure determined by `IsTruncation` is unique, not an additional choice affecting the residual.

euler02.truncation.residual-definition.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: The residual that is passed on is the momentum of the filtered velocity with its recovered pressure. It is solenoidal, so it takes the form $u_t+\mathbb P\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)$. The earlier residual $R_V$ is not assumed solenoidal, and its filtered contribution to the new residual must also be projected.
euler02.truncation.residual-definition.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.residual: The cutoff does not preserve the momentum equation, even when $R_V=0$: $u\otimes u$ need not equal $S_\Lambda(V\otimes V)$. The actual new defect in `residual` is the one for the recovered pressure. By (5.58) its two sources are the projected filtered defect $\mathbb P S_\Lambda R_V$ and the projected divergence of this tensor difference.

euler02.truncation.velocity-properties.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: An even scalar Fourier multiplier commutes with reflection and with differentiation, preserving oddness and divergence freedom. Its support restricts the new velocity to $2\Lambda$. Smoothness in time follows from the finite number of retained smooth Fourier coefficients.
euler02.truncation.velocity-properties.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_11: The velocity produced by the cutoff is the next parent, with frequencies at most $2\Lambda$. In particular the support bound in (5.1) will be available with any $\mathsf D\ge\Lambda$. Bounds on the next gradient and deformation still require the estimates in the induction; the support bound by itself gives neither.
euler02.truncation.velocity-properties.TorusEuler.nonempty_truncatedChildStage: Existence of the stage uses the finite support and evenness of the symbol to obtain a smooth odd divergence-free velocity and a Poisson pressure. The condition that the symbol equals one on the unit ball is used for quantitative approximation by $S_\Lambda$, not for preservation of these qualitative properties.
euler02.truncation.velocity-properties.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage: For this stage the velocity is exactly the periodic lift of $S_\Lambda V$. Thus any estimate of $S_\Lambda V-V$ is an estimate of the change actually made to the velocity, rather than of a different band-limited approximation. The stage stores the qualitative properties of this same lift.

euler02.truncation.residual-properties.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: For every time, $u$ has band $2\Lambda$. Its time derivative has that same band, and $\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)$ has band $4\Lambda$. The Leray projection preserves each frequency and reflection parity, so their projected sum is odd, solenoidal and has band $4\Lambda$. Hence Bernstein will control the gradient of the next residual using only its supremum.
euler02.truncation.residual-properties.TorusEuler.paperProposition511_physicalC: At the next step the cutoff supplies velocity and residual bands $2\Lambda$ and $4\Lambda$. A parent parameter $\mathsf D\ge\Lambda$ therefore covers both. The gradient and deformation must also be checked; the band alone does not bound the deformation without additional information on the flow.

euler02.truncation.error-bounds.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: The $C_tC^{2,1/2}$ bound for $u-V$ is used in the flow estimate of Lemma 5.10 and the central-gradient estimate. The two terms in the second bound control the new defect and the change in pressure curvature. In the formal statement these last norms are bounded at two independently chosen times, which permits taking the two suprema separately as in (5.56).
euler02.truncation.error-bounds.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_11_: The proof constructs the cutoff pair, uses the projected identity to estimate its residual, and uses the difference of the Poisson equations to estimate its pressure. It then adds the pressure-Hessian error to the known upper bound on the approximate pressure increment. The finite expansion is used only through the properties already proved for its physical fields.
euler02.truncation.error-bounds.TorusEuler.paperProposition511_physicalC: The cutoff acts on the defect already present in $V$ by a uniformly bounded operator, not by a small factor. The other contribution comes from the quadratic cutoff error, bounded by $C_{2,P}\varepsilon_\Lambda$. Increasing $\Lambda$ reduces the latter when $P>2$; the former must be controlled separately by the depth and by the amplitude during switching. Section 7 does both at the scale of the next frequency.

euler02.truncation.pressure-upper.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: Add $D^2(p-\Pi)$, bounded in norm by (5.56), to $D^2(\Pi-p_U)$, bounded above by Lemma 5.9. The large negative part of the latter need not be estimated. Keeping this distinction lets the pressure bound survive the cutoff even when the central shear of the new wave is large.
euler02.truncation.pressure-upper.TorusEuler.paperProposition511_physicalC: The physical estimate takes the upper bound $D^2(\Pi-p_U)\le sI$ as input. If the change in the pressure Hessian has norm at most $e$, the output is $D^2(p-p_U)\le(s+e)I$. This is uniform in space and time. The hierarchy supplies $s=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b\lambda^{-1/4}$ in the paper application.

euler02.truncation.advection-divergence.TorusEuler.divergence_advection_eq_trace:
Expanding the divergence of $u\cdot
abla u$ gives $\sum_{i,j}\partial_i u_j\partial_j u_i+u\cdot
abla(\operatorname{div}u)$. Incompressibility leaves $\operatorname{tr}((
abla u)^2)$, which is not $|
abla u|^2$. Its integral vanishes because it is the divergence of a periodic vector field; this is why it is an admissible Poisson source.

euler02.truncation.projected-residual.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage: The formula $R_u=u_t+\mathbb P\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)$ is valid for the actual recovered pressure, because the Poisson equation implies $\operatorname{div}R_u=0$. It allows the residual estimate to use only $u,V,R_V$ and the cutoff, without first estimating the pressure difference.
euler02.truncation.projected-residual.TorusEuler.nonempty_truncatedChildStage: The finite Fourier band allows the recovered pressure to be constructed at each time, and the actual projected momentum identity holds for that pressure. In the formal stage the time derivative in $R_u$ is the derivative within $[0,T]$, so the identity is also valid at the two endpoints. No evolution equation for the pressure is needed.

euler02.truncation.residual-identity.TorusEuler.projected_residual_of_cutoff: Since the cutoff commutes with the time derivative and the divergence, filter the momentum equation for $V$ and apply $\mathbb P$ to obtain $u_t+\mathbb P\operatorname{div}S_\Lambda(V\otimes V)=\mathbb P S_\Lambda R_V$. Subtract from the equation defining $R_u$; the time derivatives cancel. In the remaining tensor insert and subtract $V\otimes u$ and $V\otimes V$. This gives $(u-V)\otimes u+V\otimes(u-V)+(I-S_\Lambda)(V\otimes V)$, the three terms of (5.58).

euler-r2.truncation.quadratic-tensor-cos.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_cutoffBo: All three tensors in (5.58) need a bound of order two, but only one factor in each mixed product needs to be small. The tail $v_\Lambda$ gives $\Lambda^{2-P}\|V\|_{C^{P,1/2}}$, and $u$ and $V$ are bounded by $C\|V\|_{C^{P,1/2}}$. For the last tensor apply the tail estimate directly to $V\otimes V$, whose high norm is quadratic in the same norm of $V$. Thus there is one tail factor, not two, in the common budget.

euler02.truncation.velocity-tail.TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalfNorm_cutoffV: The convolution kernel $K_\Lambda(y)=\Lambda^3\check\psi(\Lambda y)$ has integral one and zero moments of every positive order, since $\psi$ is constant near zero. For $P>s$ subtract the Taylor polynomial of $V(x-y)$ through degree $P-s-1$. The remainder in $C^{s,1/2}$ costs $|y|^{P-s}\|V\|_{C^{P,1/2}}$, including the spatial increments of the derivatives. Integrating this against $|K_\Lambda|$ gives $\Lambda^{s-P}$. For $P=s$ the uniform convolution bound suffices.

euler02.truncation.holder-product.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_59: The estimate holds for any continuous bilinear product, with a constant depending on its operator norm. In particular it applies to tensor products of velocities and to products of their gradient matrices. Taking $m=2$ before the divergence gives the $C^{1,1/2}$ residual bound.
euler02.truncation.holder-product.TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_59: One uses (5.59) at order two for the tensor terms of (5.58), because a divergence follows the product. In the pressure equation the products are of first derivatives of the velocities and the Hessian is recovered by an operator of order zero; there the product estimate at order zero suffices.
euler02.truncation.holder-product.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_59: For a bilinear product $B$, split its spatial increment as $B(f(x)-f(y),g(x))+B(f(y),g(x)-g(y))$. Dividing by the half-power of the distance bounds the seminorm by a supremum times a seminorm in each term. Leibniz' rule then proves the estimate at order $m$ without derivative loss. The formal proof gives the constant $3(m+1)2^m\|B\|$.
euler02.truncation.holder-product.TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_bilinear: At order two the first mixed tensor in (5.58) is bounded by $C\|v_\Lambda\|_{C^{2,1/2}}\|u\|_{C^{2,1/2}}$. Uniform boundedness of $S_\Lambda$ controls the second factor by the norm of $V$. The other mixed tensor has the analogous bound. One tail factor is sufficient; neither $u$ nor $V$ is required to be small in that norm.

euler-r2.truncation.tensor-estimate.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.truncatedParent: In the last tensor of (5.58) the cutoff acts after multiplication. First bound $\|V\otimes V\|_{C^{P,1/2}}$ by $C_P\|V\|_{C^{P,1/2}}^2$, then apply (B.2) to the tensor itself with $s=2$. This produces the same tail factor as in the mixed terms. The divergence loses one derivative and the Leray projection is bounded on the remaining Hölder space.

euler02.truncation.pressure-poisson-diff.TorusEuler.divergence_gradient_cutoffPre:
Put $A=
abla u$, $B=
abla V$ and $D=
abla v_\Lambda=A-B$. The difference of the two Poisson equations is $\Delta(p-\Pi)=-\operatorname{tr}(DB+AD)-\operatorname{div}R_V$. This expansion of $A^2-B^2$ as $DB+AD$ does not assume that the matrices commute. It isolates a single small gradient of the tail in each product and a separate source from the approximate momentum defect.

euler02.truncation.pressure-error-estima.TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalfNorm_cutoffP: Apply $D^2\Delta^{-1}$ to the preceding Poisson source. On nonzero modes its symbol is $\xi\otimes\xi/|\xi|^2$; the constant mode of the source vanishes. The operator is bounded on $C^{0,1/2}$, not generally on $L^\infty$. Thus the quadratic terms need only $\|v_\Lambda\|_{C^{1,1/2}}(\|u\|_{C^{1,1/2}}+\|V\|_{C^{1,1/2}})$, and the remaining term needs $\|R_V\|_{C^{1,1/2}}$. No high norm of $\Pi$ is required.

euler02.truncation.final-upper-bound.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_11_: Proposition 5.11 propagates an upper bound on the pressure increment, not yet the complete hypothesis (5.2). The latter contains $-\nabla R_u$ as well. To apply the next endpoint inverse, Section 7 sums the pressure increments and uses the $4\Lambda$ band of the new residual to bound $\nabla R_u$ by $C\Lambda\|R_u\|_\infty$. Both the sign of the pressure estimate and the new residual band are needed.
euler02.truncation.final-upper-bound.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.pressureH: If $D^2(\Pi-p_U)\le sI$ and $\|D^2(p-\Pi)\|_\infty\le e$, evaluate both on the same vector $v$. Adding gives $v\cdot D^2(p-p_U)v\le(s+e)|v|^2$. This is the stage lemma; an absolute norm bound on $D^2(\Pi-p_U)$ would be stronger than needed.
euler02.truncation.final-upper-bound.TorusEuler.paperProposition511_physicalC: For the next application, write $\mu=\lambda_{j-1}$ and $\lambda=\lambda_j$. The initial shear has constant pressure, and the upper bounds on subsequent pressure increments sum to at most $2/N$. The parent residual has band $4\mu^5$ and norm at most $\lambda^{-3}$; Bernstein gives $\|\nabla R_U\|_\infty\le C\mu^5\lambda^{-3}$. Consequently $D^2p_U-\nabla R_U\le(2/N+C\mu^5\lambda^{-3})I\le I$ for large $N$, as required by the next mean inverse.

r2-s6-rho-hypothesis.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_6_1: The assumption $0<\rho\le1$ makes the two initial couplings positive and gives $|B_\rho|\le4\pi$. The first-wave estimate uses the latter bound; the strict positivity of $\rho$ is needed to use the ratio as the input parameter for wave $2$.

e03-s6-shear-formulas.TorusEuler.stationaryShear: The shear transports particles parallel to $e_1+\rho e_3$, with speed depending only on their second coordinate. Its gradient maps $e_2$ to $2\pi\cos(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$ and annihilates the plane perpendicular to $e_2$. This is the simple rank-one gradient needed to initialize the couplings.
e03-s6-shear-formulas.TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient: The matrix in (6.1) is the gradient at zero. At a general point it is multiplied by $\cos(2\pi x_2)$. In particular $DU_0(x)v=2\pi\cos(2\pi x_2)v_2(e_1+\rho e_3)$, so its image is contained in its kernel.

e03-s6-shear-regularity.TorusEuler.stationaryShear_base_T1: Oddness follows from the sine, and divergence vanishes since the only spatial dependence is on $x_2$ but the second velocity component is zero.
