The base-stage theorem also places this smooth, time-independent field in the required Fourier band, so it supplies (T1) at $j=0$.

e03-s6-shear-fourier.TorusEuler.stationaryShear_mFourierCoeff: Writing the sine as $(e^{2\pi i x_2}-e^{-2\pi i x_2})/(2i)$ shows why only the modes $\pm e_2$ occur. Neither coefficient vanishes, even at $\rho=0$, because the first component of the shear direction is one.

e03-s6-no-second-component.TorusEuler.stationaryShear_second: The second component of $U_0$ vanishes, so particles move in planes of constant $x_2$. As the shear depends only on $x_2$, it is constant on each of these trajectories. This gives both zero self-advection and the explicit flow (6.2).

e03-s6-no-advection.TorusEuler.stationaryShear_advection: For any vector $v$, $DU_0(x)v=\cos(2\pi x_2)B_\rho v$. Taking $v=U_0(x)$ gives zero, since its second component vanishes. Thus the nonlinear term is zero without any approximation.

e03-s6-zero-pressure-residual.TorusEuler.isEulerSolution_stationaryShe: Here $\partial_tU_0=0$ and $U_0\cdot\nabla U_0=0$. Also $DU_0(x)$ is a scalar multiple of the square-zero matrix $B_\rho$, so the pressure Poisson equation has zero right-hand side. The zero-mean pressure is therefore zero and so is the residual used in (T2).

e03-s6-fixed-second-coordinate.TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_second: The equation for the second particle coordinate is $\dot X_{0,2}=0$. Hence the velocity of each particle remains its initial velocity, and integration gives the affine-in-time trajectory in (6.2).

e03-s6-flow-deformation.TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow: Since the second particle coordinate stays equal to $a_2$, the velocity along the trajectory is $U_0(a)$ for every time. Integration gives $X_0(t,a)=a+tU_0(a)$; subtracting the same shear displacement gives the inverse.
e03-s6-flow-deformation.TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_jacobians: Differentiating in $a$ gives $D_aX_0=I+cB_\rho$, where $c=t\cos(2\pi a_2)$. As $B_\rho^2=0$, $(I+cB_\rho)^{-1}=I-cB_\rho$. There is no small-time restriction on this algebraic inverse; the short-time restriction of Lemma 6.1 enters the wave estimates.

e03-s6-square-zero.TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_sq: The factor $e_2\cdot(e_1+\rho e_3)=0$ gives $B_\rho^2=0$. Thus $(I+cB_\rho)(I-cB_\rho)=I$ for every $c$, giving (6.2) without an inverse-series estimate.

e03-s6-origin-fixed.TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_origin: The trajectory from label zero has zero sine term for every time. The gradient sampled by the central wave is therefore the constant matrix $B_\rho$, rather than the gradient along a moving noncentral trajectory.

e03-s6-gradient-bound.TorusEuler.norm_stationaryShearGradient_: The operator norm of this rank-one map is $2\pi\sqrt{1+\rho^2}$, since $|e_2|=1$. For $|\rho|\le1$ it is at most $4\pi$, which gives a uniform short-time condition in Lemma 6.1.

e03-s6-first-wave-choice.TorusEuler.FirstWaveOrigin: At $t_0=0$ the label flow is the identity, so $k_*=\lambda e_1$ is also the physical normal at launch. The amplitude along $e_2$ gives the central frame $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$. The first wave is not switched on from zero; its unit cutoff makes its central shear available at the launch of wave two.

e03-s6-first-wave-normalization.TorusEuler.firstWaveOrigin_exists: For the specified nonzero normal the seed equation is linear. A solution with initial value $e_2$ stays nonzero and transverse; let $A$ be the maximum of its length on the closed interval. Multiplying that solution by $\lambda^{-3/4}/A$ gives the prescribed peak without changing its frame or couplings.
e03-s6-first-wave-normalization.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveOrig: Solve the central equation with a positive multiple of $e_2$ at time zero. Since the homogeneous equation preserves transversality and a nonzero solution cannot meet zero, its maximum length on $[0,T]$ is positive. This justifies the positive rescaling before solving for the other labels.

e03-s6-initial-projection.TorusEuler.FirstWaveOrigin.initial_proje: The transported normal is $\kappa=(D_aX_0)^{-T}k_*$. At time zero $D_aX_0=I$ everywhere and $k_*=\lambda e_1$, so the projection $I-P_\kappa$ leaves the central initial direction $e_2$ unchanged at every label. This simplification is special to launch at zero; once the shear has acted, $\kappa(t,a)=\lambda(e_1-2\pi t\cos(2\pi a_2)e_2)$ is no longer spatially constant.

e03-s6-initial-couplings.TorusEuler.FirstWaveOrigin.initial_coupl: The two initial directions give $E_1=e_1$, $E_2=e_2$ and $E_3=e_1\times e_2=e_3$. Inserting $B_\rho e_2=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)$ gives the couplings. Their ratio is $\rho$ independently of the positive amplitude normalization.

e03-s6-lemma61-origin.TorusEuler.paperLemma61_firstWave: The first wave satisfies (5.5) with room to spare: the relative propagation constant is at most $2$, and the first coupling is at least $\pi$. The same $\mathsf D\ge2$ therefore bounds the first quantity and the reciprocal of the second. The subsequent wave will require a much larger $\mathsf D$, because its seed undergoes both amplification and decay on the comparison interval.
e03-s6-lemma61-origin.TorusEuler.paperLemma61_exists_firstWave: The small-time restriction $T|B_\rho|\le1/8$ controls the deformation of the frame and the relative growth of all transverse solutions. It is used only for this initial wave. The later waves require a long normalized interval, where the polynomial comparison rather than this short-time argument is used.
e03-s6-lemma61-origin.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_6_1: The two estimates in (5.5) have separate uses. The relative propagator bound controls the inhomogeneous transverse equations in the expansion. The lower bound on $\nu$ gives $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a=|\kappa||\mathbf a|\nu>0$ at the center, which is then extended to the envelope for the pressure estimate.
e03-s6-lemma61-origin.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_6_1: The first wave needs only comparable lengths on a short interval. The reflection $I-2P_\kappa$ has norm one, so the logarithmic derivative of the length of any nonzero solution has absolute value at most $|B_\rho|$. This gives the relative bound of (5.5) without using the growing-mode analysis.

e03-s6-lemma61-strength.TorusEuler.FirstWaveOrigin.initial_stren: Choose a time attaining the maximum $\lambda^{-3/4}$. The bound on $|\partial_t\log|\mathbf a||$ gives $|\mathbf a(0,0)|\ge e^{-T|B_\rho|}\lambda^{-3/4}$. The initial normal has length $\lambda$, so the strength is at least $e^{-1/8}\lambda^{1/4}\ge\lambda^{1/4}/2$.
e03-s6-lemma61-strength.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_6_1: If the length attains its prescribed maximum at $t_*$, the logarithmic bound gives $|\mathbf a(0,0)|\ge e^{-t_*|B_\rho|}\lambda^{-3/4}$. The factor $|\kappa(0,0)|=\lambda$ then gives the strength lower bound, while the maximum itself gives the upper bound.
e03-s6-lemma61-strength.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_6_1: At zero the leading velocity gradient has size $\lambda|\mathbf a(0,0)|$, since $F_h'(0)=1$. In contrast, the leading velocity has size at most $C\lambda^{-3/4}h=C\lambda^{-5/4}$. The steep slope of $F_h$ thus produces a shear of order $\lambda^{1/4}$ from a small velocity increment.

e03-s6-weighted-propagation.TorusEuler.FirstWaveOrigin.weighted_forw: For a nonzero transverse solution $\mathbf b$, reflection by $I-2P_\kappa$ preserves length, giving $|\partial_t\log|\mathbf b||\le|B_\rho|$. Apply the upper exponential estimate to $\mathbf b$ and the lower one to $\gamma$; their quotient costs at most $e^{2T|B_\rho|}\le2$. The zero solution satisfies the same inequality directly.
e03-s6-weighted-propagation.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_6_1_of: For $\mathbf b\ne0$, $\partial_t\log(|\mathbf b|/\gamma)$ is the difference of two logarithmic length derivatives and is at most $2|B_\rho|$. Integration gives $e^{2(t-t')|B_\rho|}\le e^{1/4}<2$. The use of a quotient makes this an estimate for arbitrary transverse data at an intermediate time $t'$, as required when solving a forced correction equation.

r2-s6-frame-control.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_6_1_of: Because $B_\rho$ is constant, differentiating $\nu=E_1\cdot B_\rho E_2$ gives only the two frame-derivative terms. Each has magnitude at most $|B_\rho|^2$. The short-time condition ensures that their integrated contribution cannot exhaust the initial coupling $2\pi$.
r2-s6-frame-control.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.first_couplin: The normalized vector derivatives have norm at most $|B_\rho|$. The product rule gives $|\nu(t)-\nu(0)|\le2t|B_\rho|^2$, which is at most $\pi$ because $t|B_\rho|\le1/8$ and $|B_\rho|\le4\pi$. This proves the lower bound exported by the declaration.

e03-s6-positive-first-coupling.TorusEuler.FirstWaveOrigin.first_couplin: The loss from $2\pi$ is at most $2t|B_\rho|^2\le |B_\rho|/4\le\pi$. The resulting $\nu\ge\pi$ is stronger than the $\mathsf D^{-1}$ needed in (5.5).

e03-s6-parent-gradient-splitting.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: Here $\mathbf a_p\otimes\kappa_p=\sigma_pE_2\otimes E_1$ is the leading gradient left by the preceding wave. Its own frame evolves with $B=\nabla U_{j-2}(t,0)$, whereas the new normal and seed evolve with $M=\nabla U_{j-1}(t,0)$. The preceding shear can consequently be large without rotating its own frame at that large rate. The term $E_c$ accounts for the higher profiles, mean and truncation, which do not belong to the preceding central wave equations.

e03-s6-preceding-wave-equations.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: The frame and strength of the preceding wave are determined by the wave equations over the older gradient $B$. Substituting its own rank-one shear into those equations would describe a different evolution. The successor solves over the full parent gradient $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes\kappa_p+E_c$.

e03-s6-frozen-strength.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: Write $\sigma_p(t)=|\mathbf a_p(t)||\kappa_p(t)|$, and set $\sigma=\sigma_p(t_0)$. The two length equations give $(\log\sigma_p)'=-B_{11}-B_{22}=B_{33}$, using $\operatorname{tr}B=0$. In particular $e^{-\|B\|_\infty(t-t_0)}\le\sigma_p(t)/\sigma\le e^{\|B\|_\infty(t-t_0)}$. The frozen strength is a useful approximation on a short interval even when it is itself large.

e03-s6-positive-frozen-couplings.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: In the reference covector equations the term $-\varepsilon\zeta_3$ turns the new wave vector away from $E_3$, with $\varepsilon=\eta/\nu$. A smaller positive ratio delays the turning and permits a larger amplification of the growing mode. The physical growth time is set independently by $r^{-1}=(2\sigma\nu)^{-1/2}$. Thus the crossing must supply both a small ratio and a large strength; a small ratio alone gives no short physical time scale.

e03-s6-rate.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl:
With zero tilt in the ideal rotating frame the transverse amplitude components satisfy $\dot a_1=-2
u a_2$, $\dot a_2=-(\sigma-
u)a_1$. Eliminating $a_1$ gives $\ddot a_2=2
u(\sigma-
u)a_2$. Thus $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$ is the limiting growth rate when $
u/\sigma$ is small, and $r^{-1}$ is the time unit used in the comparison.

e03-s6-normalized-shear.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: The factors $S^{-1}$ in (2.3) occur in complementary coordinates of $k$ and $\mathbf a$, so that $k\cdot\mathbf a=(\lambda/S)\zeta\cdot\alpha$. The scaled transverse variables have comparable components at launch, although the growing physical amplitude has an $E_1$ component of order $S^{-1}$ times its $E_2$ component. Here $S$ is a dimensionless shear parameter, not the final time $S_j$ of §7.

e03-s6-ratio.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: The input $\varepsilon$ is the ratio of the older gradient in the preceding wave's frame at launch; it is not the ratio of the new wave at launch. The target $\varepsilon_+$ is instead measured in the new frame, against $M$. At the crossing this second ratio becomes the input for the next amplification problem. In §7 these are $\varepsilon_{j-1}=L_j^{-2}$ and $\varepsilon_j=L_{j+1}^{-2}$.

e03-s6-normalized-time.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: The derivative in normalized time is $r^{-1}$ times the physical time derivative. In particular a crossing at normalized time $\tau_*$ lies at $t_0+\tau_*/r$. This conversion is needed before comparing the bracket with the time allowance $\tau_j$ of §7 (which is a physical time).

e03-s6-activation-vector.TorusEuler.inverseAdjoint_activationWave: Write $F=D_aX(t_0,0)$. From $\kappa=F^{-T}k_*$ the prescription is $k_*=\lambda F^TE_3(t_0)$, which gives the desired normal in physical space. The vector $k_*$ need not be an integer vector: the oscillatory profiles vanish near the boundary of the label cell before periodic extension, as in §3.1.

e03-s6-growing-initial-direction.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: In the strong-shear system at $\tau=0$, $\alpha_1'=-\alpha_2$ and $\alpha_2'=-\alpha_1$. The vector $(-1,1)$ belongs to the growing eigendirection. Undoing the scaling in (2.3) gives $-E_1/S+E_2$, which is perpendicular to the chosen launch normal $E_3$.

e03-s6-growing-peak-normalization.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: The covector equation determines the normal without reference to the seed. Once the normal is fixed, the seed equation is homogeneous and linear. If the unscaled seed has maximum length $A$ on $[t_0,T]$, the positive factor $\lambda^{-3/4}/A$ makes its maximum $\lambda^{-3/4}$ while leaving its frame, and hence the crossing time, unchanged. Fixing the peak rather than the initial length makes the amplitude during the switch exponentially small relative to a prescribed later velocity scale.

e03-s6-physical-comparison-error.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.amplificatio:
The four terms of (2.6) are the relative changes of $B_{12}$ and $B_{32}$, $\|B\|_\infty/r$, and $\|E_c\|_\infty/
u$. Differentiate the entries in the moving frame: their derivatives have norm at most $4\|B\|_\infty^2+\|B_t\|_\infty$. Integrating this bound and dividing by the smaller entry $\eta$ controls both relative changes. The denominator $
u$ for $E_c$ comes from the scaling of the amplitude equations ($S/r=1/(2
u)$), so smallness merely relative to the shear strength would not suffice.

e03-s6-frame-speed.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.movingFrame_: Each frame equation in (2.2) contains two entries of $B$. Their absolute values are at most $\|B\|_\infty$, so $|E_i'|\le2\|B\|_\infty$. In $B_{ij}'=E_i'\cdot BE_j+E_i\cdot B_tE_j+E_i\cdot BE_j'$ this gives $4\|B\|_\infty^2+\|B_t\|_\infty$. The time derivative of the moving matrix entry is therefore different from that of $B$ in a fixed frame.

r2-s6-two-comparison-inputs.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: The estimate is $\|G(t,s)\|\le252eS\,\gamma(t)/\gamma(s)$ for the transverse propagator from any time $s$ to a later time $t$. In particular, if the seed decays on that interval, the bound is proportional to $\gamma(t)/\gamma(s)$ even for data inserted at $s$. This is the form needed for the inhomogeneous transverse equations, whose forcing is measured relative to the seed.

The lower bound for $\nu_+$ gives $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge|\kappa||\mathbf a|\nu\varepsilon/2$ at the origin. After extending this sign to the envelope, the leading pressure Hessian is nonpositive wherever $F_h'\ge0$. Its upper bound consequently uses the small negative part of $F_h'$, rather than its order-one positive slope.

e03-s6-later-origin-bounds.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: Write $G(t,s)$ for the propagator of the homogeneous transverse equation. The displayed inequality gives $\|G(t,s)\|\le CS\gamma(t)/\gamma(s)$. A solution forced by $f$ and starting with zero data thus has size after division by $\gamma(t)$ bounded by $CS\int_{t_0}^t |f(s)|/\gamma(s)\,ds$ (with the transverse projection of $f$). This is the reason for measuring the corrections in the seed weight in §5.

The coupling bound holds on the entire active interval: $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a=|\kappa||\mathbf a|\nu_+>0$. In the leading pressure Hessian this quantity multiplies $-F_h'$ in the direction $\kappa$. Localization must preserve the sign for all these times, not merely at the crossing where the next wave is selected.

e03-s6-origin-hypotheses.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: The common bound $\mathsf D$ has to cover both $CS$ and $2/(\nu\varepsilon)$. At step $j$ the first is at most $C\mu^{1/8}L_j$, and the second at most $2L_j^2/\pi$. The logarithmic bound (1.15) allows even the smaller allowance $\mu$ for these two quantities; $\mathsf D=\mu^9$ is already needed for the parent coefficients.

e03-s6-switch-formula.TorusEuler.waveSwitch_eq_one_sub_envelop: The transition is a function of $\tau=r(t-t_0)$: it is zero for $\tau\le0$ and is $1-\chi(1+\tau)$ for $\tau\ge0$. Since the fixed profile equals one through argument $1$ and zero from argument $2$, the transition is confined to the first unit of normalized time.
e03-s6-switch-formula.TorusEuler.waveSwitch_eq_zero_of_le: Since $r>0$, every $t\le t_0$ has $r(t-t_0)\le0$. The fixed transition vanishes there, including at the activation time. This ensures that the oscillation is still zero at launch while the central seed itself is nonzero.

e03-s6-switch-smooth.TorusEuler.contDiff_waveSwitch: The transition is smooth and constant on each side of its switching interval, so the piecewise description joins smoothly at $t=t_0$ and $t=t_0+1/r$. Smoothness is preserved by composing with the affine time change.

e03-s6-switch-complete.TorusEuler.waveSwitch_eq_one_of_activati: At $t=t_0+1/r$ the argument of $\chi$ is $2$, so $\widetilde\chi$ equals one from then on. The permissible crossing bracket begins at normalized time $\tau_m\ge2/\varepsilon>1$. Hence every such crossing occurs with the entire preceding shear already switched on.

e03-s6-switch-derivative.TorusEuler.waveSwitch_weighted_derivativ: If $\theta$ denotes the fixed transition in normalized time, then $\widetilde\chi'=r\theta'(r(t-t_0))$. The large factor $r$ appears only where $0\le r(t-t_0)\le1$; the small early seed bound needs to hold only on that interval.

e03-s6-early-normalized-gain.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: For the reference solution with its initial normalization, the maximum on the first unit is at most $e$, while its peak is at least $e^{\varepsilon^{-1/2}-1}$. Comparing the actual and reference lengths at both times introduces at most $e^{2\varepsilon}$. Consequently the first-unit length divided by the actual maximum is at most $e^{3-\varepsilon^{-1/2}}$ for $2\varepsilon\le1$. The positive normalization cancels from this quotient.

Let $a_{\rm ref}$ be the reference growing amplitude, with its maximum at $\tau_m$. The actual maximum is at least its value at $\tau_m$, and the comparison controls the length there relative to $a_{\rm ref}(\tau_m)$. Thus the early-amplitude estimate survives peak normalization even if the actual maximum is attained at a different time. No assertion about the exact turning time of the perturbed amplitude is needed.

e03-s6-small-switch-residual.TorusEuler.waveSwitch_weighted_derivativ: Differentiation of the switch costs a factor $r$, since it takes physical time $1/r$. Its derivative vanishes after that time, so only the small first-unit amplitude enters the residual. A longer interval of smallness for $\gamma$ is unnecessary.

r2-s6-crossing-input.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: In Proposition 2.8 the coupling ratio at $\tau_m$ is at least $\varepsilon/18>\varepsilon_+$, while at $2(\varepsilon\varepsilon_+)^{-1/2}$ it is at most $3\varepsilon_+/4$. Since the first coupling stays positive, continuity supplies a crossing between these endpoints. The lower endpoint is the reference turning time, not the actual amplitude's maximum time.

e03-s6-first-crossing.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: The ratio is continuous because the new first coupling stays positive. Its level set at $\varepsilon_+$ in the closed bracket is nonempty and compact, so it has a least element. No monotonicity of the perturbed ratio is required to define this time.

The minimum is taken only among crossings after the reference turning time in the specified bracket. Proposition 2.8 gives the strength bounds at every such crossing, so choosing the first one fixes the activation unambiguously without needing uniqueness of the level set.

r2-s6-reference-turn.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: The reference turning time is at least $2/\varepsilon$, whereas the cutoff has completed by normalized time one. A crossing in the stated bracket therefore gives both the target coupling ratio and the full preceding shear for the next step. Its strength is estimated by (2.23), which uses the product of the amplitude and the now longer wave vector.

e03-s7-one-common-sequence.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: For each fixed order $m$ we will sum the tail of this same sequence, starting where $q_j\ge m$. The oscillations are summable in velocity and the remaining corrections in the stronger norms. The new residual, unlike the velocity increment, must already be small at the frequency of the next wave.

r3c8-s7-central-wave-provenance.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71StepData: In the manuscript the central pair is the seed and transported covector of the very expansion used to define $U_j$. The exported `Theorem71StepData` identifies its central amplitude and cutoff with the stored ones, and imposes the launch length for the expansion covector. It does not identify that covector at later times with the stored `centralWaves.waveVector`. The source comment also distinguishes the later-wave peak recorded in the crossing data from the weaker bound $\gamma\le1$ in the expansion's `S5.Origin`. These are differences in what the step record asserts, not a change to the paper's construction.

e03-s7-central-couplings.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.entry: The vectors defining the frame are those of wave $j$, but the gradient in both products is $\nabla U_{j-1}(t,0)$. Thus these are the couplings of wave $j$ with the velocity over which it was constructed. When evaluated at $t_{j+1}$ they become the frozen couplings of the following comparison.
e03-s7-central-couplings.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The first coupling in (7.1) is an entry of the older gradient in the frame of the new wave. Its bound at $t_{j+1}$ gives the next frozen value of $\nu$. The lower bound throughout $[t_j,S_j]$ has a different use: it keeps the leading pressure coefficient nonnegative at the center and, after localization, on the envelope.

r2-s7-actual-oscillation.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71StepData: In the notation of §5, $W=W_{\rm osc}+\bar W$. The physical oscillation is $O_j=(W-\langle W\rangle)^\natural$, evaluated along the inverse parent flow before the Fourier multiplier is applied. The remainder of the stage difference is then exactly $\bar W^\natural+v_\Lambda$.
r2-s7-actual-oscillation.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Steps: The equality in the step data is with the oscillation of the hierarchy *before* the Fourier cutoff. The support and zero-data assertions follow at the profile level. Applying the multiplier to the oscillation itself would in general destroy its spatial localization, even though it would preserve zero time slices.

e03-s7-half-length.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: The launch $t_j$ is inherited from the previous step. Before choosing the next crossing we set $S_j=t_j+2\tau_j$, solve the central wave on $[t_j,S_j]$ and normalize its peak there. The mean equations use the longer interval $[0,S_j]$. The next crossing does not determine the endpoint of either problem.
e03-s7-half-length.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: The two halves of $[t_j,S_j]$ play different roles. The first contains the crossing, and the second leaves enough of the parent slab for all subsequent launches. In fact the total length of all future launch gaps is at most $4\tau_j/3$, whereas the active interval has length $2\tau_j$.
e03-s7-half-length.TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.τ: For later waves $r\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}$, so $r\tau_j\ge cL_{j+1}^3$. The comparison requires a bracket of normalized length $2L_jL_{j+1}\le2L_{j+1}^2$. The extra power of the logarithm pays for the fixed comparison constant without enlarging the physical interval beyond a summable length.
e03-s7-half-length.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: There are two different intervals: the gap $[t_j,t_{j+1}]$, of length at most $\tau_j$, and the slab $[0,S_j]$, where the velocity is defined. Since future allowances decrease at least geometrically with ratio $1/4$, all later gaps together fit in $4\tau_j/3$, strictly less than the active length $2\tau_j$.

e03-s7-depth.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.step: To make the depth error of size $\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$, solve $2P/3=4K_{j+1}$. This gives $P=6K_{j+1}$, which also leaves enough decay for the derivative factors and Fourier truncation. `stepDepth` uses the shifted index $i=j-1$; thus it reads the order $q_{i+2}$.

e03-s7-existence.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: The construction fixes the profiles and exponent parameter and then makes one sufficiently large choice of $N$. The existential sequence and accumulation time are shared by all fixed derivative orders, rather than choosing a new initial velocity when a new norm is requested.
e03-s7-existence.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: Fix the cutoff symbol and the requested lower bound for the envelope exponent. The theorem then chooses the exponents and a cost majorant $F$. For every admissible $\mathcal B\ge F$ one obtains a sufficiently large threshold for $N$, uniform in $j$. This order allows $\mathcal B$ to be enlarged for the auxiliary terminal regularity estimates.
e03-s7-existence.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The analytic lemmas initially provide different lower bounds on the envelope exponent, different polynomial losses in $\mathsf D$ and different fixed-order constants. The proof of `theorem_7_1_of` takes common maxima for the envelope and polynomial exponents and forms a majorant of the costs before choosing the schedule. The public `theorem_7_1` supplies the local lemmas to this conditional assembly theorem; the induction does not require them as additional hypotheses in the exported statement.

r2-s7-shear-identification.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The stationary shear is fixed with tilt $\rho=\varepsilon_1$, so the first central ratio already agrees with the target at $t_2=0$. The construction starts from this prescribed $U_0$ rather than choosing an arbitrary smooth parent.
r2-s7-shear-identification.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: The numbered statement requires that the base velocity be exactly the stationary shear with the scheduled tilt, and that its first wave already be present at zero. This supplies the starting coupling for the subsequent comparisons.

e03-s7-T1.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: The band $|\xi|\le2\Lambda_j$ is imposed on the truncated velocity $U_j$. It is unrelated to an integer constraint on the central covector of a wave. At the next step it allows arbitrary fixed spatial derivatives of the parent to be estimated by Bernstein from $\|U_j\|_\infty$, without differentiating the hierarchy that produced it.
e03-s7-T1.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: The field `stage_regular` combines regularity and the Fourier support with a label-flow condition. Oddness keeps the origin fixed; the finite band bounds spatial derivatives of the parent. These are requirements on the supplied stage sequence.
e03-s7-T1.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The symbol is $\psi(\xi/\Lambda_j)$, supported in $|\xi|\le2\Lambda_j$. The band is consequently an exact support statement, not a statement that the high-frequency tail is merely small. This exact band will be used again for the residual's derivatives.
e03-s7-T1.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: The statement quantifies over the admissible cutoff symbol before constructing the sequence. Each stage is smooth, odd, divergence free and supported in the band of its own cutoff. The identity with the truncated expansion explains how these properties pass to the next parent.
e03-s7-T1.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: Apply the smooth Fourier multiplier to the sum of the parent and the finite expansion. It commutes with spatial differentiation and preserves oddness, since the symbol is radial. Smoothness, divergence freedom and the prescribed band are thereby inherited by the new stage; localization concerns the oscillation before this operation.

e03-s7-T2.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: At step $j+1$ the leading velocity is of size $\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/4}$ and its quadratic forcing is of size $\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ in the construction's scaled norms. The first mean must cancel the parent residual along with the averaged forcing. The inherited allowance $\lambda_{j+1}^{-3}$ is smaller than $\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ by the factor $\lambda_{j+1}^{-1/2}$. Thus the residual requirement in (T2) anticipates the leading scale of a wave not yet constructed.
e03-s7-T2.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: If $F=D_aX_j(t,a)$, its inverse is the derivative of the inverse flow at $X_j(t,a)$. The forward estimate transports the label support into a small Eulerian ball; the estimates for both $F$ and $F^{-1}$ bound the transported covector from above and below. The proof needs these bounds for the entire flow, not merely the central trajectory.
e03-s7-T2.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The pointwise velocity and residual estimates hold throughout the closed slab, with the same scale for the forward and inverse deformation maps. The residual is measured against the next frequency, not the cutoff radius of the present stage.
e03-s7-T2.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: These bounds are for the actual truncated parent that will enter the next expansion. Its velocity and Fourier band give all fixed spatial coefficient estimates; its deformation controls the change between labels and physical space. Its residual is $\partial_tU_j+\mathbb P\operatorname{div}(U_j\otimes U_j)$, so the next mean cancels the defect of this field, not the defect computed before truncation.
e03-s7-T2.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The proof obtains the deformation estimate for the truncated velocity, not just for the untruncated expansion. It also bounds the actual projected momentum residual of the truncated stage. These are the quantities that will be used when this stage is the next parent.

e03-s7-T3.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: The mean inverse requires $H^\#=(D^2\pi_j-\nabla R_j)\circ X_j\le I$, not that the pressure Hessian be small in operator norm. In the displacement energy the curvature enters with a minus sign. Even very negative curvature is compatible with coercivity; only the sum of the upper pressure allowances and the norm of the residual derivative has to be small.
e03-s7-T3.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: At $j=0$ the pressure bound is zero (the sum is empty). Each new wave costs at most $\lambda_{j-1}^{-1}I$ in the upper Hessian bound, and these matrix inequalities can be added. No absolute-norm bound on $D^2\pi_j$ follows from this clause.
e03-s7-T3.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: For each $v$ the formal upper bound is on $\langle v,D^2\pi_j v\rangle$. Its finite sum runs from frequency index $0$ to $j-1$, precisely the parent frequencies of waves $1$ through $j$. A bound of this form does not imply $\|D^2\pi_j\|\le2/N$.
e03-s7-T3.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: The expansion pressure $\Pi$ and the pressure $\pi_j$ of the truncated field are different: $\Delta\Pi=\operatorname{div}R_V-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla V)^2)$, whereas $\Delta\pi_j=-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla U_j)^2)$. The Hessian of their difference is controlled by the residual and Fourier tail in Proposition 5.11. Adding that error to the one-sided bound for the expansion pressure propagates (T3).
e03-s7-T3.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The leading pressure term in Lemma 5.9 is $-c_{\mathbf a}F_h'\kappa\otimes\kappa$, with $c_{\mathbf a}\ge0$. Since $F_h'\ge-Ch$ and $c_{\mathbf a}|\kappa|^2\le4\mathsf D^3\lambda^{1/4}$, its positive part is bounded by $C\mathsf D^3 h\lambda^{1/4}I=C\mathsf D^3\lambda^{-1/4}I$. The large negative part needs no such estimate. The higher pressures and the error in recomputing the pressure after truncation are estimated separately.

e03-s7-T4-splitting.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: The full rank-one term has norm $\sigma_j$ at the crossing and becomes the preceding shear of (6.5). It is not enough to approximate that matrix to a small relative error: the scaled amplitude equation multiplies the central error by $S/r=1/(2\nu)$, not by $1/\sigma$. The absolute tolerance $\lambda_j^{-1/4}$ therefore keeps the comparison error small even when the leading matrix grows without bound.
e03-s7-T4-splitting.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: For $v\in\mathbb R^3$ the new matrix acts as $v\mapsto(\kappa_j\cdot v)\mathbf a_j$. Its norm is $\sigma_j=|\kappa_j||\mathbf a_j|$ because it is rank one. The error bound in (T4) is absolute, so at the crossing the error is smaller than the principal shear by a factor of order $\lambda_j^{-1/2}$.
e03-s7-T4-splitting.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The leading profile is $\widetilde\chi_jg\mathbf a_jF_h$ evaluated at the inverse parent flow. At the origin its phase is zero. Since $g(0)=1$, $F_h(0)=0$ and $F_h'(0)=1$, all terms from differentiating the slow factors vanish and the fast derivative is exactly $\widetilde\chi_j\mathbf a_j\otimes\kappa_j$. The higher profiles, mean and Fourier error make up $E_{c,j}$.
e03-s7-T4-splitting.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: The matrix identity in `T4_gradient` concerns the stored central pair. `Theorem71StepData` connects the stored amplitude and cutoff to the hierarchy used to build $U_j$, and identifies its launch frequency, but has no corresponding equality between the stored normal and the expansion's transported covector on $[t_j,S_j]$. The paper identifies these normals by construction; that provenance is not fully expressed in the exported step-data fields.
e03-s7-T4-splitting.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: Lemma 5.9 controls the central derivative of the finite expansion up to $\lambda_j^{-1/3}$. The cutoff changes this by $\nabla v_\Lambda(t,0)$, of size at most $\lambda_{j+1}^{-5}$. Both are smaller than the absolute tolerance $\lambda_j^{-1/4}$ in (T4). The stored central covector in the exported step record is not separately identified with the expansion covector (see the scope note at the central data).

e03-s7-T4-clock.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: The equality $\widetilde\chi_j=1$ is needed on the whole active interval of wave $j+1$, not just at its launch. That interval is contained in $[t_{j+1},S_j]$ by the endpoint estimates. Thus the successor sees the full preceding rank-one shear throughout its comparison window.
e03-s7-T4-clock.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: The crossing window includes the equality $\widetilde\chi_j(t)=1$ for all $t$ from the next launch through $S_j$. Knowing merely that the ratio has reached its target would not give the required gradient splitting if the switch were still incomplete.
e03-s7-T4-clock.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: From $S_j=t_j+2\tau_j$ and $t_{j+1}-t_j\le\tau_j$ we have $S_j-t_{j+1}\ge\tau_j$. Since $2\tau_{j+1}\le\tau_j/2$, the next endpoint lies strictly before $S_j$. The whole next endpoint problem, beginning at time zero, can therefore use $U_j$.
e03-s7-T4-clock.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: The first wave has a constant unit cutoff, so the zero time gap $t_2-t_1=0$ also satisfies these requirements. For later waves the crossing occurs after the switch is complete. The same condition therefore covers both the base case and the later crossings.
e03-s7-T4-clock.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: For later waves the bracket begins at normalized time at least $2/\varepsilon>1$. The switch has completed by normalized time one. This is the reason the crossing inequality and full-shear condition in (T4) can be established at the same launch.

e03-s7-crossing-values.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: The ratio at the crossing sets the next gain $\varepsilon_j^{-1/2}=L_{j+1}$. The other two inequalities turn the old strength into a useful physical rate: $c\lambda_j^{1/8}\le\sqrt{2\sigma_j\nu_j}\le C\lambda_j^{1/8}L_{j+1}$. The lower bound ensures rapid amplification and the upper bound keeps the normalized comparison interval from becoming too long. Both conclusions are needed for the next step's short physical interval.
e03-s7-crossing-values.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions:
The frame is made from wave $j$, and the entries $
u_j,\eta_j$ are computed against $
abla U_{j-1}$, which governs its central equations. These entries, together with $\sigma_j$ at $t_{j+1}$, are precisely the frozen data for wave $j+1$. In particular they should not be computed using the corrected gradient of $U_j$ in place of $
abla U_{j-1}$.
e03-s7-crossing-values.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: At the next stage $r^2=2\sigma_j\nu_j$, so (7.3) gives $c\lambda_j^{1/8}\le r\le C\lambda_j^{1/8}L_{j+1}$. The lower bound places the crossing within the first half of the active interval; the upper bound limits the powers of normalized time appearing in the perturbation estimate. Both bounds on strength are needed.
e03-s7-crossing-values.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: In the formal statement the absolute strength constant is fixed to $18e^3$. The same selected crossing supplies the upper and lower strength bounds and the two coupling conditions. The induction does not choose one crossing for the ratio and another for the strength.
e03-s7-crossing-values.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: By Proposition 2.8, $\cos\varphi$ is comparable to $\varepsilon_{j-1}$ at the reference peak and to $\varepsilon_j$ at the crossing. The post-peak exponential factor in the reference amplitude is bounded between $1$ and $e^2$, so the normalized amplitude at the crossing is comparable to $(\varepsilon_j/\varepsilon_{j-1})^{1/2}$. At the same time $|\kappa_j|\asymp\lambda_j/\varepsilon_j$. Their product, with the peak $\lambda_j^{-3/4}$, is comparable to $\lambda_j^{1/4}L_jL_{j+1}$. This explains why a strong shear remains after the amplitude has fallen. Wave one is covered separately by Lemma 6.1.

e03-s7-lifetime.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: All finite stages can be restricted to the same closed interval $[0,T_\infty]$. The summable velocity increments then give a continuous limit even at its right endpoint. The high-derivative estimates are used only before the corresponding launch or outside the oscillatory support, so they do not bound the limiting gradient at the origin at $T_\infty$.
e03-s7-lifetime.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: The lifetime field requires convergence of the launch times to a positive real time, together with $T_\infty<S_j$ for every $j$. The inequalities ensure that evaluating every approximate stage at $T_\infty$ is legitimate even though the limiting gradient will be singular.
e03-s7-lifetime.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The active endpoint $S_j$ lies after $T_\infty$ by at least $2\tau_j/3$, and $S_j-t_j=2\tau_j\to0$. Thus the launches approach the limit from below and the slab endpoints approach it from above. The approximants are defined at the terminal time without extending any finite-stage solution.
e03-s7-lifetime.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: The same existential time occurs in the lifetime and stage conclusions. This gives a common closed interval for uniform convergence and for off-origin estimates, while identifying it with the maximal smooth lifespan requires the subsequent limiting argument.
e03-s7-lifetime.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: Summing the bounds on all subsequent launch gaps gives $T_\infty-t_j\le4\tau_j/3$. The active interval has length $2\tau_j$, so $S_j-T_\infty\ge2\tau_j/3$. The limit lies in the interior of every finite stage's time slab, with a margin that decreases with the stage.

e03-s7-oscillation-support.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: The support is a torus ball centered at zero, represented in the lift by balls about lattice points. The support assertion applies to the specified untruncated oscillation, not the Fourier-truncated stage difference. Its radius is at most the inverse preceding frequency.
e03-s7-oscillation-support.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: Fix a compact set $K$ away from the origin and an order $m$. Once $\lambda_{j-1}^{-1}<\operatorname{dist}(K,0)$, the localized oscillation vanishes in an open neighborhood of $K$, together with every spatial derivative. For $q_j\ge m$, (7.4) therefore bounds the full increment on $K$ by $\lambda_j^{-1}$ through order $m$, uniformly up to $T_\infty$. No bound on the fast derivatives inside the shrinking ball is asserted.
e03-s7-oscillation-support.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: Localization concerns only the rapidly oscillating part of the increment. The means are obtained by an inverse on the whole torus, and the Fourier multiplier is also nonlocal. These other terms may extend outside the envelope, but their derivatives are small through $q_j$.
e03-s7-oscillation-support.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: Fourier truncation is nonlocal in space. The compact support retained by the finite oscillatory profiles is therefore assigned to their physical evaluation $O_j$ before truncation. The difference produced by the multiplier is included with the mean in the remainder of (7.4).
e03-s7-oscillation-support.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The support in labels is $|a|\le2\ell_*$. The parent flow fixes zero and has derivative at most $\mathsf D$, so the physical support has radius at most $2\mathsf D\ell_*\le2\mathsf D^{-2}$. It shrinks with the preceding frequency even after allowing for the transport.

e03-s7-increment-bounds.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: For the supremum norm, both terms in $U_j-U_{j-1}=O_j+(U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j)$ are at most $\lambda_j^{-1}$. In a higher norm only the second bound is available. The first term can be discarded before activation or away from its shrinking support, giving convergence of the full increments in that higher norm there.
e03-s7-increment-bounds.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: The remainder is bounded in $C_tC^{m,1/2}$ for $m\le q_j$; the oscillation is bounded only in $C_tL^\infty$. In particular setting $m=0$ does not assert a uniform $C^{0,1/2}$ bound on the oscillation. Any stronger spatial Hölder estimate for the full increment requires an additional bound on $O_j$.
e03-s7-increment-bounds.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The norm is applied to $U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j$, rather than to the gradient of the entire velocity difference. At order zero the triangle inequality gives the uniform increment bound $2\lambda_j^{-1}$; at a fixed higher order the same argument works only where the oscillation vanishes.
e03-s7-increment-bounds.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: In `Theorem71Conclusions` the estimates alone concern a localized summand $O_j$ and a regular remainder. The stronger numbered statement includes `Theorem71Steps`, which identifies that summand with the physical oscillation of the finite expansion. This distinction matters when relating (7.4) to the actual profiles; the limiting velocity estimates themselves need only the support, vanishing and norm bounds.
e03-s7-increment-bounds.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The velocity scale of $O_j$ is $\lambda_j^{-5/4}$ before the coefficient loss, which (7.8) absorbs into $\lambda_j^{1/32}$. In contrast its leading central derivative contains the factor $\kappa_j$ and can be large. The estimate for the mean and Fourier tail through $q_j$ is what permits the other part of the increment to be summed even in high norms.

e03-s7-inactive-oscillation.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: Given $T<T_\infty$, choose a stage beyond which $t_j\ge T$. The oscillations at all those stages vanish on $[0,T]$, so (7.4) controls the entire increment through order $q_j$. At time zero the same argument applies to every $j\ge2$, even though the mean corrections are already present.
e03-s7-inactive-oscillation.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: The record requires exact vanishing, including the activation time. This is stronger than an early gain estimate and is why for any $T<T_\infty$ the full velocity increments, not just their remainders, are controlled through order $q_j$ for all sufficiently late $j$.
e03-s7-inactive-oscillation.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The vanishing includes $t=t_j$: the leading cutoff is zero there and the higher oscillatory profiles start with zero data. In particular the second wave, which begins activation at time zero, does not contribute an oscillatory increment to the initial data. The first wave is the exception.
e03-s7-inactive-oscillation.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: For $j\ge2$, $O_j(0)=0$. The phase-independent correction is solved with zero displacement at both ends, which is not zero velocity at both ends. Its initial value can therefore change $U_j(0)$; (7.4) makes these changes, including the Fourier errors, summable at every fixed spatial order.
e03-s7-inactive-oscillation.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The time cutoff makes the leading oscillation vanish at activation. The higher oscillatory equations are solved forward with zero data at $t_j$; consequently those profiles vanish there as well. This closed-interval statement is what the convergence proof uses at $T=t_j$.

e03-s7-all-orders.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_order_tends: Fix $m$ first. Once $q_j\ge m$, all subsequent remainders in (7.4) are bounded in $C_tC^{m,1/2}$ by $\lambda_j^{-1}$. Choosing a later index so that $t_j\ge T$ gives the same estimate for the full increments on $[0,T]$ when $T<T_\infty$.
e03-s7-all-orders.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_1_3: For convergence before $T_\infty$, choose the tail index so that both $q_j\ge m$ and $t_j\ge T$. Lemma 1.3 supplies the first choice, the activation clock the second. From then on (7.4) estimates the full velocity increment on $[0,T]$ in the desired norm.

r5-ind-figure4-inactive.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The solid part of each row is the interval where the oscillation is absent; the mean is already defined there and may change the initial velocity. The solid segment therefore marks where the full increment has the high-order estimate of (7.4), not where the two successive velocity fields agree.

r5-ind-figure4-crossing.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ce: The crossing belongs to the current wave, and the beginning of the following row's active interval is this same time. The current wave's cutoff already equals one, so its full rank-one gradient is available on the following row, whose endpoint is earlier than the current row's endpoint.

r5-ind-figure4-endpoint.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: Each row represents an entire approximate velocity on $[0,S_i]$, not a successive segment of a single trajectory. Its oscillation vanishes through $t_i$, and its mean is defined from zero. The endpoints extend beyond the accumulation time, allowing the whole sequence to be compared on the same closed time interval.

e03-s7-residual-support.TorusEuler.parentResidualFourierBand_of_: Apply the Leray projection before using Bernstein. In Fourier variables the quadratic product of two fields in the band $2\Lambda_j$ has band $4\Lambda_j$; projection, divergence and the time derivative do not enlarge this band. Thus $R_j$ is itself band-limited, and $\|\nabla R_j\|_\infty\le C\Lambda_j\|R_j\|_\infty$. This retains the smallness of the momentum defect, which would be lost by separately bounding its large summands.

r2-s7-bernstein-input.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_B_1: Bernstein applied to $U_j$ gives $\|\nabla U_j\|_\infty\le C\Lambda_j\lambda_j$. Applied instead to $R_j$ with its enlarged band and smaller supremum norm, it gives $\|\nabla R_j\|_\infty\le C\Lambda_j\lambda_{j+1}^{-3}$. The latter estimate is needed even though (T2) bounds the residual itself, because the endpoint curvature includes its derivative.

e03-s7-low-gradient.TorusEuler.exists_parentDerivedLowBounds: The spatial Bernstein bound costs one power of $\Lambda_j=\lambda_j^5$ and gives $C\lambda_j^6$ for the gradient. To estimate $\partial_t\nabla U_j$, take one spatial derivative in (7.5). The quadratic term now contains two derivatives and the Leray projection is bounded in $C^{0,1/2}$; using a third ordinary derivative to control this Hölder norm costs $C\Lambda_j^3\lambda_j^2=C\lambda_j^{17}$. Together with the small differentiated residual this fits $\lambda_j^{18}$. The Hölder step avoids using an $L^\infty$ operator bound for the projection.

r2-s7-step-inputs.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71StepData: There are two parent scales in the step. The finite expansion is over $U_{j-1}$, on the full slab $[0,S_j]$, so its coefficient bound is $\mathsf D=\lambda_{j-1}^9$. The comparison for its central pair is written in the frame of wave $j-1$, which evolves over $U_{j-2}$; the bounds for this older gradient are at $\lambda_{j-2}$. Keeping the two estimates distinct is what makes the comparison perturbative even when $\nabla U_{j-1}(t,0)$ is large.

e03-s7-half-length-decay.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_halfLength_: By (1.15), $\tau_j\le\mu^{-1/8}(\log\mu)^6\le\mu^{-1/16}$ for large $N$. At $j+1$ this gives $4\tau_{j+1}\le4\lambda_j^{-1/16}\le4\mu^{-1/4}\le\mu^{-1/8}\le\tau_j$. The last inequality uses $L_{j+1}\ge1$. Both estimates are uniform because $\mu\ge N$.

e03-s7-step-constant.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_step_consta: At depth $P=6K(q_{j+1})$ the estimates through $P+1$ fit in the range $7K(q_{j+1})$. Thus $\Gamma_P\le\mathcal B(q_{j+1})\le\mu$. With $\mathsf D=\mu^9$ and $\lambda=\mu^{K_j}$, this gives $C_{\rm step}\le\mu^{10b}\le\lambda^{1/32}$. In particular the lower restriction $C_{\rm step}^{12}\le\lambda$ and the upper restriction $\lambda\le\|R_{j-1}\|_\infty^{-2/5}$ (when the residual is nonzero) are compatible: the two endpoints lie at most at $\lambda^{3/8}$ and at least at $\lambda^{6/5}$, respectively.

e03-s7-base-velocity.TorusEuler.norm_stationaryShear_le: The shear has length at most $\sqrt{1+\rho^2}\le2$ since $\rho=\varepsilon_1\le1$. Its velocity bound is independent of $N$; choosing $N$ large then supplies the much weaker allowance $\|U_0\|_\infty\le\lambda_0$ of (T2).

e03-s7-base-deformations.TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_jacobian_: Equation (6.2) gives the same bound for both signs of the deformation: $1+t|B_\rho|\le1+4\pi$ on $[0,1]$. Thus the forward and inverse maps both fit the initial allowance $\lambda_0=N$ for large $N$.

r2-s7-base-induction.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_7_1_of: At $j=0$ the stationary shear is a smooth odd divergence-free single-mode field. Its velocity and deformation bounds are absolute and its residual and pressure are zero. These give (T1)–(T3); (T4) begins only once wave one has been constructed.

e03-s7-parent-interval.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_endpointSla: The parent $U_{j-1}$ must be available from time zero, since the mean is selected by two displacement endpoint conditions on $[0,S_j]$. For $j\ge2$, the previous crossing and $4\tau_j\le\tau_{j-1}$ give $S_j\le t_{j-1}+\tau_{j-1}+\tau_{j-1}/2<S_{j-1}$. For $j=1$, $S_1=2\tau_1<1=S_0$ for large $N$. Thus no extension of the parent beyond its slab is required.

e03-s7-pressure-sum.TorusEuler.inductionPressure_sum_le: Since $\lambda_i\ge2^iN$, the pressure allowance is bounded by $N^{-1}\sum_{i\ge0}2^{-i}=2/N$. This estimate is independent of the stage and keeps the positive part of the Hessian small even as more waves are added.

r2-s7-parent-coercivity.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_7_1_of: Using the residual's own band gives $\|\nabla R_{j-1}\|_\infty\le C\mu^5\lambda^{-3}$. This tends to zero uniformly since $\lambda=\mu^{K_j}$. The pressure allowance is at most $2/N$. Adding these bounds gives $D^2\pi_{j-1}-\nabla R_{j-1}\le I$ as quadratic forms; in the displacement energy the two zero endpoint conditions then give the coercivity estimate of §4. Symmetry of the residual derivative is not needed.

r2-s7-first-wave-input.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_6_1: For wave one, $S_1=2\tau_1\le2N^{-1/16}$, so $S_1|B_\rho|\le1/8$ for large $N$. Lemma 6.1 gives the central estimates over the stationary parent and the strength at time zero. In particular no growing comparison or gain estimate is needed to start the induction.
r2-s7-first-wave-input.TorusEuler.FirstWaveOrigin.initial_coupl: Here the starting tilt was chosen to be $\rho=\varepsilon_1$. The initial coupling calculation gives $\eta_1(0)/\nu_1(0)=\varepsilon_1$, with $\nu_1(0)=2\pi$. The desired ratio is already present at $t_2=t_1=0$, so no crossing search is needed for wave one.

e03-s7-growth-rate.TorusEuler.activationGrowthRate_bounds: The square root in $r=\sqrt{2\sigma\nu}$ turns the strength bounds at the preceding crossing into $c\mu^{1/8}\le r\le C\mu^{1/8}L_j$. Consequently $2r\tau_j$ is between $2cL_{j+1}^3$ and $CL_jL_{j+1}^3\le CL_{j+1}^4$. The lower estimate allows the required crossing, and the upper one limits the polynomial loss in (2.7).

e03-s7-older-gradient.TorusEuler.induction_older_gradient_scal: The older matrix $B$ evolves at frequency $\lambda_{j-2}=\mu^{1/K_{j-1}}$, so (7.6) gives $\|B\|\le\mu^{9/K_{j-1}}\le\mu^{1/32}$ and $\|B_t\|\le\mu^{18/K_{j-1}}\le\mu^{1/16}$. These estimates would be useless with $B=\nabla U_{j-1}$. They also give retention of the preceding strength: on the next launch gap, $(\log\sigma_{j-1})'=B_{33}$ and $\tau_j\le\mu^{-1/16}$ imply a logarithmic change of at most $\mu^{-1/32}$. This is used in the interval-wise vorticity estimate of §8.

e03-s7-error-budget.TorusEuler.induction_comparison_error_bu: The first term of (6.6) bounds the variation of the moving-frame couplings relative to $\eta=\nu\varepsilon$. The length $2\tau_j=2\mu^{-1/8}L_{j+1}^3$ multiplies a bound $C\mu^{1/16}$ for $\|B\|^2+\|B_t\|$. This yields $C\varepsilon^{-1}L_{j+1}^3\mu^{-1/16}$. The older gradient divided by $r$ costs $C\mu^{-3/32}$, and the central error divided by $\nu$ costs $C\mu^{-1/4}$. Both latter denominators are bounded below by the inherited crossing values.

r2-s7-comparison-smallness.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: Put $\Theta=2r\tau_j$. Since $\varepsilon^{-1}=L_j^2$ and $\Theta\le CL_{j+1}^4$, dividing the first error term by $\varepsilon$ costs $L_j^4L_{j+1}^3\le L_{j+1}^7$. All three terms in $C_0\Theta^{C_0}\delta/\varepsilon$ are therefore bounded by $C\mu^{-1/16}L_{j+1}^{4C_0+7}$, with $C$ depending on fixed $C_0$. Besides the uniform threshold for the chosen comparison constant, the formal conclusion records eventual smallness for every fixed integer comparison exponent.
r2-s7-comparison-smallness.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_7_1_of: For the fixed constant $C_0$ in (2.7), $C_0\varepsilon\le C_0(\log N)^{-2}$, and $C_0(2r\tau_j)^{C_0}\delta/\varepsilon\le C\mu^{-1/16}(\log\mu)^{8C_0+14}$. Each bound tends to zero uniformly in $\mu\ge N$ as $N$ grows. The threshold thus does not have to be chosen again at each comparison.

e03-s7-ratio-decay.TorusEuler.couplingRatioOfGain_step: Since $L_{j+1}=K_{j+2}L_j$, the target ratio is $\varepsilon_j=K_{j+2}^{-2}\varepsilon_{j-1}$. In particular it lies below $\varepsilon_{j-1}/32$ as required by Proposition 2.8. This same geometric decrease will make the changes in the logarithm of the first coupling summable.

e03-s7-crossing-half-window.TorusEuler.crossingClock_le_endpointHalf: The upper bracket in physical time is $2L_jL_{j+1}/r$, at most $C\mu^{-1/8}L_{j+1}^2\le\tau_j$. The lower endpoint also gives a useful lower bound: $(t_{j+1}-t_j)\ge 2L_j^2/r\ge c\mu^{-1/8}L_j$. The upper bound places the next slab; the lower bound supplies positive elapsed time.

e03-s7-cumulative-log.TorusEuler.firstCoupling_cumulative_log_:
At wave $j$ the frozen first coupling is $
u_{j-1}(t_j)$ and the first coupling at its crossing is $
u_j(t_{j+1})$. The comparison gives a bound $2\varepsilon_{j-1}$ for the absolute logarithm of their ratio. Summing from $
u_1(t_2)=2\pi$ telescopes the logarithms, with total error at most $2\varepsilon_1/(1-1/32)<4\varepsilon_1$.

e03-s7-uniform-coupling.TorusEuler.firstCoupling_pi_bounds: By the logarithmic estimate, $\nu_j(t_{j+1})/(2\pi)$ lies between $e^{-4\varepsilon_1}$ and $e^{4\varepsilon_1}$. Choose $N$ so that $4\varepsilon_1\le\log2$; both bounds then give the fixed interval $[\pi,4\pi]$ at every crossing. No further shrinking of this interval with the stage is needed.

e03-s7-switch-residual.TorusEuler.exists_waveSwitch_scheduled_w: The derivative is confined to the first normalized unit. There $\gamma\le e^{3-L_j}$ and $|\widetilde\chi'|\le Cr$, so $\|\widetilde\chi'\gamma\|_\infty\le Ce^3\mu^{1/8}L_j\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}\le\mu\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$. The last inequality follows from (1.15), uniformly in $j$. Wave one contributes no switching residual.

r2-s7-expansion-step.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_7_1_of: The parent estimates supply the band, deformation, residual and effective-Hessian hypotheses in §5.1; the comparison supplies the two central estimates (5.5). The smallness condition for the hierarchy is independent of those hypotheses: $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le\lambda^{-5/96}$. It follows from the cost test at order $q_{j+1}$ that one may solve the finite hierarchy at depth $6K_{j+1}$. The local estimates are assembled with precisely these inputs in `theorem_7_1_of`.

e03-s7-depth-residual-identity.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_residual_ex: The factor $\lambda^{-2P/3}$ is the remainder *before* the physical derivative and coefficient costs in (5.48). Solving $2P/3=4K_{j+1}$ gives $P=6K_{j+1}$, hence the same next-frequency power $\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$ as the exponential smallness from switching on the wave.

e03-s7-residual-power.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_residual_bu: The two errors inside the parentheses of (5.48) are bounded by $\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$ and $\mu\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$. With the physical derivative cost $\lambda^2$ and $C_{\rm step}\mu\le\lambda^{1/16}$, their contribution is at most $2\lambda^{2+1/16}\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$. At the next frequency this loses at most half a power, since $\lambda_{j+1}^{1/2}=\lambda^{K_{j+1}/2}$ dominates $2\lambda^{2+1/16}$. The resulting $-7/2$ leaves room for the constant in Proposition 5.11 before imposing the $-3$ residual allowance.

e03-s7-parent-full-order.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_fullOrder_p: The parent has cutoff $\Lambda_{j-1}=\mu^5$ and velocity norm at most $\mu$. To bound its $C^{P,1/2}$ norm, Bernstein through order $P+1$ costs at most $C_P\mu^{5(P+1)+1}$. Since $C_P\le\mu$, this is at most $\mu^{5P+7}\le\lambda^{P+2}$. Thus the parent norm is estimated at the new frequency without differentiating its previous expansion.

e03-s7-wave-coefficient-cost.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_fullOrder_w: A derivative in physical space may differentiate the phase, at cost $|\kappa|/h\lesssim\mathsf D^2\lambda^{3/2}$. The oscillatory $C^{P,1/2}$ estimate in (5.48) uses $P+1$ derivatives at this scale and starts at size $\lambda^{-5/4}$. Including the coefficient bound gives exponent $3(P+1)/2-5/4+(P+2)/32=(49P+10)/32<2(P+1)$. The mean estimate is smaller, so both fit the full-depth bound used for truncation.

e03-s7-cutoff-tail.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_tail_absorp: The cutoff residual contains a divergence of quadratic tensors. To estimate that residual in $C^{1,1/2}$ one needs the tensors in $C^{2,1/2}$, hence $\Lambda^{2-P}(1+\|V\|_{C_tC^{P,1/2}})^2$. Substituting $\Lambda=\lambda^5$ and the full-depth estimate gives $9\lambda^{14-P}$. Multiplication by $\mu$ gives at most $\lambda^{15-P}=\lambda^{15}\lambda_{j+1}^{-6}\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5}$. The factor five in the cutoff exponent outweighs the factor four from the squared velocity norm.

r2-s7-new-truncation.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71StepData: The velocity $V$ is the exactly divergence-free field obtained from the finite expansion. The new parent is $U_j=S_{\Lambda_j}V$, and its pressure is computed afresh from $\Delta\pi_j=-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla U_j)^2)$. If $v_\Lambda=U_j-V$, then $U_j-U_{j-1}=O_j+\bar W^\natural+v_\Lambda$. The last two terms, rather than the oscillation itself, will have small high-order norms. This is the decomposition used in (7.4).
r2-s7-new-truncation.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The cutoff is scalar and even, preserving divergence freedom and oddness. It also commutes with the Leray projection, so the new projected residual consists of the projected cutoff of $R_V$ and the divergence of the error in cutting off $V\otimes V$. Proposition 5.11 bounds both, giving the required small residual for the following wave.

r2-s7-flow-input.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_7_1_of: The flow estimate of Lemma 5.10 avoids applying Gronwall directly to the large physical gradient. In parent labels set $c=(D_aX)^{-1}(W+v_\Lambda\circ X)$. Solenoidality gives $k_*\cdot c_{\rm osc}=-\partial_s^{-1}\operatorname{div}_a c_{\rm osc}$; thus the phase velocity is controlled without the full factor $|k_*|$. The flow of $(c,k_*\cdot c)$ has bounded derivative in the scaled label and phase coordinates. Returning to the graph $s=k_*\cdot a$ costs $|k_*|/h\le\mathsf D\lambda^{3/2}$, giving the factor $\lambda^{3/2-5/4}=\lambda^{1/4}$ in the deformation estimate. The perturbation $v_\Lambda$ is allowed because it is divergence free and $C_tC^2$-small.

r2-s7-localized-support.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The compact support of the oscillatory profiles is in the label ball $|a|\le2\ell_*$. Because $X(t,0)=0$, the forward deformation bound gives $|X(t,a)|\le2\mathsf D\ell_*\le2\mathsf D^{-2}$. With $\mathsf D=\mu^9$ this is much smaller than $\mu^{-1}$, even after transport. The statement is about $O_j$ before the nonlocal Fourier cutoff.

e03-s7-low-order-mean-cost.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_lowOrder_me: For $m\le q_j$ the coefficient is at most $\mu^{10b(m+2)}$. The inequality $m+2\le2(q_j+1)$ gives $10b(m+2)\le K_j/16$, so it costs only $\lambda^{1/16}$. Multiplying by the mean size $\lambda^{-5/2}$ gives a bound smaller than $\lambda^{-3/2}$ in the required derivative norm.

e03-s7-velocity-increment.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_child_veloc: For $m\le q_j$ the mean costs at most $\lambda^{-3/2}$. The tail estimate at order $m$ gives $\|v_\Lambda\|_{C_tC^{m,1/2}}\le\Lambda_j^{m-2}\mu\varepsilon_\Lambda$. Since $\Lambda_j\ge1$, the extra factor is at most $\lambda^{5q_j}\le\lambda_{j+1}$, so the tail is at most $\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$. The sum is at most $\lambda^{-1}$ for large $N$. No fast derivative of $O_j$ enters this estimate.

e03-s7-new-velocity.TorusEuler.induction_child_velocity_boun: The velocity allowance in (T2) is deliberately much larger than the increment. Indeed, the oscillation and the remainder each cost at most $\lambda^{-1}$ in supremum norm, so $\|U_j\|_\infty\le\mu+2\lambda^{-1}\le\lambda$. In the limit it is instead the estimate $\|U_0\|_\infty+2\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_j^{-1}$ that gives bounded velocity, despite the increasing gradient.

e03-s7-central-error.TorusEuler.induction_child_center_error_: At the origin the derivative of the untruncated expansion is its leading rank-one term plus an error bounded by $\lambda^{-1/3}$. Truncation adds $\nabla v_\Lambda$, whose norm is at most $\lambda_{j+1}^{-5}$. Relative to the new error allowance $\lambda^{-1/4}$, their sum is at most $\lambda^{-1/12}+\lambda^{1/4}\lambda_{j+1}^{-5}$. This is less than one for large $N$, leaving an absolute error small on the next coupling scale.

r2-s7-completion.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_7_1_of:
To restart, restrict the new parent to $[0,S_{j+1}]$. The analytic assumptions follow from (T1)–(T3); on the active portion $[t_{j+1},S_{j+1}]$, the old cutoff equals one, so (T4) is exactly the splitting (6.5) with older gradient $
abla U_{j-1}$. The same crossing supplies $\sigma_j,
u_j,\eta_j/
u_j$ for the next comparison. All of these data are needed before repeating the construction.

e03-s7-limit-of-clock.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: Wave one supplies the prescribed ratio at time zero; its first successor therefore begins activation at zero as well. Every later gap is strictly positive because the selected crossing lies after the positive reference turning time. Thus the accumulating clock starts with $t_3>0$, although its first two entries coincide.
e03-s7-limit-of-clock.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: The formal strict-increase clause starts with $t_2<t_3$; $t_1=t_2$ is a separate initial condition. The crossing estimates also bound the lengths of these positive gaps, which is needed for convergence of the clock.
e03-s7-limit-of-clock.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The quantifier in `times_increase` begins at $j=2$, as the first two activations coincide. For any finite $j$ there is a later strictly larger activation time. In conjunction with convergence this gives $t_j<T_\infty$, so no finite launch is the terminal time.
e03-s7-limit-of-clock.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: Strictness of the launch gaps is a consequence of the crossing bracket. Finiteness comes from a different bound, their summable upper allowances. The two facts give a positive finite accumulation time rather than merely a nondecreasing bounded sequence that could be constant at zero.
e03-s7-limit-of-clock.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The initial pair of equal launch times has a different origin from the later crossings: the stationary shear was tilted to give the desired ratio at zero and wave one is fully present then. All subsequent activations are selected in a bracket with strictly positive elapsed time.

e03-s7-terminal-room.TorusEuler.activationTimes_converge: Let $d_p=t_{p+1}-t_p$. The bounds $0\le d_p\le\tau_p$ and $\tau_{p+k}\le4^{-k}\tau_p$ imply that $T_\infty=t_1+\sum_{p\ge1}d_p$ exists. Each later strict gap makes $T_\infty>t_j$, and $T_\infty-t_j\le\sum_{p\ge j}\tau_p\le4\tau_j/3$. Hence $S_j-T_\infty\ge2\tau_j/3>0$ for every $j\ge1$. The first zero gap causes no difficulty.

e03-s7-all-endpoints.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_commonLifet: Every positive-index slab contains $[0,T_\infty]$ by the tail estimate, and the zeroth slab contains it because $T_\infty<S_1\le S_0=1$. This common interval is obtained without extending any finite approximate velocity beyond its prescribed endpoint.

r2-s8-setting.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.section8: For each wave $S_j=t_j+2\tau_j$ is the end of its construction interval, whereas the next wave starts by $t_j+\tau_j$. Since $\tau_{j+1}\le\tau_j/4$, the time still to elapse after $t_j$ is bounded by $\sum_{p\ge j}\tau_p\le4\tau_j/3<2\tau_j$. Thus the common closed slab lies inside every construction interval, as needed to compare successive velocities at the same time.
r2-s8-setting.TorusEuler.Paper.Text.section8_setting: The common slab is supplied together with the increment and residual estimates, not chosen anew for each spatial order. In particular every finite approximation is available at the terminal time, and all subsequent estimates compare restrictions of a single sequence on this slab.
r2-s8-setting.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.section8_set: The linked proof first chooses the cutoff symbol and an admissible order threshold, then uses Theorem 7.1 with its sufficiently large initial frequency $N_1$. It retains the construction and its conclusions, including the common time $T_\infty$, without needing the full step data again. The limiting arguments below work with those conclusions.

r3c8-s8-increment-estimate.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.closedSlab_ve: Write $D_j=U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j$. Inequality (7.4) bounds $O_j$ in $L^\infty$ and $D_j$ in $C^{m,1/2}$ for $m\le q_j$, each by $\lambda_j^{-1}$. Taking $m=0$ gives $\|U_j-U_{j-1}\|_\infty\le2\lambda_j^{-1}$; to use $m>0$ for the entire increment one must first remove $O_j$ by localization.

e03-s8-summable.TorusEuler.reciprocal_inductive_frequenc: The quadratic gap implies the simpler geometric inequality $\lambda_{j+1}\ge\lambda_j^2\ge2\lambda_j$, since $\lambda_0\ge2$. Thus $\lambda_{j+k}^{-1}\le2^{-k}\lambda_j^{-1}$ and $\sum_{k\ge0}\lambda_{j+k}^{-1}\le2\lambda_j^{-1}$. This is the tail estimate used below, independently of how rapidly the orders increase.

e03-s8-uniform-limit.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.closedSlab_ve: The estimate $\|w-U_n\|_{C_tL^\infty}\le4\lambda_{n+1}^{-1}$ holds on the closed slab, including $T_\infty$. Constructing $w$ in this way uses only the increment bound and continuity of the finite velocities. The linked theorem additionally takes Proposition 8.1 as input to identify $w$ with the smooth solution before $T_\infty$; that identification is not an assumption needed for the uniform limit itself.

r3c8-s8-derivative-strategy.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: There are two ways to remove the oscillatory tail. On $[0,T]$ for $T<T_\infty$, the activation times eventually lie after $T$. On $[0,T_\infty]\times K$ for $K$ away from zero, the shrinking supports eventually miss a neighborhood of $K$. In either region only $U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j$ remains in the late increments, and (7.4) sums its derivatives once $q_j$ exceeds the desired order.

e03-s8-initial-data.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.paper_pr: The first two activation times are both zero, but only the first cutoff is identically one. The second oscillation vanishes at its activation time, as do all later ones at time zero. Thus the initial datum is built from the first truncated wave and the sum of the later mean and Fourier corrections, not by prescribing the stationary shear as the final initial datum.
e03-s8-initial-data.TorusEuler.PaperLimitAgreement: The limit $u_0=w(0)$ is forced by the closed-slab uniform limit. Oddness follows by passing to the limit in $U_j(0,-x)=-U_j(0,x)$, and incompressibility by passing to the first derivatives. The same initial field has both properties and is the datum for the limiting equation.
e03-s8-initial-data.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8: At $t=0$ one has $O_j(0)=0$ for every $j\ge2$, even for wave two, whose activation time is zero. Thus $u_0=U_1(0)+\sum_{j\ge2}(\bar W_j^\natural(0)+v_{\Lambda_j}(0))$. For each fixed spatial order the series has the summable bound (7.4) after finitely many terms. Its mean terms can have nonzero initial data from the endpoint problems.
e03-s8-initial-data.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_1: Taking $T=0$ in the earlier-slab convergence gives precisely the convergence of the initial slices. More explicitly, the error at order $m$ is bounded by $2\lambda_{n+1}^{-1}$ once $n$ is large enough that $q_n\ge m$. Thus the initial datum is determined by the same sequence used to obtain the evolution.
e03-s8-initial-data.TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition81Conclusion: The initial convergence in the conclusion is the convergence of the norm of $U_j(0)-u(0)$ to zero, for every $m$. It is stronger than pointwise convergence of the individual derivatives: all of the derivatives through order $m$ and their half-Hölder seminorms are controlled in one norm.

e03-s8-initial-smooth.TorusEuler.PaperLimitAgreement: The uniform limit on the closed slab defines both $w(0)$ and $w(T_\infty)$. The additional preactivation vanishing at $t=0$ upgrades the first of these limits to every fixed spatial order. At the terminal time the corresponding upgrade from (7.4) is local, on compact sets separated from the shrinking supports of the oscillations.
e03-s8-initial-smooth.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.paper_pr: Fix the derivative order $m$ before taking the limit. Once $q_n\ge m$, the later increments at time zero have sum in $C^{m,1/2}$ at most $2\lambda_{n+1}^{-1}$. The limit in this norm must equal the order-zero limit $w(0)$; varying $m$ therefore proves smoothness of one and the same datum.
e03-s8-initial-smooth.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8: For each fixed $m$, the terms beyond an index with $q_j\ge m$ are summable in $C^{m,1/2}$ at time zero. The finitely many earlier terms are themselves smooth. Completeness gives a limit at this order, and uniqueness of the order-zero limit identifies it with $u_0$; this works for every $m$ without a common bound in all orders.
e03-s8-initial-smooth.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_1: The approximations are not exact Euler evolutions from $U_j(0)$, so continuity of the Euler solution map on its own would not identify their limit. Instead (7.5) provides an integrated equation with an explicit residual tending to zero. The limit of the initial slices is then the datum of the exact equation obtained from that identity.
e03-s8-initial-smooth.TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition81Conclusion: The convergence in each $C^{m,1/2}$ uses a possibly different starting index, but the sequence and its limit are unchanged. Compatibility of the limits follows from their common order-zero limit. Thus the construction gives a single smooth initial field, rather than a family of initial fields each with only a prescribed finite regularity.

r3c8-s8-maximal-solution-interface.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8: The paper invokes the classical maximal solution from $u_0$, whose maximal time might initially be infinite. In the formal statement of Proposition 8.1 the solution on $[0,T_\infty)$ is constructed first, and then compared with a given maximal solution of finite real lifespan. Corollary 8.3 establishes that the constructed solution itself is maximal at $T_\infty$.
r3c8-s8-maximal-solution-interface.TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition81Conclusion: The lifespan comparison in the conclusion record is an implication for any given maximal smooth solution of finite real lifespan. Its proof uses uniqueness and the constructed solution on earlier intervals. It is not a general existence theorem for a maximal solution with an infinite endpoint; the constructed finite endpoint is established later.

e03-s8-prefix.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.paper_pr: For $T<T_\infty$, the late oscillations vanish throughout the closed time interval $[0,T]$, so the telescoping bound gives convergence in every fixed spatial Hölder norm. All these limits coincide with $w$ by convergence in supremum norm. This identifies a single spatially smooth field on $[0,T]$; its time regularity and Euler equation are established by the integrated equation below.
e03-s8-prefix.TorusEuler.paper_section_8_of_inductiveE: The formal assembly invokes two results producing a velocity on the closed slab, one carrying the terminal conclusions and one carrying the earlier-time convergence. They are identified pointwise as limits of the same sequence $U_j$, including at $T_\infty$. This last identification uses uniqueness of limits in the velocity space, not uniqueness of smooth Euler evolution, which is available only before the terminal time.
e03-s8-prefix.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8: The assertion is for each pair $(T,m)$ with $T<T_\infty$ and $m$ fixed. The stage from which the derivative estimates apply may depend on both. In particular the proposition gives no bound in $C^{1,1/2}$ on the closed slab reaching $T_\infty$, where the vorticity will diverge.
e03-s8-prefix.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_1: The limiting equation yields a smooth solution through each time $T<T_\infty$. If a maximal solution with datum $u_0$ ended at an earlier time, uniqueness would make it the restriction of this longer solution, contradicting maximality. The argument uses existence of the constructed limit through every earlier time.
e03-s8-prefix.TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition81Conclusion: The conclusion has a constructed velocity and pressure on the half-open slab and then a comparison with any maximal solution of the same datum. In Lean the comparison is conditional on the given solution and its real lifespan; the existence of the constructed velocity does not depend on that comparison.

r2-s8-orders-and-times.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_1_o: Choose the index after fixing both $T$ and $m$. We require $j_0\ge1$, $T\le t_{j_0}$ and $m\le q_{j_0}$. For $j>j_0$ the time restriction then eliminates $O_j$ throughout $[0,T]$, and the order restriction allows (7.4) to be used at order $m$. Either restriction alone would be insufficient for the derivative estimate.

e03-s8-late-vanishing.TorusEuler.inductive_oscillations_eventu: For $j>j_0$ we have $T\le t_{j_0}\le t_j$. The vanishing in Theorem 7.1 includes the activation time itself, so it holds on the whole closed slab $[0,T]$. At each time the oscillatory field is identically zero in space, and hence all of its spatial derivatives vanish there.

e03-s8-tail-estimate.TorusEuler.reciprocal_inductive_frequenc: The sum is over the finite increments $n<j\le\ell$, so it is bounded by the infinite reciprocal-frequency tail beginning at $\lambda_{n+1}$. The bound is independent of $\ell$, and passing $\ell\to\infty$ gives the same error $2\lambda_{n+1}^{-1}$ between $U_n$ and $w$ in the chosen norm.

r2-s8-nonlinear-limit.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_1_o: The quadratic difference is $(U_j-w)\otimes U_j+w\otimes(U_j-w)$. On $[0,T]$ both factors that do not tend to zero are bounded in $C^{1,1/2}$, so (5.59) and boundedness of $\mathbb P\operatorname{div}$ give uniform convergence of the momentum integrand. The residual integral costs at most $T\lambda_{j+1}^{-3}$. This proves the integrated equation for $w$ without convergence of $\partial_tU_j$. To obtain time smoothness, Lean applies the signed momentum map as a bounded bilinear map from spatial jets of order $m+2$ to jets of order $m$, and differentiates the resulting integral identities at every fixed order. Only the limit equation is differentiated in this last step.

e03-s8-uniqueness.TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.velocity_eq_o:
For two smooth velocities $v,u$ with the same datum, set $z=v-u$. Its equation has transport term $v\cdot
abla z$ and remaining nonlinear term $z\cdot
abla u$. Testing with $z$ and using zero divergence and periodicity eliminates both the transport and pressure integrals. Hence $ rac{d}{dt}\|z\|_2^2\le2\|
abla u\|_\infty\|z\|_2^2$, and Grönwall gives equality on each compact common time interval.
e03-s8-uniqueness.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_1_o: The uniqueness argument applies only after the limit has been shown to satisfy Euler and to have the same initial datum as $u$. It identifies $w$ and $u$ on the overlap of their smooth existence intervals. Maximality then rules out an endpoint of $u$ strictly before $T_\infty$.

r5-term-lifespan-comparison.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_1_o: If $T_*<T_\infty$, choose $T$ with $T_*<T<T_\infty$. The smooth limit on $[0,T]$ has the same datum as $u$, hence agrees with it before $T_*$ and extends it beyond $T_*$. This contradicts maximality and gives the lower lifespan bound without using any estimate at the terminal time.

e03-s8-bounded-velocity.TorusEuler.paper_section_8_of_inductiveE: The order-zero convergence extends all the way to the accumulation time, whereas the global derivative convergence used in Proposition 8.1 stops before that time. It follows that the exact solution has a continuous velocity trace at $T_\infty$ even though the derivative argument deliberately gives no global gradient bound there.
e03-s8-bounded-velocity.TorusEuler.PaperTerminalVelocityCurl: The global velocity estimate involves no sum of gradients. At the level of (5.44), the oscillation has size $\lambda_j^{-5/4}$ and a first derivative bounded by $\lambda_j^{1/4}$, up to parent powers. The frequency grows much faster than the parent factors. This explains how the former estimate gives summability while the central derivative, whose lower bound requires the separate projection argument, can grow without bound.
e03-s8-bounded-velocity.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8: The bounded velocity and the diverging curl are properties of the same limit, but they use different estimates.
