Taking the real part cannot increase the kernel's absolute mass, and for the even symbol in Appendix B it gives the ordinary real cutoff. This estimate applies to an essentially bounded measurable input.
e03-appb-operator-bounds.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_holder: Apply the same convolution estimate to $f(\cdot+z)-f$, using $S_\Lambda(f(\cdot+z))=(S_\Lambda f)(\cdot+z)$. Dividing by $|z|^{1/2}$ and taking the supremum over $z\ne0$ bounds the Hölder seminorm with exactly the same kernel mass as for the value bound.
e03-appb-operator-bounds.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_B_1: A pointwise bound controls the convolution of $f$, and the half-Hölder bound controls the convolution of every translate difference $f(\cdot+z)-f$. Both use the same kernel mass. Thus the bound survives even when the number of modes of the cutoff increases without limit. The real-velocity clause uses continuous inputs; a separate theorem treats measurable real inputs.

e03-appb-bernstein.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_bernstein_real_m: The residual has frequencies up to $4\Lambda$. Reproduce it with $S_{4\Lambda}$, whose symbol equals one on that entire band, then differentiate the reproducing kernel rather than the residual. Its order-$m$ derivative has $L^1$ norm $C_m(4\Lambda)^m$. This proves (B.1) with the factor $4^m$ absorbed in the constant; the formal real-target version tests support against continuous linear functionals.
e03-appb-bernstein.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_bernstein: An ordered list of $m$ coordinate derivatives can represent the same multi-index in several ways. The linked complex Banach-valued estimate bounds the sum with these repetitions; dropping them gives (B.1). A separate version proves the multi-index estimate for real normed targets.
e03-appb-bernstein.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_B_1: Use the plateau at scale $4\Lambda$ to reproduce the entire band-limited input before placing the derivatives on the kernel. The formal Bernstein clause has the paper's multi-index sum and real normed-target generality, with even symbols and positive scales.

e03-appb-tail.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_tail: Set $k=M-s$. For $k>0$ the moments through degree $k-1$ reproduce the Taylor polynomial of the input; only its remainder contributes to $(\operatorname{Id}-S_\Lambda)f$. The $k$th absolute kernel moment costs $\Lambda^{-k}$. At $s=M$ there is no spare derivative, so the estimate is just boundedness of the difference, not a decay estimate.
e03-appb-tail.TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalfNorm_realVec: For real velocities the estimate applies to the Fourier tail itself, including its spatial increments. The plateau is used for cancellation, so evenness is unnecessary for the estimate of the real-part cutoff; the linked theorem assumes a positive scale and the stated regularity of the velocity.
e03-appb-tail.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_B_1: If $\|V\|_{C^{P,1/2}}\le\lambda^{2(P+1)}$, as in the hierarchy, the cutoff at $\Lambda=\lambda^5$ gives $\|V-S_\Lambda V\|_{C^{s,1/2}}\le C_P\lambda^{-3P+5s+2}$. Increasing the depth thus buys three powers of $\lambda^{-1}$ per additional derivative at fixed $s$, even though the uncut approximation is becoming more oscillatory.

e03-appb-uniform-constants.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_bernstein_real_m: The Bernstein constant is obtained by summing the absolute integrals of the derivatives of the one fixed kernel $K$, with the factor $4^m$ from using $S_{4\Lambda}$. In particular, it does not depend on the number of Fourier modes of the parent or on the target space.
e03-appb-uniform-constants.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_tail: The constant in (B.2) can be taken to dominate the finitely many absolute moments of the fixed kernel through order $M$, the Taylor and derivative-sum constants, and the operator bound for $s=M$. It is chosen before $f$ and $\Lambda$. Thus the cutoff cost at depth $M$ is eligible for the numerical threshold in Appendix C.
e03-appb-uniform-constants.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_B_1: One fixes the constants from the symbol before choosing the frequencies. The $L^1$ mass gives the operator bound, derivatives of the kernel give $C_m$ in (B.1), and a maximum over the finitely many moments through order $M$ and the operator bound gives $C_M$ in (B.2). These can all be included in $\mathcal B$ before the schedule is chosen.
e03-appb-uniform-constants.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_B_1: The proof obtains its constants from the fixed kernel and finitely many derivative or moment integrals. The scale dependence has already been removed by dilation. Thus changing $\Lambda$ at each step of the construction requires no change of these constants.

e03-r2-appb-proof-symmetries.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_B_1: On the Fourier side, both differentiation and divergence are multiplications by components of $2\pi i\xi$, and reflection sends $\xi$ to $-\xi$. The scalar, even multiplier commutes with each of these operations. For the time derivative the corresponding fact is that the cutoff is fixed on the stage interval.

e03-r2-appb-proof-support.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_B_1: Outside $|\xi|\le2\Lambda$ the coefficient $\psi(\xi/\Lambda)$ vanishes, independently of the input. The support conclusion is proved for both complex fields and real velocities, for every positive scale.

e03-r2-appb-kernel-definition.TorusEuler.cutoffSchwartzKernel: The inverse Fourier transform of a smooth compactly supported symbol is Schwartz. Its rapid decay gives the finite kernel mass, derivative integrals and absolute moments used in the following three estimates. The Lean kernel is complex-valued; its real interpretation follows from evenness of the symbol.

e03-r2-appb-kernel-dilation.TorusEuler.scaledLiftKernel: Under dilation the mass stays fixed, while derivatives and moments scale in opposite directions. In particular $\|\partial^\beta K_\Lambda\|_1=\Lambda^{|\beta|}\|\partial^\beta K\|_1$ and $\int |y|^k|K_\Lambda(y)|\,dy=\Lambda^{-k}\int |y|^k|K(y)|\,dy$. These are the two scale factors in (B.1) and (B.2).

e03-r2-appb-convolution-representation.TorusEuler.liftConvolution_cutoffSchwart: There is no need to compare the number of torus lattice points with a Euclidean volume. The periodic lift retains the discrete modes, and convolution on $\mathbb R^3$ acts on each by $\widehat K_\Lambda(\xi)=\psi(\xi/\Lambda)$. Thus the desired torus operator is represented by a kernel with scale-independent mass on $\mathbb R^3$.

e03-appb-convolution-bound.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_sup: Taking the supremum after the convolution gives $\|S_\Lambda f\|_\infty\le\|K_\Lambda\|_1\|f\|_\infty$. The bound is uniform in the scale by dilation. This declaration is for continuous fields and does not yet use increments.
e03-appb-convolution-bound.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_sup: Taking the real-velocity norm inside the kernel integral gives the uniform estimate with the same mass bound. The Hölder part is obtained by applying that argument to differences of translates.
e03-appb-convolution-bound.TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_aeBound: A torus null set in the input lifts to a periodic null set in $\mathbb R^3$. Its translate in the kernel integral is still null for each $x$. Thus the a.e. bound on the input gives a pointwise bound on the output of the finite Fourier cutoff.
e03-appb-convolution-bound.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_B_1: For the supremum estimate integrate the values, and for the Hölder estimate integrate $f(x+z-y)-f(x-y)$ before dividing by $|z|^{1/2}$. The mass is scale independent. The theorem packages both estimates, with continuous real velocities and measurable complex Banach-valued inputs in their respective clauses.

e03-appb-kernel-derivative-scale.TorusEuler.integral_norm_iteratedFDeriv_: For $|\beta|=m$, $\partial^\beta K_{4\Lambda}(y)=(4\Lambda)^{3+m}(\partial^\beta K)(4\Lambda y)$. Changing variables removes the factor $(4\Lambda)^3$. The formal identity also gives this scaling for the norm of the derivative tensor on any specified list of directions.
e03-appb-kernel-derivative-scale.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_B_1: The identity leaves the factor $(4\Lambda)^{|\beta|}$ when derivatives are moved to the kernel of the reproducing cutoff. Summing these bounds gives (B.1), absorbing $4^{|\beta|}$ in $C_m$. The linked full lemma gives Bernstein, rather than stating the kernel identity separately.

e03-r2-appb-taylor-remainder.TorusEuler.norm_sub_liftConvolution_scal: For $k=M-s>0$, expand each $\partial^\beta f(x-y)$, $|\beta|\le s$, in $y$ through degree $k-1$. The integral of every nonconstant Taylor term vanishes. The remainder uses derivatives of order $|\beta|+k\le M$, which explains why the order-$s$ tail gains precisely $M-s$ powers of $\Lambda^{-1}$.

For the half-Hölder part, apply the Taylor estimate to $\partial^\beta f(\cdot+z)-\partial^\beta f$ before dividing by $|z|^{1/2}$. Its $k$th derivative, with $k=M-s$, has uniform norm bounded by $|z|^{1/2}$ times an order-$M$ Hölder bound. Thus no extra spatial derivative or extra factor of $\Lambda$ is spent to estimate the half-Hölder tail.
e03-r2-appb-taylor-remainder.TorusEuler.integral_scaledCutoffSchwartz: Fourier inversion gives $\int K_\Lambda=\psi(0)$ independently of the positive scale. Here $\psi(0)=1$ by the plateau; hence the constant Taylor term reproduces $f(x)$. No evenness is needed for this mass identity.

Reflection symmetry would cancel odd moments but not even ones. Instead the plateau gives $\partial^\beta\widehat K_\Lambda(0)=0$ for every $|\beta|>0$, so all the corresponding kernel moments vanish. This is the cancellation needed for an arbitrarily high-order tail bound.
e03-r2-appb-taylor-remainder.TorusEuler.integral_norm_pow_scaledLiftK: Set $z=\Lambda y$ in the absolute moment integral. The Jacobian cancels $\Lambda^3$ and $|y|^k$ becomes $\Lambda^{-k}|z|^k$. The Schwartz kernel makes both integrals finite; the formal scaling identity is also expressed for arbitrary kernels under its integral convention.

e03-appc-admissible-order.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_order_steps: At step $j$ the choice of $q_{j+1}$ is made using the already available $\lambda_{j-1}$. For $j\ge2$, the preceding choice gave $\mathcal B(q_j)\le\lambda_{j-2}\le\lambda_{j-1}$; for $j=1$ use $\mathcal B(1)\le N$. Thus increasing the analytic constants cannot make the current order inadmissible.

e03-appc-threshold.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_order_advan: The maximum defining $q_{j+1}$ is taken using $\lambda_{j-1}$, before the next frequency $\lambda_j$ is chosen. Since $q_j$ is already admissible, the only test is whether $\mathcal B(q_j+1)\le\lambda_{j-1}$. This prevents choosing an order whose analytic constants the current parent cannot yet absorb.
e03-appc-threshold.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_order_steps: Since the maximum has upper endpoint $q_j+1$ and already contains $q_j$, no other value of $q_{j+1}$ is possible. This conclusion is independent of how large $\mathcal B(q_j+1)$ is.

e03-appc-frequency-growth.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_frequency_t: In the recurrence $\lambda_{j+1}=\lambda_j^{K(q_{j+1})}$, $K(q_{j+1})\ge2$. Thus $\lambda_j\ge N^{2^j}$ when $N>1$. The frequency-growth theorem needs only the power recurrence and this lower bound on the exponents, not the maximum rule for the orders.

e03-appc-order-growth.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_order_tends: For any integer $s$, if the nondecreasing order sequence remained below $s$, it would eventually be constant, say at $r<s$. But $\lambda_{j-1}\to\infty$ eventually makes the single fixed threshold $\mathcal B(r+1)$ admissible, forcing another increase. No upper bound on the growth of $\mathcal B$ is needed.

e03-appc-three-steps.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_three_log_s: The wave after step $j$ has seed scale $e^{-L_{j+1}}=\lambda_{j+2}^{-4}$. Controlling its logarithm using the frequency of the parent at step $j$ requires three successive powers: $L_{j+1}=4K_{j+2}K_{j+1}K_j\log\lambda_{j-1}$. This accounts for the cubic, rather than linear, floor in the threshold.

e03-r2-appc-exponent-monotonicity.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_log_bound: The bounds $q_j\le q_{j+1}$ and $q_{j+2}\le q_{j+1}+1$ place all three factors below $K(q_{j+1}+1)$. Cubing that common bound prepares the threshold inequality; this is an intermediate step in the linked logarithmic estimate.

e03-appc-floor.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_log_bound: The schedule gives $\log\mathcal B(q_{j+1})\le\log\lambda_{j-1}$, while the floor gives $4K(q_{j+1}+1)^3\le\log\mathcal B(q_{j+1})$. Each of the three frequency exponents is at most $K(q_{j+1}+1)$. In the expression for $L_{j+1}$ their product therefore costs at most one extra factor $\log\lambda_{j-1}$.
e03-appc-floor.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_1_3: Lemma 1.3 combines two distinct facts: admissibility lets the order increase slowly but without bound, and the cubic threshold floor controls the three-step logarithmic growth. The theorem assumes the initial order and maximum rule; monotonicity of $\mathcal B$ and domination of the analytic costs are additional choices in the paper, not needed for this arithmetic result.

e03-appc-cubic-floor.TorusEuler.frequencySchedule_log_bound: Even in the fastest permitted order growth, $K_j,K_{j+1},K_{j+2}\le K(q_{j+1}+1)$. The floor in $\mathcal B(q_{j+1})$ bounds four times their product by $\log\lambda_{j-1}$, since the threshold has already been met. This makes $L_{j+1}\le(\log\lambda_{j-1})^2$ available before the next wave is constructed.

r5-app-weighted-directions.TorusEuler.hierarchyMixedDirection: In the independent variables $(a,s)$ a derivative of a localized envelope can cost $\ell_*^{-1}$, while a derivative of its periodic profile can cost $h^{-1}$. Use the commuting directions $\ell_*\partial_{a_i}$ and $h\partial_s$ to count these as unit costs. A derivative in physical position also differentiates the carried phase; that conversion is separate.
r5-app-weighted-directions.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.fieldNorm: In a mixed derivative of order $(\beta,j)$ the constant scales can be pulled out, giving $\ell_*^{|\beta|}h^j$. Summing over the mixed multi-indices and taking suprema on the specified time set gives the unweighted norm. Finiteness of each derivative supremum is required.

r5-app-fixed-parent-power.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3: Apply the zero-order estimate to one scaled derivative of $v$. The new source contains $\ell_*\partial_{a_i}c_\nu$ times $v$, and its contribution is multiplied by $C_{\rm low}b_\nu$. The condition (D.7) bounds this combined coefficient independently of the parent. Repeated differentiation therefore does not raise the original inverse cost to a power proportional to the derivative order.
r5-app-fixed-parent-power.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_13: For the mean, differentiation of the integrated equation leaves a forcing term with a derivative on $K$ or $\Omega$. The time integral of the latter has length at most one. By D.2(c) and (D.2) the weighted positive-order Hölder norms of these coefficients are bounded by a parent power times $\ell_*^{1/2}$. Choose the radius exponent to pay for the inverse bound $A$ in (5.13); this works at all orders without requiring $K$ or $\Omega$ themselves to be small.

e03-appd-exact-order-norm.TorusEuler.appendixCoefficientMultiIndex: Here $|c|_m$ is a sum over derivatives of exact order $m$. In particular $|c|_0$ need not be small when the positive-order terms of the finite norm are small. This distinction is used in (D.7), which involves only $m\ge1$.
e03-appd-exact-order-norm.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.coefficientOr: The exact-order quantity sums one supremum for each label multi-index $|\beta|=m$; no lower derivatives are included. This definition works for a phase-independent field in any real normed space. Smoothness and boundedness are separate hypotheses.

e03-appd-field-norm.TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm: For instance, $\ell_*h\partial_{a_1}\partial_s f$ is a term of order two, and so is $\ell_*^2\partial_{a_1}\partial_{a_2} f$. The scaled directions used in Lean encode these factors directly. A word sum counts different orderings of the same commuting derivatives, which can be compared with the multi-index sum using constants depending only on the order.
e03-appd-field-norm.TorusEuler.hierarchyMixedDirection: The four scaled directions account for all factors $\ell_*^{|\beta|}h^j$. Their definition does not yet take the finite derivative sum or normalize by the time-dependent amplitude.
e03-appd-field-norm.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.fieldNorm: At order $n=1$, the norm is $\sup|f|+\ell_*\sum_i\sup|\partial_{a_i}f|+h\sup|\partial_s f|$. The higher-order definition includes each mixed multi-index through total order $n$, taking the supremum of each derivative separately.
e03-appd-field-norm.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.weightedField: On the active interval the bound $\|f\|_{[0],\gamma}\le A$ means $|f(t,a,s)|\le A\gamma(t)$ at each time. The small amplitude on the switching interval is therefore retained when the profile is read on the graph. The definition normalizes by the actual positive weight, not by its maximum over time.

r5-app-weighted-time-domain.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.weightedField: The weight is the seed amplitude at the time at which the profile is evaluated. Thus a bound by $A$ in the weighted norm gives $|f(t,a,s)|\le A\gamma(t)$ throughout the active interval, including near activation. A uniform unweighted bound at the final amplitude would not give that conclusion. The mean need not vanish at activation and is estimated without this weight.
r5-app-weighted-time-domain.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_1: The estimates hold with any positive time weight, since only label and phase differentiation is involved. Choosing the seed amplitude and active interval gives the application to the oscillation; no time derivative of the amplitude is involved in Lemma D.1.

e03-r2-appd-phase-independent-norm.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.fieldNorm_pha: A phase-independent field $c$ has $\partial_s^j c=0$ for $j>0$. Its norm consequently contains no power of $h$, and evaluation at the physical phase introduces no fast oscillatory derivative. Only the label scale and the parent deformation enter the physical derivative bound.

e03-r2-appd-holder-norm-definition.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.holderOrderNo: The exact-order Hölder expression sums a $C^{0,1/2}$ quantity for each derivative of order $m$. Lean combines the uniform norm and seminorm by a maximum; their sum is between that maximum and twice it, so the unspecified constants in the paper absorb the convention.
e03-r2-appd-holder-norm-definition.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.holderFieldNo: The weighted Hölder norm pays $\ell_*^m$ for derivatives of order $m$, including their spatial increments. Each summand uses the maximum of its uniform and half-Hölder parts. Replacing that maximum by their sum changes the full expression by at most a factor two.

Group the finite label-derivative sum by $m=|\beta|$. The weight is the same within each group, so the result is $\sum_{m\le n}\ell_*^m|c|_{m,1/2}$, with the formal maximum convention for the individual Hölder norms.

e03-r2-appd-holder-interpolation.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.norm_sub_sqrt_o: For $r=|a-b|$, the two bounds on the increment are $2\|v\|_\infty$ and $r\|Dv\|_\infty$. The smaller is at most their geometric mean. Dividing by $r^{1/2}$ eliminates the separation and gives a bound for the half-Hölder seminorm using just the value and first derivative bounds.
e03-r2-appd-holder-interpolation.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_D_2: Apply the geometric-mean bound to every derivative of order $m$ and sum. Cauchy–Schwarz pairs the order-$m$ supremum sum with the order-$(m+1)$ sum. This is the interpolation step used in the proof of (D.2), whose stated conclusion is the finite-norm comparison.

e03-appd-holder-comparison.TorusEuler.paperAppendixD_holderComparis: The mean inverse is bounded on $C^{0,1/2}$, not merely in supremum norm. To use it at label order $n$ with supremum bounds on the source, (D.2) supplies the missing seminorm from order $n+1$. Its factor $\ell_*^{-1/2}$ is paid once in the conversion. The standalone comparison assumes the Hölder quantities finite; the full formal statement also establishes finiteness.
e03-appd-holder-comparison.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_D_2: Writing $A_m=\ell_*^m|c|_m$, the weighted half-Hölder seminorm at order $m$ is bounded by $C\ell_*^{-1/2}(A_m A_{m+1})^{1/2}$. The arithmetic-geometric mean inequality and summation give (D.2). Thus a half-Hölder estimate uses one additional derivative in the supremum norm and costs half an inverse radius. Lean proves finiteness and the comparison with an explicit constant $4$ in its norm convention.
e03-appd-holder-comparison.TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_D_2: The lower comparison follows by dropping the increment part. For the upper comparison, a half derivative is paid for by the geometric mean of adjacent derivative orders and costs at most $\ell_*^{-1/2}$ in the scaled norm. Lean proves finiteness as well as the two inequalities.

e03-appd-derivative-product.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_derivatives: When one additional label derivative is removed from the norm at order $n+1$, it costs $\ell_*^{-1}$. Each resulting multi-index was counted at most three times, once for each possible final label direction. The phase index has only one such predecessor and costs exactly $h^{-1}$.
e03-appd-derivative-product.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_product: In a Leibniz term the label and phase weights split exactly: $\ell_*^{|\beta|}h^j=(\ell_*^{|\beta'|}h^{j'})(\ell_*^{|\beta-\beta'|}h^{j-j'})$. Normalize only the second factor by $\gamma(t)$. Each input is needed through at most order $n$, with no additional derivative. The operator norm of the bilinear action is included in the bound.
e03-appd-derivative-product.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_1: The derivative estimates spend one order and one inverse length. The product estimate spends no additional order because every Leibniz term uses derivatives whose total is at most $n$. The formal lemma assumes positive scales and weight, bounded normalized derivatives at the indicated orders, and allows continuous bilinear products.
e03-appd-derivative-product.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_1: In (D.3), the label and phase shifts cost different inverse lengths. In (D.4), the product keeps its full derivative budget, because the weight and every derivative split between the factors. The theorem also supplies boundedness of the output families, under the corresponding bounded input derivatives.

e03-appd-phase-operators.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_phaseAverage: Averaging commutes with label derivatives, and the average of a positive phase derivative is zero by periodicity. Hence the average has no greater finite norm than the profile. Removing it costs at most two and gives the zero-mean forcing required for the periodic primitive. The linked statement is unweighted; apply it to $f/\gamma(t)$ for the weighted version.
e03-appd-phase-operators.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_phasePrimitive: The integral from zero is periodic because a full-period integral of $f$ vanishes. Subtracting its average fixes its constant and does not change its derivative. On a period the integral and its average are each bounded by $\sup|f|$, giving constant two independently of $h$. The operation therefore solves for an oscillatory primitive without a derivative loss.
e03-appd-phase-operators.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_1: The time weight can be placed inside every phase operation. Averaging is a contraction; removing the average costs at most two; the normalized primitive of a zero-mean input costs at most two. Positive phase derivatives of the primitive are derivatives of the input one order lower, or equivalently commute with the primitive on centered periodic fields.
e03-appd-phase-operators.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_1: The phase integral runs over an interval of length one, so averaging has constant one and subtraction has constant two. The zero-mean primitive has the same bound two when the input has zero mean. The formal result requires bounded normalized mixed derivatives, positive scales and weight, and a smooth period-one real Banach-valued profile.

e03-appd-holder-product.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_product: For a bilinear action $B$, write its increment as $B(f(x),g(x)-g(y))+B(f(x)-f(y),g(y))$. This gives $[B(f,g)]_{1/2}\le\|B\|(\|f\|_\infty[g]_{1/2}+[f]_{1/2}\|g\|_\infty)$. Applied to each Leibniz term, it gives the product estimate at the same finite order in the Hölder norm.
e03-appd-holder-product.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_1: Leibniz' rule gives the derivative products, and splitting their spatial increments gives the Hölder product inequality. The theorem handles continuous bilinear products with their operator norms and uses a maximum for the two Hölder contributions; the paper's unspecified constant absorbs an equivalent convention.

e03-r2-appd-derivative-count.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_1: A multi-index of order at most $n+1$ can arise by adding one of three coordinate directions to an index of order at most $n$. Hence its multiplicity is at most three. The phase shift has multiplicity at most one. The proof uses this counting to obtain the derivative clauses of Lemma D.1.

e03-appd-product-proof.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_product: Write the normalized product as $B(f,g/\gamma)$, since $\gamma$ depends only on time. Each Leibniz term then has its weights divided between the two differentiated inputs. The theorem bounds the sum of these terms rather than asserting the product-rule identity itself.
e03-appd-product-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_1: The weight is attached to whichever factor is measured relative to the amplitude. For example $fg/\gamma=f(g/\gamma)$, and no label or phase derivative falls on $\gamma$. This is how the proof obtains the weighted product clause of Lemma D.1.

e03-appd-average-contraction.TorusEuler.norm_phaseMean_le: The norm of the phase integral is at most the integral of the norm. The interval has length one, so a bound $M$ for the integrand gives the same bound for the mean. The paper's smooth profiles supply the required integrability.

e03-appd-primitive-definition.TorusEuler.phasePrimitive: For a centered periodic source, integration from $0$ gives a periodic primitive. There remains one arbitrary constant; subtract the average of the primitive to choose the unique one with zero mean. Thus the inverse of $\partial_s$ on centered profiles neither introduces a mean component nor requires a choice of phase origin in the result.
e03-appd-primitive-definition.TorusEuler.periodic_phasePrimitive: The increment $G(s+1)-G(s)$ is the integral of $f$ over a full period, hence zero when $f$ is periodic and centered. Subtracting a constant preserves that periodicity. The linked theorem gives this part of the primitive construction; the ordinary integral interpretation uses a Banach target.
e03-appd-primitive-definition.TorusEuler.phaseMean_phasePrimitive: Integrating $G-\langle G\rangle_s$ over a unit interval gives zero. This normalization does not require $f$ itself to be centered or periodic; those hypotheses are needed to make $G$ periodic, not to make the normalized primitive have zero mean.
e03-appd-primitive-definition.TorusEuler.hasDerivAt_phasePrimitive: By the fundamental theorem of calculus $G'=f$ for continuous Banach-valued $f$. The subtracted mean is constant in $s$, so it has zero derivative. The other primitive properties use the separately stated centering and periodicity conditions.

e03-appd-primitive-sup.TorusEuler.norm_phasePrimitive_le: By periodicity it suffices to estimate $G$ on $[0,1]$, where $|G(s)|\le M$. Its mean also has norm at most $M$, giving $|G-\langle G\rangle_s|\le2M$. The zero mean of $f$ ensures that this bound extends to all real phases.

e03-appd-power-condition.TorusEuler.FiniteCoefficientMultiIndexPo: The coefficient condition separates growth with order from growth with the parent. The numbers $C_m$ can be arbitrary, but $C$ is fixed in $|c|_m\le C_m\mathsf D^{C(m+1)}$. Multiplication by $\ell_*^m$ gives $C_m\mathsf D^C(\ell_*\mathsf D^C)^m$. A single radius therefore controls the parent power at every label order.
e03-appd-power-condition.TorusEuler.finiteCoefficientPower_iff_mu: In three dimensions, each coordinate partial derivative is an evaluation of the full derivative tensor, while the tensor norm is bounded by a finite order-dependent sum of its coordinate components. Thus the two polynomial coefficient conditions are equivalent after changing the constants; neither implies the analytic bound without one of the conditions as input.
e03-appd-power-condition.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.CoefficientPo: The constants $C_m$ may grow with order without any prescribed growth law; the exponent $C$ must remain fixed for the coefficient. When $\mathsf D\ge1$, rounding the exponent upward gives the formal integer-power condition. The radius must subsequently be chosen for that enlarged exponent.

r5-app-coefficient-hypotheses.TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.CoefficientPo: The exponent $C$ is fixed for a coefficient, and the numbers $C_m$ may depend on the order. The bounds in (D.6) are uniform in time but concern only derivatives in $a$. In particular they do not bound derivatives in time; those are obtained separately in the auxiliary note.
r5-app-coefficient-hypotheses.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_2: Lemma D.2 chooses the output constants uniformly before the parent parameter and fields. It applies to products via bounded bilinear maps, and to inverses in complete real normed algebras with pointwise inverse control. The exponent is an integer; the paper's real exponents may be enlarged for these polynomial bounds.

e03-appd-product-coeff.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_mul_multiIndex: An order-$m$ Leibniz term pairs orders $r$ and $m-r$. The product of their parent powers is $\mathsf D^{C(m+2)}\le\mathsf D^{2C(m+1)}$ for $\mathsf D\ge1$. Thus the exponent doubles at most once, regardless of the number of derivatives. The uniform choice of order constants is made explicit in the full formal Lemma D.2.
e03-appd-product-coeff.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_mul: The operator-norm version of the product estimate uses the same Leibniz splitting of derivative orders. Its polynomial exponent can be enlarged independently of $m$, but this standalone result chooses constants after the inputs and parent parameter; the full lemma makes their uniformity explicit.
e03-appd-product-coeff.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_2: If the two input exponents are $q,r$, every Leibniz term is bounded by a power with exponent at most $\max(q,r)(m+2)\le2\max(q,r)(m+1)$. The formal lemma proves uniform output constants with exponent $2\max(q,r)$ for a bilinear action of norm at most one.
e03-appd-product-coeff.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_2: For the matrix product the derivative orders add, so the two input powers can be replaced by one common exponent $2\max(q,r)$. The theorem proves the bound uniformly before the fields and parent parameter; integer exponents suffice after upward rounding of the paper's exponents.

e03-appd-inverse-coeff.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_inverse_multiInd: The identity $c^{-1}c=I$ gives $\partial_i c^{-1}=-c^{-1}(\partial_i c)c^{-1}$. The inverse must already be controlled at order zero: bounded derivatives of $c$ alone do not prevent it from approaching a singular element. The same identity iterated bounds all higher inverse derivatives.
e03-appd-inverse-coeff.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_inverse: Differentiating $ce=I$ with $e=c^{-1}$ always leaves $cD^me$ as the only term with $m$ derivatives on $e$. Multiplying by $e$ expresses $D^me$ in terms of lower derivatives of $e$ and positive derivatives of $c$. Thus the independent bound on $e$ at order zero starts the induction; coefficient regularity alone would not supply it. The standalone theorem fixes its constants after the input, unlike the uniform full lemma.
e03-appd-inverse-coeff.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_2: Take $C$ to dominate both the exponent for $c$ and the bound $|c^{-1}|\le\mathsf D^C$. A term with $k$ positive derivatives of $c$ (of total order $m$) contains $k+1$ inverse factors, hence has power at most $\mathsf D^{C(m+2k+1)}\le\mathsf D^{C(3m+1)}$. This proves (D.6) with exponent $3C$; the formal theorem chooses $C=\max(a,e)$ for the integer input exponents and works in a complete real normed algebra.
e03-appd-inverse-coeff.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_2: Control of the inverse is a separate hypothesis, $\|c^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D^e$, in addition to the derivative bounds for $c$. Lemma D.2 then gives a common enlarged exponent for all inverse derivatives, with uniform constants. The formal algebra and integer-exponent conventions differ from the matrix and real-exponent formulation.

e03-appd-radius-coeff.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_weighted_multiIn: After scaling the derivative, the bound reads $C_m\mathsf D^C(\ell_*\mathsf D^C)^m$. For $m\ge1$, keep one factor $\ell_*\mathsf D^C$ and use $\ell_*\mathsf D^C\le1$ on the rest. This gives the stronger bound $C_m\ell_*\mathsf D^{2C}$ needed to compensate a subsequent application of the inverse.
e03-appd-radius-coeff.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_weighted: The factor $\ell_*$ in the positive-order bound must be kept: bounding every factor $\ell_*\mathsf D^C$ by one would prove the first assertion but would not compensate the inverse in Lemma D.3. No smallness of the zero-order coefficient is needed.
e03-appd-radius-coeff.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_2: D.2(c) is stronger than boundedness of the scaled coefficient norm: for $m\ge1$ it retains $\ell_*^m|c|_m\le C_m\mathsf D^{2a}\ell_*$ with integer $a$ in Lean. The zero-order term has size $C_0\mathsf D^a$ and is not part of the smallness condition. If an exponent is enlarged after multiplication or inversion, impose the radius restriction with the new exponent.
e03-appd-radius-coeff.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_2: The same choice of radius works at every derivative order: each extra factor $\ell_*\mathsf D^a$ is at most one. Reserving one such factor at positive order gives $\ell_*\mathsf D^{2a}$, with no dependence on $m$ in its exponent. The constants $C_m$ may still depend on $m$.

e03-r2-appd-product-coeff-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_2: In each Leibniz term, the two factors of $\mathsf D^C$ independent of order survive the splitting, giving $C(m+2)$ in the exponent. Since $m+2\le2(m+1)$, a new common exponent $2C$ suffices. The full formal lemma generalizes to unequal integer exponents using their maximum.

e03-r2-appd-inverse-coeff-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_2: With $e=c^{-1}$, the term $c\partial^\beta e$ in the differentiated identity $ce=I$ is moved to the left and multiplied by $e$. A term with $i$ derivatives on $c$ then has exponent $C+C(i+1)+C(3(m-i)+1)=C(3m-2i+3)\le C(3m+1)$ for $i\ge1$. Thus the proposed exponent closes the induction starting from $|e|_0\le\mathsf D^C$.

e03-r2-appd-radius-coeff-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_2: Writing the scaled bound as $C_m\mathsf D^C(\ell_*\mathsf D^C)^m$ explains both estimates at once. If $m\ge1$, keep one of the factors $\ell_*\mathsf D^C$ and bound the rest by one. The formal proof uses the same factorization with its integer exponent.

e03-appd-positive-coefficient.TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_equati:
For one label derivative the equation reads $\mathcal L(\partial_{a_i}v)=\partial_{a_i}F-\sum_
u T_
u((\partial_{a_i}c_
u)v)$. The same operator acts on $\partial_{a_i}v$, and all new terms on the right contain a derivative of a coefficient. Repetition gives the lower-order terms in the lifting estimate.

e03-appd-lifting-equation.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD3_lifting: Lemma D.3 is an a priori estimate for a solution of the given equation, not a construction of the inverse. Its input is a zero-order estimate valid throughout the admissible space. Its output is the finite derivative estimate with that same inverse cost, using commutation for the constant operators and the product rule for the coefficient actions.
e03-appd-lifting-equation.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3: For the mean the constraint belongs to the displacement $z$, with $z(0)=z(T)=0$ and $v=z_t$. The integrated equation contains $Kv$ and the time integral of $\Omega v$, modulo a label gradient. Taking a label derivative preserves the constraints and produces the same integrated equation for the differentiated unknown, with a new forcing. The inverse from the preceding section supplies existence; D.3 estimates such solutions.

e03-appd-lifting-commutation.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD3_lifting: The fixed linear maps must commute with differentiation, but the variable multiplication $v\mapsto c_\nu v$ does not. Its commutator is precisely the forcing term with a derivative on $c_\nu$. The abstract formal hypotheses encode the principal commutation and the Leibniz identities for the coefficient actions.
e03-appd-lifting-commutation.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3: For a coefficient action, the formal commutation hypothesis is the product rule $D_F(T(c,v))=T(D_Ac,v)+T(c,D_Ev)$. It is the constant part $\mathcal L_0$ that commutes without a correction. Thus the assumptions identify exactly the new forcing terms under differentiation.

e03-r2-appd-constraint-subspace.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3: The differentiation must preserve the space on which the zero-order inverse is available. In the mean problem, label derivatives preserve both the divergence constraint and the endpoint values of the displacement. In the transverse problem this is why one works in fixed coordinates as in (5.18): direct differentiation of $\kappa\cdot V=0$ introduces the inhomogeneous constraint $\kappa\cdot\partial_{a_i}V=-(\partial_{a_i}\kappa)\cdot V$.

e03-appd-low-order.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD3_lifting:
The estimate must hold for every admissible solution, not just for the one being differentiated. Indeed $\partial_{a_i}v$ solves the same equation with forcing $\partial_{a_i}F-\sum_
u T_
u((\partial_{a_i}c_
u)v)$ and the differentiated data. The original wording needs this universal reading for the next use of the zero-order inverse.
e03-appd-low-order.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3: “For every admissible source” means the same nonnegative $C_{\rm low}$ bounds every unknown in the solution space with its own forcing and prescribed data. Under (D.7) through order $n$, the statement bounds the order-$n$ solution norm by $C_n C_{\rm low}$ times the order-$n$ norm of the forcing and data.

e03-r2-appd-lifting-operator-norm.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3: For the mean, time integration costs at most $T\le1$ in the spatial Hölder norm. The coefficient action also includes multiplication by the differentiated coefficient and, if the equation is projected, the Leray projection. In the formal abstraction $b_\nu$ bounds the whole bilinear action in the chosen zero-order seminorms, so every such fixed operator cost must be included before using (D.7).

e03-appd-slow-bound.TorusEuler.appendixSlowCoefficient_word_: For a particular weighted derivative of $c_\nu$ of order $i\ge1$, its norm times $b_\nu C_{\rm low}$ is at most the whole nonnegative sum in (D.7). The word used by the formal proof is one coordinate multi-index after commuting the directions. This gives a bound $C_i$ for each product-rule term, without requiring the coefficients themselves to be small.
e03-appd-slow-bound.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD3_lifting: A derivative of total order at most $n$ can put between one and $n$ derivatives on a coefficient. Every one of these terms is covered by (D.7). The formal word estimate only needs the bound on each such term; it follows from the summed bound by nonnegativity.
e03-appd-slow-bound.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3: In the differentiated equation the product with zero derivatives on $c_\nu$ belongs to the same operator on the new unknown. It is not a term to be bounded perturbatively. Only the terms with $i\ge1$ derivatives on $c_\nu$ are put on the right, and (D.7) pays for the inverse on these terms.

e03-appd-lifted-conclusion.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD3_lifting: For a scaled first derivative the estimate has the form $V_1\le C_{\rm low}F_1+C_1V_0$. The second coefficient is $C_1$, rather than another uncontrolled inverse norm, because (D.7) already includes $C_{\rm low}$. Substituting $V_0\le C_{\rm low}F_0$ gives a single inverse factor. The same argument at order $n$ involves only strictly lower orders of $v$ on the right.
e03-appd-lifted-conclusion.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3:
In the recursion following differentiation, the coefficient of the lower-order norm of $v$ is $C_{m low}\sum_
u b_
u\ell_*^i|c_
u|_i$, with $i\ge1$. Under (D.7) it is an order constant. Thus induction involves powers of these constants, not successive powers of the inverse norm.
e03-appd-lifted-conclusion.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_3: The high-order estimate retains the parent cost of the original inverse. The proof is valid for any finite family of commuting derivatives with the stipulated product rules and seminorms. With the paper's scaled label and phase directions it gives the displayed finite-order bound under (D.7).

e03-r2-appd-lifting-constant-dependence.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3: The constant in the lifted estimate is fixed by the derivative order and the bounds in (D.7). It is not required to be uniform as the order increases. What must be uniform is the power of the parent in $C_{\rm low}$: the new order-dependent constants can enter $\mathcal B$, whereas a new parent power at every hierarchy level would not be paid for by the fixed frequency margin.
e03-r2-appd-lifting-constant-dependence.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_3: Only the target order, coefficient constants through that order and the number of available derivative directions enter the combinatorial constant. Since the latter is fixed in the paper, the constant does not introduce any additional parent power.

e03-r2-appd-lifting-holder-case.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3: Use the zero-order inverse in $C^{0,1/2}$, the Hölder product inequality, and (D.7) with $|c_\nu|_{m,1/2}$. The same recurrence follows. The extra cost of passing from supremum bounds to these Hölder hypotheses is paid separately by (D.2), not by the lifting induction.

e03-appd-differentiated-equation.TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_equati: A derivative word of length $n$ splits into a subword hitting $c_\nu$ and the complementary subword hitting $v$. The empty coefficient subword gives the original operator on the $n$th derivative. For commuting coordinates, grouping the remaining subwords by the number of occurrences of each coordinate gives $\binom{\beta}{\beta'}$ in the display.
e03-appd-differentiated-equation.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_3: The terms with no derivative on a coefficient combine into $\mathcal L\partial^\beta v$. Move the remaining product-rule terms to the forcing side. The full lifting theorem uses this identity; the separate derivative-word theorem states the identity directly.

e03-appd-weights.TorusEuler.appendixFiniteDerivativeNorm_: Since $\ell_*$ and $h$ are constant in label and phase, a product-rule term with $i$ label derivatives on the coefficient carries $\ell_*^i$ there and $\ell_*^{|\beta|-i}h^j$ on the unknown. No phase derivative can hit the phase-independent coefficient. This allocates exactly the weight needed by (D.7).

e03-r2-appd-lifting-recursion.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD3_lifting:
A term with $i$ label derivatives on $c_
u$ carries the factor $\ell_*^i|c_
u|_i$ and involves $V_{n-i}$, not $V_n$. Its coefficient after the zero-order estimate is $C_{m low}b_
u\ell_*^i|c_
u|_i$. Since $i\ge1$, (D.7) bounds it by an order constant and the recurrence closes from lower orders. No smallness condition on the undifferentiated coefficients is needed.

e03-appd-induction.TorusEuler.paperLemmaD3_lifting: After the coefficient sum is bounded by (D.7), the recurrence has the form $V_n\le C_{\rm low}F_n+C_nV_{n-1}$. Since $F_{n-1}\le F_n$, substituting the induction bound for $V_{n-1}$ leaves a single factor $C_{\rm low}$. The remaining constant may grow with order, but it is independent of the parent size.
e03-appd-induction.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_3: Although the zero-order inverse estimate is applied at every order, in the recurrence its additional occurrences are multiplied by the quantities bounded in (D.7). Substituting the lower-order estimates therefore leaves a single $C_{\rm low}$ in front of the source norm. The constants depending on derivative order may enter $\mathcal B$ without changing the parent exponent.

c8-coefficient-radius-gain.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_2: The term needed here is the second estimate of D.2(c), not the bound for the full coefficient norm. For $m\ge1$, $\ell_*^m|c|_m\le C_m\mathsf D^{2C}\ell_*$. The factor $\ell_*$ has been kept precisely because the differentiated coefficient will be multiplied by another inverse bound.

c8-holder-radius-gain.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_13_of: The positive-order estimate of D.2(c) gives a factor $\ell_*$ in both $\ell_*^m|c|_m$ and $\ell_*^{m+1}|c|_{m+1}$ when $m\ge1$. The cost $\ell_*^{-1/2}$ in (D.2) leaves $\ell_*^{1/2}$. This is the gain in (5.13) for $K$ and $\Omega$, whose zero-order inverse is a Hölder estimate.

c8-common-envelope-exponent.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_13: Suppose the weighted positive-order coefficient bound is $C_m\mathsf D^C\ell_*^{1/2}$ and the inverse costs $\mathsf D^{C_A}$. With $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ their product is at most $C_m\mathsf D^{C+C_A-a/2}$. Choose $a\ge2(C+C_A)$, also large enough for D.2(c). The same radius then pays for all orders, since $m$ occurs only in $C_m$.

c8-auxiliary-abstract-extension.TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness: The main paper obtains a limit for $\partial_tu$ away from the origin using the projected equation: the local stress converges in a Hölder norm and the distant stress is handled by the smooth pressure kernel off the diagonal. This does not directly iterate, since higher time derivatives of the distant stress have not been controlled. The auxiliary note obtains these derivatives by estimating the stage increments instead. Its conclusion concerns the velocity, not an Euler solution continued through the singular time.

e03-aux-threshold-choice.TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness: Choose the threshold for the time-jet constants before $N$, along with the original spatial constants. For every fixed time order the schedule eventually permits all the needed estimates. Increasing the threshold does not alter the order-growth argument; it only postpones individual increases. Thus the proof concerns one sequence, rather than constructing a new solution for each time derivative.
e03-aux-threshold-choice.TorusEuler.AuxiliaryTerminalSmoothness: The formal existence assertion first chooses the construction exponent, the threshold and a lower bound on the initial frequency. It then provides a sequence and a singular solution for each sufficiently large $N$. The mixed bounds hold along that sequence at every fixed pair of derivative orders, with starting indices that may depend on the pair. The linked declaration specifies these choices; the proved selected theorem supplies them.
e03-aux-threshold-choice.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Statement.theorem_1: The generalized formal `theorem_1_1` asks for the conclusion for every cutoff and threshold meeting its hypotheses; it is recorded as an open target. The proof of the selected version instead chooses a threshold containing the needed time estimates. That suffices for the existential claim of Remark 1.2.

e03-aux-extension.TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness: The assertion is local smoothness in space and time through the terminal slice, for the very same velocity that becomes singular at the origin. The selected formal result gives a periodic extension on the punctured lift for all real times. Only agreement before $T_*$ is required of that extension; neither Euler nor the pressure is prescribed beyond $T_*$.
e03-aux-extension.TorusEuler.HasSmoothOffOriginExtension: The condition asks for a single periodic smooth field on the punctured periodic lift that agrees with $u$ throughout the physical interval. The extension may be defined for all real times; smoothness is the requirement, not satisfaction of Euler beyond $T_*$. This is a property of a velocity, not its proof.
e03-aux-extension.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Statement.theorem_1: The linked Lean statement requires a smooth extension away from the origin for every qualifying cutoff and threshold. Its conditional proof assumes the still open uniform mixed-derivative statement of auxiliary Lemma 1.2. The Lean proof of Remark 1.2 establishes the paper’s existence conclusion for a selected construction.
e03-aux-extension.TorusEuler.Paper.SmoothTerminalExtension: The extension property is formulated on the periodic lift, with the integer lattice removed. A jointly smooth periodic field near the terminal slice must agree with $u$ on the preterminal punctured slab. The condition imposes no pressure or Euler equation on the extended portion.

e03-aux-retain-main.TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness: The same stage sequence gives both the central vorticity divergence of the main theorem and the mixed limits away from the origin. In particular the accumulation time of the sequence is the maximal lifespan of the velocity being extended. The extra time estimates leave the bounds used to prove blow-up intact.
e03-aux-retain-main.TorusEuler.AuxiliaryTerminalSmoothness: The existence condition retains the main singularity conclusions for the same velocity and time as the extension. It does not include comparison with another maximal solution from the same data. That comparison uses periodic Euler uniqueness in the proved Remark 1.2.
e03-aux-retain-main.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Statement.theorem_1: Although the generalized target lists the retained singularity and uniqueness conclusions, it quantifies over every qualifying cutoff and threshold and is not proved or used. The selected-construction theorem and Remark 1.2 together give the existence conclusion of the auxiliary note.
e03-aux-retain-main.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.remark_1_2: The theorem identifies the maximal solution from the constructed initial data, so the extension is a property of that solution. If another maximal classical solution from the same data is given, periodic Euler uniqueness identifies the two on their common interval, and maximality identifies their lifespans. The formal comparison is for solutions with finite real lifespan.
e03-aux-retain-main.TorusEuler.Paper.remark_1_2: Remark 1.2 combines the singularity conclusions of the selected construction, the smooth terminal extension of its velocity off the origin, and uniqueness among maximal solutions of finite real lifespan from the same data. It is an existence result with the auxiliary strengthening included.

e03-aux-equation-domain.TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution: The Euler equation, divergence condition, smooth periodic velocity and normalized pressure are imposed on $0\le t<T_*$. The derivative at time zero is taken from within that interval. No value at $T_*$ at the origin and no equation beyond $T_*$ are part of this solution condition.
e03-aux-equation-domain.TorusEuler.HasSmoothOffOriginExtension: The extension condition specifies a smooth periodic velocity off the lattice with agreement on the physical interval. It does not impose an equation even there by itself; the separate Euler-solution hypothesis supplies the preterminal equation. In particular the extension is not a continuation of Euler through the singular time.

e03-aux-augment-costs.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step: The enlarged cost table retains the original spatial rows and adds rows summing the absolute values of the terminal costs through the requested time order, including a reserve of spatial orders. Bounding this table controls each individual estimate without cancellation. The original numerical budget survives unchanged, so the auxiliary estimates can be added before choosing $N$ without replacing the main construction.
e03-aux-augment-costs.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.abs_: The finite hierarchy may spend several extra spatial derivatives while passing from one level to the next. The formal table therefore includes indices $m\le7K(s)+r(q,d)$ for time order $q$ and depth $d$, rather than just the final requested order. It uses sums of absolute values so that each needed constant is bounded by the same threshold. This reserve is part of the finite numerical cost, not an extra frequency exponent.
e03-aux-augment-costs.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.TimeDerivativeThres: The inequality $G(7K(s))\le\mathcal B(s)$ is a numerical requirement on the majorant of the time-estimate constants. Once the analytic estimates have provided $G$, it can be included together with the original majorant and the logarithmic floor. The predicate alone does not assert the estimates.
e03-aux-augment-costs.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.exists_threshol: There is no upper growth restriction on $\mathcal B$. Given the two finite-order majorants, take the maximum of their bounds through index $s$, the logarithmic floor $\exp(4K(s+1)^3)$ and a positive lower bound. The resulting nondecreasing threshold merely delays the increases of $q_j$; Appendix C still implies $q_j\to\infty$.

e03-aux-threshold-before-frequency.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.exis: Choosing the majorant after $N$ could make the current order inadmissible. The formal schedule theorem first builds the enlarged threshold from the cost table and then requires $N$ to be above its first value. The subsequent choices of order use the old frequencies and never require revising the threshold.

e03-r2-aux-threshold-growth.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters: Distinguish the fixed time order $q$ from the scheduled spatial order $q_j$. At step $j$ the expansion depth is $P=6K(q_{j+1})$. For any fixed $q$, $P+q+2\le7K(q_{j+1})$ eventually. The inequality (1.1) then bounds the corresponding paper constants by $\mu=\lambda_{j-1}$. The formal threshold also includes the additional finite reserve needed to build the intermediate levels.

e03-aux-same-fields.TorusEuler.AuxiliaryTerminalSmoothness: All the extra estimates apply to the velocities, oscillations and residuals of one selected sequence. Its stage limit is the solution used in the extension proof. The exported existence condition records the estimates and the singular solution at the shared terminal time, but does not itself include an explicit convergence-to-that-solution clause; the assembly proof makes that identification.

e03-aux-slabs-beyond-terminal.TorusEuler.AuxiliaryTerminalSmoothness: The strict inequality $S_j>T_\infty$ ensures that all finitely many early stage terms are smooth even at the terminal slice. The need for a new estimate is entirely in the infinite tail: it must converge there with every fixed mixed derivative. Smoothness of each finite stage alone would not imply smoothness of that sum.

e03-aux-mixed-quantifiers.TorusEuler.auxiliaryLemma12: Fix $m,q$ first; the index $j_{m,q}$ may depend on both and on the chosen construction. The conclusion is a bound on the entire closed child slab for every later stage. It does not assert a finite stage beyond which all orders are bounded simultaneously. This order of quantifiers suffices for smooth convergence on compact subsets.
e03-aux-mixed-quantifiers.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.HasTermi: The numerical condition expresses eventual bounds for each fixed pair $(m,q)$, rather than a bound valid at all orders at any one stage. Since a finite collection of orders has a common late starting stage, it gives the simultaneous estimates needed for any fixed finite mixed norm. Continuity in that norm is supplied separately.
e03-aux-mixed-quantifiers.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Statement.lemma_1_2: The generalized Lemma 1.2 asks for the mixed bounds for every qualifying construction rather than for the selected one. It is an unproved target. The selected-construction theorem proves precisely the eventual estimates required for the convergence argument here.

e03-aux-mixed-display.TorusEuler.auxiliaryLemma12: The quantity that is small is $U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j$, not $U_j-U_{j-1}$ in a global high-order norm. The large central derivatives belong to the localized uncut oscillation $O_j$. The remainder is exactly the mean plus the nonlocal Fourier tail, and its mixed norm is estimated on the whole torus. This is what permits the argument to be restricted to any compact set away from the origin.
e03-aux-mixed-display.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se: For nearby times apply the half-Hölder interpolation inequality to the difference $\partial_t^qf(t)-\partial_t^qf(t')$ and its spatial derivatives. Smoothness of the stage on the compact slab gives uniform continuity through order $m+1$. It follows that the $C^{m,1/2}$ difference tends to zero as $t'\to t$, including at either time endpoint. This establishes continuity in the norm used in (1.2).
e03-aux-mixed-display.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.MixedIncrementBound: At one stage the condition bounds the $q$th Eulerian time derivative of the correction in the spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ norm on $[0,S_j]$ and requires continuity in that norm. The condition does not select the late stage or establish the bound; those are supplied by the selected lemma.

e03-aux-fixed-spatial-point.TorusEuler.slabTimeJet: The derivative here acts on $t\mapsto f(t,x)$ with $x$ fixed. This differs from the profile derivative at fixed Lagrangian label and phase used later. On the positive closed interval the endpoint derivatives are taken from within the interval.

e03-aux-mixed-starting-index.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.HasTermi: For a fixed mixed order $(m,q)$ take the maximum of the finitely many starting indices $j_{m,i}$, $0\le i\le q$, and the support-separation index for $K$. The increment estimate then holds simultaneously for every term of the $C_t^qC_x^m(K)$ norm. No common starting index over all $m,q$ is necessary for smoothness of the limit.

e03-r2-aux-time-step-order.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.Terminal: At time order $q$, the parent equation supplies the $q$th time derivative of the parent velocity from velocity and residual jets through order $q-1$. The mean equation in the child hierarchy then gains one time derivative on its forcing. These two steps are needed together: without the second, construction of the new residual would still require the unavailable $q$th time derivative of the old residual.

e03-aux-time-quantifiers.TorusEuler.auxiliaryLemma13: The same $\psi_q$ and $j_q$ work for the finitely many orders $i\le q$ of the velocity and residual. One may take $\psi_q$ to be an integer by enlarging it, since $\lambda_j\ge1$. No uniformity of the exponent in $q$ is required for smooth extension on a fixed compact set.
e03-aux-time-quantifiers.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Statement.lemma_1_3: The generalized Lemma 1.3 quantifies over every construction with the threshold and step data. It is recorded as unproved and unused. The selected version proves existence of the common integer exponent and starting index for each fixed time order, which is all the induction uses.

e03-aux-time-display.TorusEuler.auxiliaryLemma13: The residual rate is tied to the *next* wave. For the parent $U_{j-1}$ of step $j$, (1.3) gives $\|\partial_t^i R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda_j^{-5/2}$. This is the scale of the stress quadratic in the leading velocity of size $\lambda_j^{-5/4}$. In the induction the parent residual retains this factor through time order $q-1$, not merely a small power of the old frequency.
e03-aux-time-display.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.stageTim: For each specified stage, time and order, take the supremum over the periodic spatial field in the pointwise inequalities. This gives the two numerical norm bounds. The linked theorem does not choose a uniform exponent, provide continuity in time, or prove eventual validity.
e03-aux-time-display.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.StageTim: The fixed-stage condition records the two pointwise estimates for all $i\le q$, with the same exponent on the velocity. The residual rate is $\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$, not a power of $\lambda_j$ alone. The full auxiliary lemma adds time continuity and the eventual choice of stage.
e03-aux-time-display.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.TimeBounds: This condition combines the two numerical bounds through order $q$ at a single stage with continuity in the uniform spatial norm. The exponent is a nonnegative integer. Lemma 1.3 additionally proves that some such exponent works from a sufficiently late index onward.

e03-aux-time-frequency-support.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve: In the Fourier expansion of $U_j$, only the coefficient of each mode depends on time. Differentiation therefore keeps the band $|\xi|\le2\Lambda_j$ at every time order, including one-sided derivatives at the slab endpoints.
e03-aux-time-frequency-support.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_re: The residual is the sum of $\partial_tU_j$ and the projected divergence of $U_j\otimes U_j$. The largest possible frequencies come from sums of two frequencies of length at most $2\Lambda_j$. The Leray projection, divergence and time differentiation preserve the resulting band of radius $4\Lambda_j$.

e03-aux-bernstein-cost.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_sl: For a time jet of $U_j$ or $R_j$, the Fourier band remains $2\Lambda_j$ or $4\Lambda_j$, respectively. Each spatial derivative therefore costs at most a constant times $\Lambda_j=\lambda_j^5$. In particular the factor $\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ in the residual estimate survives at every fixed spatial order, multiplied only by a polynomial in $\lambda_j$.

e03-aux-induction-on-time.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.terminal: For $q=0$ both estimates are already consequences of Theorem M.7.1. For the induction step, use the time bounds (1.3) at order $q-1$ on the old parent, obtain the mixed correction estimate (1.2) at order $q$, and then establish (1.3) at order $q$ for the new stage. The numerical induction theorem assumes the analytic child-step implication; the subsequent estimates establish it for the selected construction.
e03-aux-induction-on-time.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.lemma_1_3_of_co: The implication for generalized Lemma 1.3 assumes a uniform analytic time-step estimate for arbitrary qualifying constructions. That hypothesis remains open, so this implication does not prove the generalized lemma unconditionally. The selected-construction proof establishes the bounds along its own sequence.
e03-aux-induction-on-time.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.lemma_1_2_of_co: The analogous implication for Lemma 1.2 assumes the order-growth result, generalized velocity-residual time bounds and a uniform correction step. The open generalized time-step hypotheses are not used in the selected-construction proof. That proof gives the mixed bound directly along the selected sequence.

e03-aux-base-mixed.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.stageMix: At time order zero the mixed correction is the second estimate of (7.4). For fixed $m$, the inequality holds when $q_j\ge m$, which eventually follows from order growth. The linked result supplies the numerical Hölder bound; continuity of the correction curve is separate.

e03-aux-base-time.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.stageTim: Condition (T2) is stronger than needed at order zero: $\|R_j\|_\infty\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-3}\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$, while $\|U_j\|_\infty\le\lambda_j$. Hence $\psi_0=1$ and the first stage suffice for the numerical bounds. The continuity statement follows from stage regularity.

e03-aux-parent-polynomial-slab.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.term: From $T\ge\mu^{-1/8}$ we have $T^{-i}\le\mu^{i/8}$. Thus extracting a fixed time derivative from the time-jet sum costs at most $i!\mu^{i/8}$. This bound may depend on the time order but not on the hierarchy depth or on the new frequency $\lambda$.

e03-aux-parent-projected-equation.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.slabTimeJ: From $\partial_tU=-\mathbb P\operatorname{div}(U\otimes U)+R_U$, differentiate $q-1$ times. The product contains only velocity jets of total time order $q-1$, and the last term is $\partial_t^{q-1}R_U$. The Fourier band and Bernstein turn the spatial derivative and Hölder cost of the projected divergence into an old-frequency polynomial. This is the first half of the one-order gain; the mean inverse supplies the second.

e03-aux-parent-mixed-bounds.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_te: For $i\le q$, obtain the new velocity time derivative from the projected equation and then apply Bernstein in space. For $R_U$ use the preceding time-order estimate only, through $q-1$. The linked theorem obtains the powers in (2.1); its common constants are chosen after the time order and input exponent, while the separate Bernstein theorem gives the sharper independence of the residual constant.
e03-aux-parent-mixed-bounds.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex: The induction hypothesis on the old slab restricts to $[0,S_j]$. The projected equation supplies order $q$ of $U$, but (2.1) retains order $q-1$ for $R_U$. Bernstein in the old band contributes $\Lambda_U^n=\mu^{5n}$ to each line. It does not replace the new-frequency factor $\lambda^{-5/2}$ in the second line by an old-frequency power.
e03-aux-parent-mixed-bounds.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_sl: For the residual, no differentiated nonlinear estimate is needed once its time bound and band limit are known. Bernstein gives $C_n\mu^{5n}\lambda^{-5/2}$ with $C_n$ independent of time order. The corresponding velocity time bound must first be obtained from the projected equation.

e03-aux-no-high-residual-jet.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex: The old residual appears in the mean equation at level two, not in the centered transverse source. This is essential: the induction knows the old residual only through time order $q-1$. The mean equation gains the missing time derivative by (2.3); subsequent sources use the resulting mean velocity $B_2$, not its forcing or its pressure.

e03-aux-residual-coefficient-jets.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex: Along the parent flow, each time derivative on $R_U\circ X$ is a material derivative on $R_U$ followed by composition with $X$. The iterated product rule keeps exactly one factor involving $R_U$, at time order at most $q-1$. Consequently the small factor $\lambda^{-5/2}$ survives. The other factors and the composition cost parent powers; the label weights absorb the per-derivative growth in $\mathsf D^{16m}$.

e03-r2-aux-parent-coefficient-bounds.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Sc: For the inverse deformation, $\partial_t(D_aX)^{-1}=-(D_aX)^{-1}M$; for the normalized wave vector, $\partial_t(\kappa/\lambda)=-M^T(\kappa/\lambda)$. Differentiation therefore introduces parent quantities but no positive power of the new frequency in these normalized coefficients. The formal bound uses $\kappa/\lambda$ and its reciprocal squared length, with label cost $\mathsf D^{16m}$ paid by $\ell_*^m$.

e03-aux-time-norm.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ: With the weights $T^i/i!$, the binomial coefficients in the time product rule cancel exactly: $T^i\binom{i}{r}/i!=(T^r/r!)(T^{i-r}/(i-r)!)$. Thus a product of two finite time jets through order $q$ is bounded by the product of their jet sums. No assumption of time analyticity is involved; $q$ is fixed and the sum is finite.

e03-aux-fixed-label-phase.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeD: The independent phase $s$ is held fixed along with $a$. On a parent trajectory $x=X(t,a)$ the physical evaluation has phase $k_*\cdot a$, independent of time. Thus profile time differentiation corresponds to the material derivative $D_t$, not the Eulerian derivative $\partial_t$. The transport term is restored in the later graph estimate.

e03-aux-amplitude-after-derivative.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te: The weight divides the derivative, not the field before differentiation: $(\partial_t^i f)/\gamma(t)$. This retains the instantaneous amplitude even for time derivatives of the switched wave. A derivative of the normalization would instead generate terms involving $\gamma_t/\gamma$ and would estimate a different quantity.

e03-aux-mean-without-amplitude.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te: The mean is selected by the endpoint condition on its displacement, and generally has a nonzero initial velocity. Its time norm therefore uses the full parent slab and no factor $1/\gamma(t)$. The factorial weights are unchanged, so it can still be multiplied by an oscillation measured in the weighted norm.

e03-aux-extract-time-derivative.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_: Keeping the $i$th term of the nonnegative jet sum gives $N(\partial_t^if)\le i!T^{-i}\mathcal J_l(f)$ for $i\le l$. For a fixed target order, the slab lower bound makes $T^{-i}$ a fixed power of the preceding frequency. No power depending on the spatial order or depth is introduced by this extraction.

e03-r2-aux-material-graph-identity.TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.slabTi:
Along a particle with fixed label $a$, the profile is evaluated as $f^
atural(t,X(t,a))=f(t,a,k_*\cdot a)$. Differentiating this equality in $t$ gives $D_t f^
atural=(\partial_tf)^
atural$. Since the phase stays fixed on this trajectory, no factor $\lambda$ enters this particular time derivative. Iteration gives the corresponding material jets.

e03-aux-factorial-convolution.TorusEuler.terminalTimeJetWeight_mul_cho: The coefficient of $(\partial_t^if)(\partial_t^{n-i}g)$ in the weighted $n$th derivative is $(T^n/n!)\binom ni=(T^i/i!)(T^{n-i}/(n-i)!)$. Hence the factorial-weighted derivative estimates multiply as ordinary finite convolution sums, without an additional binomial cost at each expansion level.
e03-aux-factorial-convolution.TorusEuler.terminalTimeConvolution_le: If $a_i$ and $b_j$ denote the norms with the weights $T^i/i!$ and $T^j/j!$ included, the time derivative product bound summed through order $q$ is at most $\sum_{i+j\le q}a_i b_j\le(\sum_{i\le q}a_i)(\sum_{j\le q}b_j)$. In particular the products at a higher expansion level do not demand additional time orders from the lower levels.

e03-r2-aux-mean-differentiated-equation.TorusEuler.terminalProjectedHigherTimeDe: For the selected displacement velocity $v=z_t$, put $\mathcal T(t)w=\mathbb P(K(t)w)$ on divergence-free label fields. The projected strong equation gives $\mathcal T v_t=\mathbb P(g-\mathcal Dv)$. Its $(q-1)$st derivative has only one term containing $\partial_t^qv$, namely $\mathcal T\partial_t^qv$. All terms from differentiating $K$ or $\mathcal D$ contain lower derivatives of $v$, and $g$ is differentiated at most $q-1$ times.

e03-r2-aux-mean-time-gain-display.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex: The integrated endpoint inverse first bounds the actual $v=z_t$; it determines its initial trace from the two conditions on $z$. The fixed-time inverse of $\mathbb P(K(t)\cdot)$ then bounds each higher time derivative from the differentiated strong equation, using (D.3) in Hölder norms. This gives (2.3), with one extra label derivative on the source but one fewer time derivative. Lean chooses the minimum radius exponent before the time order (its index $q$ on the right corresponds to $q+1$ on the left), so the construction need not be changed for higher time orders.

e03-aux-mean-gains-time-order.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.selec: The original endpoint inverse fixes the initial trace of $v=z_t$. Its higher time derivatives are then obtained from the differentiated strong equation, not by imposing new zero endpoint data. The formal estimate uses source jets through $q-1$ (through zero when the natural-number index $q$ is zero); it assumes the requisite Hölder bounds on those source jets.

e03-r2-aux-transverse-time-bound.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex: The oscillatory estimate must bound both the transverse velocity and its pressure. In particular (M.5.16) computes $\partial_s p$ from $\kappa\cdot f-2\kappa\cdot MV$ by division by $|\kappa|^2$. A $q$th time derivative of this identity involves the $q$th time derivative of $f$. Thus one cannot use the mean-velocity gain as a gain for the entire oscillatory solver. The mean pressure is not used in subsequent sources.

e03-r2-aux-mean-source-order.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te: The hierarchy uses the mean-source norm at time order $q-1$ and the mean-velocity norm at order $q$. The oscillatory sources and their velocity and pressure solutions all use order $q$. This particular allocation allows the mean source to contain $R_U\circ X$ at level two without asking for the unavailable $q$th derivative of the old residual.

e03-r2-aux-residual-time-source-bound.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.sc: At level two the mean source consists of the averaged quadratic stress of the leading wave and the transported parent residual. Both have scale $\lambda^{-5/2}$ up to old-parent powers. The average removes the fast phase derivative in the stress. By (2.2) the residual has the required time norm through $q-1$; this is precisely the order needed by (2.3) to bound the mean velocity through $q$.

e03-aux-recurrence-smallness.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.even: The level-two source target is $\lambda^{-5/4-2/3}=\lambda^{-23/12}$. Of the three direct source powers $-9/4,-5/2,-2$, the last is closest to the target and leaves $\lambda^{-1/12}$. The same spare power occurs after the level-two mean estimate. At later levels the common factor $\lambda^{-2(p-2)/3}$ is present on both sides. Since $\lambda=\mu^{K_j}$, any fixed parent cost $C\mu^A$ is eventually absorbed by $\lambda^{-1/12}$. Independence of $A$ from $p$ is essential.

e03-aux-hierarchy-time-lift.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex: The induction first estimates the mean source at order $q-1$ and obtains the mean velocity at order $q$; only then is that velocity used in the extra transverse source. Each new source contains a bounded number of solved-profile and coefficient factors. The margin absorbs their combined parent loss, restoring a source bound without a growing power of the parent at successive levels. The formal theorem uses $L=\mathsf D^e$ and the sufficient condition $L^6\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$.

e03-r2-aux-aggregate-expansion-rates.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Sc: After the finite induction there are four estimates to retain. The oscillation starts at level one and is measured relative to $\gamma$, the mean starts at level two and is unweighted, the remainder carries the depth factor $\lambda^{-2P/3}$, and the switching error is measured relative to $\gamma$ on its short support. The formal aggregate estimates require the finite reserve $m+3P\le H$ for the first three, and $m+1\le H$ for the switch. The reserve accounts for derivative orders spent at intermediate levels, not an additional frequency power.

e03-r2-aux-oscillatory-spatial-cost.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi: The graph differentiation of an oscillation has a term $\kappa\partial_s f$, whose scale cost is $|\kappa|h^{-1}\lesssim\mathsf D^C\lambda^{3/2}$ since $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$. Absorb the parent factor in $\lambda^{1/2}$ to obtain the cost $\lambda^2$ per physical derivative. For a mean the phase term is zero, leaving only parent powers even at high fixed orders.

c8-auxiliary-mean-polynomial-absorption.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Po: For the mean, $\bar W^\natural(t,x)=\bar W(t,X^{-1}(t,x))$ has no fast phase. Each additional physical or time derivative at fixed orders costs only a parent polynomial. The factor $\lambda^{-5/2}$ therefore survives the graph readout. The linked predicate records the resulting bound for a specified stage and order, before the eventual absorption is proved.
c8-auxiliary-mean-polynomial-absorption.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te: At the fixed pair $(m,q)$ the ratio of the mean bound $C\mu^A\lambda^{-5/2}$ to the required $\lambda^{-1}$ is $C\mu^{A-3K_j/2}$. For all sufficiently late stages it is at most $1/2$. Thus half of the increment allowance remains for the nonlocal cutoff tail. Here the exponent $A$ may depend on $(m,q)$, unlike the exponent in the hierarchy induction.

e03-aux-physical-time-estimates.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.po: To read the $q$th Eulerian time jet, expand the transport identity repeatedly. Each term has one profile jet with at most $q$ extra spatial derivatives and products of old-parent jets. If the $n$ further spatial derivatives split as $n_1+n_2=n$, the parent factors cost at most $\lambda^{n_1}$ and the profile at most $\lambda^{2(n_2+q+1)}$, apart from fixed parent powers. Hence the exponent in (2.5) can be written $2(n+1)+\psi'_q$ with $\psi'_q$ independent of $n$. The formal reserve is $(P+q+1)+3P\le H$.

e03-r2-aux-tail-depth-identity.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi: The remainder at depth $P$ has the factor $\lambda^{-2P/3}=\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$ because $P=6K_{j+1}$. The activation error has no such depth factor. It is supported only during the initial switch, when the seed amplitude is at most $Ce^{-L_j}=C\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$. This is the separate reason both terms of the residual have the same next-frequency decay after graph conversion.

e03-aux-cutoff-commutation.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ: At step $j$ the operator $S_{\Lambda_j}$ is fixed throughout the slab. Therefore $\partial_t^q(S_{\Lambda_j}-\operatorname{Id})V=(S_{\Lambda_j}-\operatorname{Id})\partial_t^qV$. This permits direct application of (B.2) to each time jet of the uncut approximation; no derivative of the symbol or scale appears.

e03-aux-cutoff-tail-estimate.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ: At order $P$ the differentiated approximate velocity grows at most as $\lambda^{2(P+1)+\psi'_q}$. The Fourier tail gains $\lambda^{5(m-P)}$, so its combined exponent is $-3P+5m+2+\psi'_q$. At fixed $(m,q)$ this tends to $-\infty$ as the scheduled depth increases. The additional cost $\mu$ for the cutoff constant is absorbed since $\mu\le\lambda$.

e03-aux-half-tail.TorusEuler.terminalTime_cutoff_tail_rate: Since $\mu\le\lambda$, the cutoff tail bound is at most $\lambda^{-3P+5m+3+\psi'_q}$. For fixed $(m,q)$ eventually $3P\ge5m+5+\psi'_q$, so this is at most $\lambda^{-2}\le\tfrac12\lambda^{-1}$ for $\lambda\ge2$. The formal arithmetic lemma uses precisely this sufficient depth inequality.

e03-aux-exact-correction-split.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se: Subtract the spatially localized, uncut $O_j=W_{\rm osc}^\natural$, not $S_{\Lambda_j}O_j$. Adding and subtracting $V$ leaves exactly $\bar W^\natural+(S_{\Lambda_j}-\operatorname{Id})V$. A finite Fourier sum cannot in general retain the support of the wave. The global tail estimate is what permits one to discard the uncut oscillation off the origin without discarding its cutoff error.

e03-aux-add-half-bounds.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ: Both terms in the exact correction identity are estimated in the same mixed norm: the mean by (2.4), without any fast phase cost, and the Fourier tail by (B.2) applied to the time jet. Their bounds are each $\tfrac12\lambda^{-1}$. Thus the estimate for the correction is global even though the oscillation it excludes is localized. Norm continuity on the closed slab is obtained separately.

e03-aux-new-velocity-power.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ: At $n=0$, (2.5) bounds the time jet of $V$ by $\lambda^{2+\psi'_q}$. The uniform cutoff bound costs at most another factor $\lambda$ eventually. This yields $\psi_q=\psi'_q+3$ for all $i\le q$, as required in (1.3).
