e03-r2-aux-cutoff-residual-identity.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ: Write $v=U_j-V$. Because time differentiation commutes with $S$, subtracting the cut and uncut projected equations leaves $SR_V$ and the projected divergence of $v\otimes U_j+V\otimes v+(\operatorname{Id}-S)(V\otimes V)$. Each of the three stress terms contains a cutoff tail. For the projected divergence in $C^{1,1/2}$ estimate the tensors in $C^{2,1/2}$; time differentiation distributes over the factors without removing the tail.

e03-aux-new-residual-power.TorusEuler.slabTimeJet_cutoffResidual_ra: The projected uncut residual contributes at most $\lambda^{1+\psi'_q}\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$ after bounding its operator constant by $\lambda$. The new cutoff terms contribute at most $\lambda^{15+2\psi'_q}\lambda_{j+1}^{-6}$, by $\Lambda=\lambda^5$ and $P=6K_{j+1}$. The formal rate lemma uses the sufficient condition $K_{j+1}\ge16+2\psi'_q$ to bound each term by $\lambda_{j+1}^{-3}$. Their sum is at most $\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ once $\lambda_{j+1}\ge4$.

e03-aux-oscillations-leave-compact.TorusEuler.inductive_oscillations_eventu: Let $d=\operatorname{dist}(K,0)>0$ on the torus. Once the support radius of $O_j$ is less than $d/2$, the oscillation is identically zero on the open $d/2$-neighborhood of $K$ throughout the slab. On the periodic lift the separation is from the entire integer lattice. Consequently every mixed derivative of the late oscillations vanishes there. The increment bound for the remaining terms is global; only the starting index and the early finite sum can depend on $d$.

e03-aux-all-jets-terminal-limit.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.terminal: Fix a closed spatial ball separated from the lattice. For any finite joint order $k$, take a starting stage valid for all mixed orders up to $k$. Expanding each joint derivative into time and space directions gives at most $2^k$ mixed terms. The increments are bounded by $2^k\lambda_j^{-1}$, and hence are summable. On the closed cylinder the uniform convergence of the fields and each successive derivative identifies the limits as derivatives of the same field, by integration along line segments, including one-sided derivatives at the time faces.

The spatial ball in the local argument depends only on separation from the lattice, not on the derivative order. All fixed orders converge on this same cylinder; their starting indices may differ. Restricting to the interiors of these balls gives joint smoothness up to the terminal face throughout the punctured slab. No bound uniform as the spatial point approaches the origin is asserted.

e03-r2-aux-limit-identification.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.smoothTerminalE: The off-origin limit has the same values as the global uniform velocity limit $w$ on the common slab. Proposition M.8.1 gives $w=u$ on every $[0,T]$ with $T<T_\infty$. Hence the limiting mixed derivatives are the actual one-sided terminal jets of $u$, not prescribed data for a separate solution.

e03-aux-extension-theorem-step.TorusEuler.exists_terminalSmoothExtensio: The paper applies Seeley in the normal coordinate $T_\infty-t$. Its reflection series matches every normal derivative at the boundary. Lean proves the extension by a different construction: localize the smooth boundary jets $a_n(x)=\partial_t^n u(T_\infty,x)$ in space, then form a Borel series with terms $a_n(x)(t-T_\infty)^n/n!$ multiplied by cutoffs on successively smaller time scales. For each fixed derivative order the tail is summably small, while the $n$th term has exactly the prescribed $n$th normal jet. Glue to the original field across the face using equality of all normal jets as smooth functions of $x$. Both arguments give a smooth extension agreeing on the original slab.
e03-aux-extension-theorem-step.TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.hasSmoothOffO: The paper glues local extensions by a spatial partition of unity. On the punctured lift Lean also extends across both time endpoints and periodizes the extension by a locally finite weighted sum of lattice translates. On the preterminal slab all translated fields agree by periodicity of $u$, so normalization of the weights preserves $u$ there. Neither the gluing nor periodization is an Euler evolution past the terminal time.

e03-r2-aux-generalized-auxiliary-conclus.TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness: The velocity has a smooth extension off the origin, while the central vorticity is unbounded as $t\uparrow T_\infty$. A classical solution on the whole torus extending beyond that time would have bounded vorticity on the compact time interval ending there, a contradiction. Thus $T_*=T_\infty$ even for the selected construction with the stronger off-origin conclusion.
e03-r2-aux-generalized-auxiliary-conclus.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.remark_1_2: Remark 1.2 is the existence statement needed in the main paper. The selected auxiliary theorem supplies the stage construction, the central singularity and the off-origin extension; periodic Euler uniqueness identifies the maximal solution from the resulting data. This does not require the stronger generalized assertion about arbitrary qualifying step sequences.
e03-r2-aux-generalized-auxiliary-conclus.TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Proof.theorem_1_1_o: The linked conditional proof takes the main stage and limit results together with the generalized mixed-increment assertion as hypotheses, then applies the extension argument. The generalized Lemma 1.2 remains an open antecedent. The selected theorem proves the mixed estimates along the chosen sequence and establishes the existence statement of Remark 1.2 independently of that stronger antecedent.
